body:
## NFS Most Wanted Vita 1.5.2

### New: split screen
Quick Race > Split Screen now works: two players, one view each (top and bottom), racing side by side from the start line.

**Controllers**
- **PS TV:** pair two controllers.
- **PS Vita:** player 1 uses the Vita's own controls, player 2 a DualShock through [ds34vita](https://github.com/MERLev/ds34vita).
  - With a single DualShock, also install [reVita](https://github.com/MERLev/reVita) (before ds34vita in `config.txt`), turn on *Profile > Controller > "Vita as virtual DS4"* (menu: START + SQUARE), then reconnect the DualShock.
  - Two DualShocks work with ds34vita alone.
  - DS4Vita/DS3Vita can't be used for player 2: they feed the controller into the Vita's own buttons.

### Fixes and changes
- **Tollbooth races:** should fix a crash or freeze after crossing a tollbooth, likely caused by a HUD message too long for its buffer in Spanish and Finnish. If it still happens to you, please tell me (#127, #133, #134).
- **Widescreen option:** *Off* brings back the 1.5.0 look (menus, HUD and world stretched to 16:9, bigger car). *On* (default) keeps the 1.5.1 look: 4:3 menus, the widescreen HUD and a wider view of the world (#130).
- **Race win screen:** the texts sit on the photo again, and the photo is no longer stretched (#124).
- **Semi trailers:** their cargo (logs, crates, containers) now breaks loose when you hit them, so they work as pursuit breakers again (#125).

### Thank you
The Credits screen now thanks everyone who helped build this port by opening issues and commenting on GitHub. Thank you all!

### Online multiplayer?
I'm thinking about adding online multiplayer, but only if enough people would play it. If you would, please react with 👍 to [this discussion](https://github.com/germanalvarez15/nfsmw-vita/discussions/113), answer its questions and share it with other Vita players. It would help me a lot.

### Updating from 1.5.1
Install the VPK over the old one. Your save and game data stay as they are.

name: Deltarune Vita v0.81
body:
Hey everyone! **Wolff here again!** After months of development, countless experiments, internal builds, performance testing, GPU crashes, shader tweaks, and more debug logs than I'd like to admit, **DELTARUNE for PS Vita v0.81** is finally here! This release brings together everything I've been working on since the public **v0.73** release, marking another major step forward for the project. While **v0.80** laid the technical groundwork with the introduction of **native GXM rendering, a redesigned texture pipeline, and significant memory management improvements**, **v0.81** shifts the focus toward refining the actual gameplay experience. The goal? **Smoother performance, more consistent frame pacing, native C optimizations tailored to real PS Vita hardware, animated borders, enhanced shaders, and fixes for some of the most troublesome bottlenecks across all five chapters.** There's still work to be done, but this update represents a huge step toward making DELTARUNE feel right at home on the PS Vita. > [!IMPORTANT] > The PS Vita VPK does **not** include the full official DELTARUNE game. You must provide your own legally obtained game data. > > Always back up your save files (`ux0:data/deltarune_saves/`) before updating. ### Deltarune for PS Vita (Unofficial Fan Port) - Announcement Trailer


--- ## Release Highlights The main changes since v0.73 include improvements, bug fixes, and general optimizations. ### VitaGL and VitaGXM: Two Graphics APIs Previously, I had been working on gradually replacing VitaGL with a native GXM (`libgxm`) implementation. However, after extensive experimentation with VitaGXM, I decided to give VitaGL another chance. Improvements made to Butterscotch (my local fork), together with what I learned from the native GXM implementation, allowed me to fix many of the original reasons for switching APIs, including GPU crashes, Vita freezes, and some RAM leaks. Occasional crashes may still happen, and I'm continuing to work on them. **VitaGXM has not been discontinued.** DELTARUNE for PS Vita still supports both graphics APIs, and you can choose which one to use: - **VitaGXM** - Renderer: One native rendering mode, with no additional variants. - **VitaGL** - **Legacy:** No shader support. More stable, but potentially less optimized due to higher CPU usage. - **Modern-GL:** Lower CPU usage and proper shader support, but may experience GPU crashes. - **Experimental-GL:** A hybrid of Legacy and Modern-GL, designed to preserve Legacy's stability while providing the shader support required by certain chapters and areas. The work on `libgxm` also helped resolve other issues, such as enemy dialogue text being cut off at the bottom of the screen. For now, I've paused further GXM development to focus on polishing and finalizing VitaGL, especially because shaders remain essential to parts of the game. ### Recommended Graphics Settings **These are my recommended settings for the current release.** | Setting | Recommended value | | --- | --- | | Texture Compression | Optimized | | FPS Limit | 30 FPS | | Screen Filter | None (although I recommend trying the new CRT filter :D) | | Shaders | On | | Graphics API | VitaGL | **P.S.** You can select **Aggressive** texture compression for some extra FPS at the cost of occasional slightly incorrect pixel colors (nothing too serious). --- ### Animated Borders! This update introduces **Animated Borders**, a PS Vita-exclusive mod that brings dynamic, animated backgrounds to the game's borders! Here are three examples of the new animated borders: | Castle Town | Sunset Town | Castle Café | |:---:|:---:|:---:| | | | | Animated borders have minimal processing and VRAM overhead (**less than 768 KiB**). In more demanding rooms, an animation or frame may be temporarily paused rather than competing with the game's rendering resources. --- ### Enhanced CRT Effect! Inspired by [this GameBanana mod](https://gamebanana.com/mods/733383), a new shader-based CRT filter now works across all chapters. The previous basic screen filters have been replaced with a new collection of enhanced visual effects, ranging from subtle improvements to authentic retro CRT aesthetics. ### Original (Reference)

No Filter

Original DELTARUNE visuals without additional processing.

### CRT Filters

Soft CRT           ㅤㅤㅤㅤㅤㅤㅤㅤMedium CRT           ㅤㅤㅤㅤㅤㅤㅤㅤAggressive CRT

Subtle scanlines and gentle CRT effects.    Enhanced contrast and stronger scanlines.    Full retro CRT look with stronger analog-style effects.

### Additional Display Filters

Sharp Bilinear        ㅤㅤㅤㅤㅤㅤㅤㅤDithering Blending        ㅤㅤㅤㅤㅤㅤㅤㅤVHS (Scanlines)

Smoother scaling while preserving pixel-art sharpness.    Softer color transitions and blended dithering patterns.    Classic analog video aesthetics with VHS-inspired scanlines.

> [!TIP] > For the most authentic retro experience, try **Medium CRT** or **Aggressive CRT**. --- ### New Features! - Added mouse simulation for **Mike's Room in Chapter 4**, using the right analog stick or the front touchscreen. It turned out pretty cool! - Added microphone support for Mike's Room. If your microphone doesn't work (or you simply don't want to use it) tapping the screen will simulate sound input. - Added a Chapter 4-specific **mouse sensitivity** setting in Game Settings. ### A Mysterious Prologue... For first-time players, the opening video now leads to a place that may seem... familiar.

The goal is to create a more immersive introduction while displaying notices about optional plugins ([NoTrpDrm](https://github.com/Rinnegatamante/NoTrpDrm) and [CapUnlocker](https://github.com/GrapheneCt/CapUnlocker)). This screen also displays the available language options based on the installed languages. --- ### And More... - Improved loading times with VitaGL. - Faster chapter loading. - General optimizations. --- ## 1. Improvements by Category ### Performance, VSync, and Frame Pacing - **30 FPS Frame Pacer Fix:** Fixed a critical *double-advance* bug that doubled frame deadlines and caused kernel waits of up to 55 ms. This restores smooth, consistent 30 FPS gameplay in town and throughout the game. - **Hardware VSync at 30 FPS:** The 30 FPS mode is now synchronized directly to the hardware display's VBlank signal (presenting one frame every two refreshes of the 60 Hz screen), reducing frame-time fluctuations and microstutter. - **Native C Implementations:** - `obj_plat_floortex_FLOOR` and `AlignBottom1TILE`: Prebaked ground and grass surfaces rendered directly in C, saving approximately 33 ms per frame of GML processing in climbing and castle areas. - `obj_plat_vertical_floor_grass_strip`: Native surface caching for vertical grass strips. - `obj_parallax_cliffs_moving_layers` and `obj_parallax_cliffs_sunlayer`: C-based drawing and sunlight caching, saving 15–20 ms in the cliffs. - `obj_blue_platform`: Drawing logic moved to C while preserving the original physics and collision behavior. - **Reduced Room-Transition Freezes:** VitaGL texture cleanup and garbage collection (`glFinish()` and `vglForceGarbageCollection()`) are now handled together in a single batch, reducing Garden room transitions from 2.4 seconds to just a few milliseconds. - **Camera-Based Culling:** - Temporarily hides sliding doors outside the camera view (`obj_plat_fusuma_mask`). - Applies frustum culling to background trees in the Garden (`obj_blocktree_bg`). *Similar optimizations may be implemented in other areas in future updates.* ### Graphics, Shaders, and Visuals - **Diagonal Petal Transition (`shd_petalcut`):** Implemented the proper diagonal wipe that reveals the pink Garden from a dark scene in Chapter 5, accompanied by a dense diagonal curtain of 96 petal particles (`pt_petal_whirl`). - **Batch Flush Before Blend Mode Changes:** The draw queue is now flushed before changing blend modes (`vitaQuadBatchFlush`), preventing visual artifacts and unwanted outlines in composited elements. ### Dynamic and Animated Borders - **Seamless Feathering:** The full static background border now blends into the animated side strips (`frames_side.bani`) using a smooth 24-pixel linear transparency gradient, removing harsh seams between static and moving artwork. - **Low-Memory Mode:** Visible side-border streaming uses less than **768 KiB of VRAM** in total, helping keep animations active even when Chapter 5 places heavy demands on memory. ### Audio and Video - **Music Recovery:** Music volume is preserved after loading save files and exiting battles. - **Stream and Pitch Management:** Generational audio IDs prevent channels from being reused incorrectly, and pitch adjustments (`snd_pitch`) are now handled properly. ### Controls and Debug Tools - **Mike's Controls (Chapter 4):** Added customizable mouse sensitivity (20%–200%) and pointer controls using the right analog stick or front touchscreen, while preserving Kris's normal movement with the D-pad.

- **DEBUG / DEVMODE Improvements:** Several developer tools have been redesigned and refined to make debugging, testing, and navigating the game easier: - **Game Settings:** Redesigned the interface, with improved layouts and accessibility for DEV-exclusive options. - **Room Navigator:** Improved the interface and navigation controls, allowing faster room switching and more efficient testing. - **Collision and Object Mapping:** Enhanced the debugging overlay to better visualize collision boundaries, identify in-game objects, and investigate missing textures. - **Screen Adjustment:** Refined the interface for easier display positioning and alignment.

Room Navigator ㅤ     Collision e Object Mapping ㅤ    Screen Adjustment

--- ## 2. Fixes by Chapter ### Chapter 2 - Improved protection against disappearing mice in Noelle's puzzle and the tower puzzle ([Butterscotch PR #556](https://github.com/ButterscotchRunner/Butterscotch/pull/556)). The previous workaround remains available if needed, helping prevent softlocks. - Fixed alpha testing and added fog support for compatible renderers. ### Chapter 3 - Prevented freezes during Tenna's cutscene through native execution of `scr_chromakey` and a five-second freeze watchdog. - Added native C rendering for the wavy background of the post-chapter menu (`DEVICE_MENU`), eliminating hundreds of repeated draw calls per frame. ### Chapter 4 - Fixed the climbing lockup in the church towers (`global.flag[23]`). - Fixed direct rendering of enemies in battle without creating unnecessary individual surfaces (`obj_darkshape`). - Implemented native C processing for foreground tiles in the Titan's tower (`room_dw_churchc_titanclimb1_tiled`). - Improved the School-to-Castle Town transition with optimized border cleanup. ### Chapter 5 - **Fixed Duplicate TP Bar:** Resolved a visual glitch in Chapter 5 where two TP bars could appear simultaneously during the Floradinn encounter (`room_dw_garden_floradinnencounter`). Improved battle-state detection and surface cleanup to prevent leftover Garden UI elements from overlapping the battle interface.

Before          After

- **Complete Petal Transition:** Restored the proper diagonal scene wipe (`shd_petalcut`) with a curtain of 96 pink petal particles. - **Reduced Stuttering:** Faster transitions between Garden areas (`room_dw_garden_*`) without synchronous GPU stalls. - **Native C Processing in the Cliffs and Castle:** Ground and grass (`floortex`), moving cliff layers (`moving_layers`), sunlight (`sunlayer`), and blue platforms now run through compiled native code. - **Textures Kept in VRAM:** Protected Krákrá's attacks (tongues and multiple projectiles), Kris, and floor textures against premature video-memory deallocation, preventing invisible elements. - **PS4 Button Glyphs:** Krákrá battle prompts now display the correct PlayStation-style button icons. - **Border Fixes:** Corrected the nighttime border in `room_town_mid` and removed the unwanted border in the flower shop. - **Restored the tower visuals during the final battle**, fixing the broken or incomplete background rendering and bringing the scene back to its intended appearance.

Before          After

--- ### Other Fixes and Improvements - Fixed a missing pixel row at the bottom of enemy dialogue boxes during battles.

- Added smooth fade-to-black transitions for school doors and menus. - **Font Rendering:** Improved subpixel alignment and rendering of accented characters in Portuguese and other languages, resulting in sharper text. - **Background Music:** Improved soundtrack recovery after loading save files. - **Stable 30 FPS and Hardware VSync:** Fixed the critical frame-pacer delay that could drop gameplay to 15 FPS. Frame presentation now targets a consistent **33.333 ms** cadence synchronized with the PS Vita's 60 Hz screen. - **Native C Fast Paths (Chapters 4 and 5):** Replaced expensive GML interpreter operations with native C routines for drawing floors, grass, platforms, cliff layers, and tower elements, saving up to 35 ms per frame. --- ## Build Information and Installation - **VPK File:** `Deltarune-v0.81-11.vpk` - **Title ID:** `DELT00001` - **VPK SHA-256:** ```text 7ff182a70b266abb5ea745171c5faaba440a25cad05847d693cb800956ca1a1e ``` ### How to Update 1. Install `Deltarune-v0.81-11.vpk` using your preferred file manager (VitaShell, FMVita, or File Manager). 2. If you use the Animated Borders mod, make sure the `.bani` packages are up to date in `ux0:data/deltarune/deltarunevita/mods/bordersanim/`. 3. Launch the game as usual. Your saves and settings will be preserved. > [!NOTE] > **v0.81 does not require updated game data files.** However, the patcher has been updated to include the animated border assets and the updated Brazilian Portuguese translation of Chapter 5 by [Teiarruma](https://github.com/teiarruma/deltarune-ptbr). If you'd like to get just the animated border files, you can download them separately here: [Download Animated Borders](https://drive.google.com/file/d/11W7fCJN8WxkmlahuEhHD65BnQsp0NhIn/view?usp=sharing) --- ## Installation Guide For full setup steps, please refer to the [Installation Guide](https://github.com/WolffsRoom/DeltaruneVita#installation-guide).

“Hey, traveler. Why don't you come by my store?”

Access the Seam's Patcher.

--- ## Bug reports and diagnostics If you encounter a problem, please open a ticket on the Issues page: https://github.com/WolffsRoom/DeltaruneVita/issues Please include: ```text ux0:data/deltarune/deltarunevita/butterscotch-probe.log ``` and, when relevant: - Chapter and Room. - Selected language. - Renderer. - Texture-compression mode. - FPS limit. - Screenshot/video of visual problems. - Generated `psp2dmp` crash dump when available. _If Dev Mode is enabled, also include the corresponding diagnostic information from the affected Room._

Acknowledgments and Credits

DELTARUNE VITA is an unofficial port developed by Wolff, using the Butterscotch engine, VitaGL, VitaSDK, and other native PS Vita graphics libraries.

Special thanks to all Butterscotch developers, the PS Vita homebrew community, the translation teams, and everyone who submitted detailed bug reports, logs, and gameplay videos during testing.

And, of course, a huge thank-you to Toby Fox and the DELTARUNE team for creating this incredible game.

homebrew_description: Monster Hunter Tri for the PS Vita.
homebrew_long_description:
A static recompilation of Monster Hunter Tri (Wii) to native ARM code. The game's PowerPC code is translated to C++ and linked with a native runtime that replaces the Wii's hardware and system software: there is no emulator, interpreter or JIT. Rendering goes through native GXM on the PS Vita and OpenGL ES 3.0 on Linux; a WebAssembly build draws through WebGPU.

The repository contains no game code or data. You need your own copy of the European disc (RMHP08, "Monster Hunter Tri (Europe) (En,Fr,De,Es,It)") as an ISO or RVZ image. WIA images are recognized too, but untested and possibly unstable. Other regions are not supported.

How the port reaches full speed on a 444 MHz Cortex-A9, written so that the techniques carry over to other Wii games: docs/optimizations.

name: PsVita Alive Store 02.18
body:
# PSVitaAlive 02.18

**02.18** updates the native PS Vita / PSTV client with a V1/V2 catalog reader and usability and memory-management improvements. This client is released **before** the public JSON catalog format switches to V2.

## Highlights

- **Catalog compatibility:** reads V1 and compact V2 Homebrew, author, category, PS Vita, PSP and PS1 metadata, and preserves support for previously cached V1 catalogs.
- **Game Files status:** shows a localized alert if a port is installed but all known required Game Files folders are missing.
- **Screenshot memory:** retains screenshots as long as their actual rendered rectangles intersect the viewport; continues freeing off-screen GPU textures through the safe deferred-release mechanism.
- **Readable details:** wraps long requirements, descriptions and metadata to the actual text width.
- **Installed-data management:** clearer APP-only, Game Files-only and combined removal options, appropriate warning text, and consistent confirmation dialogs.
- **Visual fixes:** improvements to marquee clipping, modal overlap and eight-language interface labels.
- **Web and tools:** supports both schema formats without changing published catalog content ahead of the client.

## Safe catalog rollout

This is the **compatibility update**. Public catalogs remain V1 at the time 02.18 is published. Only after this release and its VPK are confirmed available will a separate change introduce compact V2 JSON. Updating to 02.18 first is important: old clients with disabled, failed or cancelled updates may not be able to read V2.

## Install or update

1. Download **PSVitaAlive.vpk** from the release assets below.
2. Install over the existing PSVitaAlive using VitaShell, or use its built-in release updater.
3. Reopen PSVitaAlive after installing the update.

**Title ID:** `PSVAS1178`  
**Version:** `02.18`

The official VitaSDK release workflow checks the VPK's internal `APP_VER`, Title ID, ZIP integrity, and attached SHA-256 checksum.

Website: https://vegettosan.github.io/PSVitaAlive/  
Source: https://github.com/VegettoSan/PSVitaAlive

name: v1.1
body:
Local co-op, a startup intro, smoother heavy waves, custom characters, and a pair of glasses you should not trust.

### What's new
- **Local co-op**: two Vitas on the same Wi-Fi, from Co-op in the main menu. One hosts and picks the stage, the other joins with any character they have bought. A fallen player comes back at the other's next level-up.
- **Intro** at startup, animation from the Ode to Castlevania announcement trailer set to original music. Any button skips it.
- **Performance, thanks to Marcin ([DrakonPL](https://github.com/DrakonPL))**: heavy waves run around 56 fps where v1.0 dropped to 39. His pull request measured where the frame time was going and brought every idea behind the speed-up: no more waiting on the GPU every frame, music and sound effects off the main thread, incremental sorting and off-screen culling for the draw list, enemy templates for spawning, and a grid for projectile hits. They are rewritten for this port, but the speed-up is his.
- **Wolff ([WolffsRoom](https://github.com/WolffsRoom))'s interface ideas**: photosensitivity warning, pixel button glyphs, animated main menu, centered prompts, zoom and touch movement in the Options, achievements fixed at the edges.
- **Custom characters** in the format of the Unity custom character beta, in `ux0:data/VampireSurvivors/CustomCharacters/`.
- **Jukebox**: every stage hides a vinyl record; the first unlocks the Jukebox in the main menu.
- **The Funny Glasses**: somewhere in the Mad Forest. See below.

### Experimental: 3D view
The glasses give 30 seconds of 3D and then unlock a View option for good. **It is a beta and an easter egg, made for fun rather than to be played seriously**: the game was never designed for 3D, so props can float, walls can look odd, ground effects stay flat and the frame rate drops. Rough edges are expected and part of the joke.

### Fixed
- Pause: the weapon evolutions panel fits the screen; the Grimoire box grows with its text.

### Updating from v1.0
Install the VPK. Your save carries over. For co-op, both Vitas need v1.1.

### Downloads
- `VampireSurvivors-Vita-v1.1.vpk`: the game
- `VampireSurvivorsSetup-Windows.exe`, `-macOS.zip`, `-Linux.zip`: the setup tool, unchanged from v1.0
- `libraylib.a`: only for building from source

### Known issues
- Very heavy waves can still dip below 60 fps.
- The 3D view: see above.

Thanks to Wolff ([WolffsRoom](https://github.com/WolffsRoom)) for the interface ideas and the animated menu, and to Marcin ([DrakonPL](https://github.com/DrakonPL)), whose performance work is the reason this release runs as smoothly as it does.

body:
# Ultimate Spider-Man for PS Vita v1.1

A big speed and stability update. Install it over 1.0: your saves and game files stay where they are.

**You need your own copy of the PC game.** No game data is included. New here? See the install steps in the README.

## Faster
- Typical play now runs at about 25 fps with the default 30 fps cap, and often 28-30 in quieter spots.
- Cutscenes are much smoother.
- Game logic, drawing and the renderer now each get their own CPU core.
- Much of the busiest code was rewritten for the Vita's processor, and music and speech no longer pause the game while they load.
- The default resolution is now 960x544, because lowering it gained almost nothing.
- World textures are sharper.

## Fixed
- Quit now exits straight away instead of freezing (#6).
- The garbled map and the shards in cutscenes are gone (#2).
- Fixed a crash during busy gang fights (#5).
- Revert to Default no longer removes the web, zip and camera controls (#3).
- Spanish, French, German and Italian can now be picked in Settings. You need that language's PC game files (#1).
- The Options menu opens much faster.

## New in Settings
- Language
- Smoke and fire detail
- Map detail
- World texture detail
- Fog in cutscenes

If you changed settings in 1.0, press Triangle in Settings to get the new defaults.

## Known issues
- Stutter is still the biggest problem. Short hitches happen while the city streams in, and the worst ones come just after a mission ends.
- The heaviest scenes, such as big explosions, can drop to 10-15 fps.
- The map can run slowly when fully zoomed out.

## Reporting a bug
Turn on **DEBUG: write log.txt** in Settings and play until it happens. Then attach `ux0:data/usm/log.txt` to an issue, plus `ux0:data/usm/crash.txt` if the game stopped with an error.

name: The Impossible Game — PS Vita Port v1.3.1
body:
# The Impossible Game — PS Vita Port v1.3.1

Hotfix for v1.3.0: some saves unlocked trophies the player never earned on the first launch.

## 🐛 Fixed in v1.3.1

- **Phantom trophies on first launch**: saves written by older builds could hold garbage values (e.g. `38`, `20`, `15`) in medal slots. The retroactive unlock treated any non-zero value as earned, so it unlocked e.g. *SIN BANDERAS 3*, *PRACTICA 4* and *SIN BANDERAS 4* right after boot. The game only ever stores `1` in a medal slot, so any other value is now reset to `0` when the save loads (and logged as `Save medal[i]=N corrupt`).
- Trophies that v1.3.0 already unlocked by mistake stay unlocked. The Vita can't re-lock a trophy; you can only delete the game's trophy data.

---

# v1.3.0

Adds **native PS Vita trophies**: every in-game medal now also unlocks a system trophy, with a Platinum for collecting them all.

---

## 🏆 New in v1.3.0: Trophies

- **13 trophies** (1 Platinum, 5 Gold, 1 Silver, 6 Bronze), one per native medal:

| Trophy | Type | How to get it |
|---|---|---|
| LO IMPOSIBLE | Platinum | Unlock every other trophy |
| PERSEVERANCIA | Silver | 500 attempts without quitting |
| SALTARIN | Bronze | 999 jumps in total |
| PRACTICA 1-5 | Bronze | Finish Level 1 / Xbox Level / Level 2 / Level 3 / Level 4 in Practice Mode |
| SIN BANDERAS 1-5 | Gold | Finish that level with no flags |

- **Retroactive unlocks**: medals already in your save unlock their trophies on the next launch.
- Trophy icons are the game's own medal art.
- ⚠️ The **base game** only has 6 medals (Level 1 + Xbox Level), so the Platinum needs the **Level Pack**.
- Requires [**NoTrpDrm**](https://github.com/Rinnegatamante/NoTrpDrm/releases) under `*main` in `ur0:tai/config.txt` (**reboot** after adding it). Install the **full VPK** — trophies live in `sce_sys/` and are not installed by copying only `eboot.bin`.

---

## 🚨 Critical Fixes (from v1.2.1)

### 1. Fix for White Worlds / Missing Textures
- **Stack Alignment Fix in `ImpossibleGame_initGame`**: In previous builds, passing `fps` as a `jfloat` under modern hardfp toolchains caused the compiler to place it in VFP register `s0`, skipping a stack slot. `libimpossible.so` (compiled under softfp AAPCS) expected `fps` at `[sp, 4]`, which shifted the texture ID arguments: the main texture atlas (`gametextures.png`) received the second texture ID and the second received garbage, leaving game textures unbound and rendering obstacles and background as blank white quads. Passing `fps` as a 32-bit bitcasted word preserves exact stack layout.
- **Fixed-Function GLES1 Float Bridge**: Calls to `glColor4f`, `glClearColor`, `glTexEnvf`, `glPointSize`, `glTranslatef`, and `glRotatef` from `libimpossible.so` now pass through softfp-to-hardfp integer bridge wrappers, ensuring color and transform values are correctly delivered to VitaGL.

### 2. Fix for Total Audio Silence
- **ABI Mismatch in Math Functions**: `stb_vorbis` was passing float arguments in integer registers (`r0-r3`), while VitaSDK GCC 15 `libm.a` (`sin`, `cos`, `pow`, `floor`) expected them in VFP registers (`s0-s15`). This resulted in math functions reading uninitialized registers and returning NaNs/0, causing audio decoding to output total silence.
- Rebuilding the project natively with `-mfloat-abi=hard` and linking against hardfp runtime libraries completely restores BGM and SFX audio playback.

### 3. ABI Bridge Wrappers (`source/dynlib.c`)
- Implemented dedicated softfp-to-hardfp bridge wrappers for all 10 external float functions imported by `libimpossible.so`:
  - Math: `sinf`, `cosf`, `truncf`, `round`
  - GLES1: `glClearColor`, `glColor4f`, `glTexEnvf`, `glPointSize`, `glTranslatef`, `glRotatef`
- Removed `-Wl,--no-warn-mismatch` entirely from CMake; all project components now compile and link cleanly with `-mfloat-abi=hard`.

---

## ✨ Features & Universal Compatibility (from v1.2.0)

- **Universal APK Auto-Detection**:
  - Dynamically resolves JNI exports with automatic fallback between the Level Pack prefix (`Java_com_flukedude_impossiblegamelevelpack_*`) and the Base Game prefix (`Java_com_flukedude_impossiblegame_*`).
  - Drop in either `05133-the-impossible-1.5.2.apk` (2 levels) or `05133-Impossible-Level-Pack.apk` (5 levels) — no code changes or separate builds needed.
- **Adaptive Menus & UI**:
  - **Base Game Mode (2 levels)**: Automatically displays the original 2-button level selector (Fire Aura & Original Xbox Level) and restricts Stats & Medals to 3 subpages, eliminating missing texture errors.
  - **Level Pack Mode (5 levels)**: Automatically enables the full 5-level grid and 6 subpages for Medals and Stats.
- **Bounded Save Synchronization**:
  - Syncs up to 6 medals / 2 levels when running the base game, and 12 medals / 5 levels with the Level Pack.
- **Toolchain Modernization**:
  - Full compatibility with modern VitaSDK (GCC 15.2.0 / C23 standards).
  - Resolved `ATOMIC_VAR_INIT` deprecation in `logger.c`.
  - Corrected return types in FalsoJNI (`GetPrimitiveArrayCritical`, `jda_sizeof`).
- **Persistent Diagnostics Logging**:
  - File logger (`ux0:data/theimpossiblegame/logs/log_XXX.log`) enabled unconditionally for runtime diagnostics.

---

## 📋 Requirements

- PS Vita / PS TV running Custom Firmware (**HENkaku** or **Enso**), firmware 3.60/3.65+.
- [**kubridge**](https://github.com/TheOfficialFloW/kubridge/releases) installed as a kernel plugin (`ur0:tai/config.txt`).
- [**NoTrpDrm**](https://github.com/Rinnegatamante/NoTrpDrm/releases) under `*main` in `ur0:tai/config.txt` (only needed for trophies).
- [**libshacccg.suprx**](https://github.com/Rinnegatamante/ShaRKBR33D/releases/latest) installed in `ur0:data/`.
- A legally obtained copy of:
  - **The Impossible Game** for Android (`05133-the-impossible-1.5.2.apk`), **OR**
  - **The Impossible Game: Level Pack** (`05133-Impossible-Level-Pack.apk`).

---

## 📦 Installation Instructions

1. Install `theimpossiblegame.vpk` on your PS Vita using VitaShell.
2. Open your legally obtained `.apk` using any zip tool (7-Zip, WinRAR, etc.):
   - Copy `lib/armeabi-v7a/libimpossible.so` to `ux0:data/theimpossiblegame/libimpossible.so`.
   - Copy the `assets/` folder to `ux0:data/theimpossiblegame/assets/`.
   - Copy the `res/` folder to `ux0:data/theimpossiblegame/res/`.
3. *(Optional)* If you own the **Level Pack** (`05133-Impossible-Level-Pack.apk`), simply copy and overwrite `libimpossible.so` and merge the `assets/` and `res/` folders into `ux0:data/theimpossiblegame/`. The game will automatically detect all 5 levels.

name: Inotia 3: Children of Carnia v1.0.3 — PS Vita Port
body:
# Inotia 3: Children of Carnia v1.0.3 — PS Vita Port

Bug-fix and quality-of-life update for the native Android-to-PS Vita wrapper port of **Inotia 3: Children of Carnia** (originally by Com2uS). Powered by so-loader, FalsoJNI, and vitaGL.

This release builds on **v1.0.2**. It fixes input issues reported while playing on physical PS Vita hardware and adds a game speed option.

## 🛠️ Fixes & Improvements

1. **Dialogues advance again**: Cutscene dialogues could stop responding to both touch and buttons, forcing a restart. A button press could leave a virtual finger "stuck" on the screen; every press is now always released.
2. **Dragging works again**: Quest descriptions scroll again, and items can be moved in the bag again, so equipping weapons and armour works.
3. **Buttons no longer press hidden menu items**: While a pop-up, NPC window or dialogue choice is open, the D-pad and Cross no longer trigger the menu behind it.
4. **Left stick works as a D-pad** everywhere, including in menus.
5. **Game speed option (Start + Select)**: Cycles between 15 FPS (original), 23, 25 and 30 FPS. A short notice at the top of the screen shows the new value without pausing the game. The game's logic runs per frame, so a higher FPS also makes the game run faster. The choice is saved.
6. **Skill quick-slots stay visible**: With the touch controls hidden, quick-slots that have a skill assigned (including its cooldown) are now shown, not only item slots.
7. **L + R shows or hides the touch controls**, with an on-screen notice. Start + Select no longer does this; it now changes the game speed.

## 📋 Prerequisites & Requirements

Before installing, ensure your PS Vita has:

- Custom Firmware (3.60 / 3.65 Enso recommended).
- Plugins installed in `ur0:tai/config.txt` under `*KERNEL`:
  - `kubridge.skprx` (v0.3 or newer)
  - `fd_fix.skprx` (or rePatch)
- `libshacccg.suprx` installed in `ur0:data/` (can be extracted using ShaRKBR33D).

## 📦 Installation Guide

**Updating from v1.0.0 / v1.0.1 / v1.0.2:** just install the new `inotia3.vpk`. Your game files and saves in `ux0:data/inotia3/` are kept.

**Fresh install:**

1. Install `inotia3.vpk` on your PS Vita using VitaShell.
2. Legally obtain a copy of the Inotia 3: Children of Carnia Android APK (v1.3.2).
3. Open the `.apk` using any zip extractor (like 7-Zip).
4. Copy `lib/armeabi/libgame.so` to:
   `ux0:data/inotia3/libgame.so`
5. Extract the `assets/` folder from the `.apk` and copy its contents to:
   `ux0:data/inotia3/assets/`
   *(Or copy extracted game resources into `ux0:data/inotia3/assets/common/game_res/`)*
6. Launch the game from LiveArea!

## 🎮 Controls

| Button | Action |
| :--- | :--- |
| D-Pad / Left Analog | Move Character / Navigate menus |
| Cross (✕) | Attack / Confirm / Action |
| Circle (◯) | Back / Close menu / Cancel pop-up |
| Square (▢) | Skill / Quick Slot |
| Triangle (Δ) | Special Skill / Quick Slot |
| L / R Triggers | Quick Slots / Target Toggle |
| Start | Pause Menu |
| Select | Map / Character Info |
| L + R | Show / hide on-screen touch controls |
| **Start + Select** | **Game speed: 15 / 23 / 25 / 30 FPS** *(new)* |
| L + R + Select | Button remap menu |
| Touchscreen | Full Touch UI Navigation |

## 📜 Credits

- Original Game by **Com2uS**.
- **TheOfficialFloW** for so_loader.
- **Rinnegatamante** for vitaGL & FalsoJNI.
- **Bythos** for kubridge.

name: Crash Bandicoot: The Wrath of Cortex for PS Vita v0.1.0-beta
body:
# v0.1.0-beta

First public beta of the PS Vita port.

## Files

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `crashwoc.vpk` | The game for the Vita (install with VitaShell) |
| `crashwoc-extract.exe` | Windows: copies the game files from **your own** USA disc image |
| `crashwoc-extract-linux`, `crashwoc-extract-macos` | Same for Linux / macOS (Apple Silicon) |
| `SHA256SUMS.txt` | Checksums |

No game files are included: you need your own GameCube disc (USA, `GCBE7D`).

Installation: see the [README](../README.md).

## Highlights

- Whole game playable with saves, music, sound and LiveArea bubble.
- Screen modes 4:3 / stretched / widescreen (Select + up) and frame lock (Select + down).
- Windows extractor with a small window: pick the disc image and the Vita (VitaShell USB mode, detected automatically) or a folder, then click Extract.
- Rendering on a second CPU core and vertices streamed directly to the GPU.

## Known issues

- *Crash Blast* (GBA link-cable minigame) is not available on the Vita.
- Some crushing platforms in *Earth Crisis* may not show up.
- Busy scenes can drop below 30 fps; level loads take ~8–13 s.

Please report problems and attach `ux0:data/crashwoc/crashwoc.log`.

name: Zenonia 4 PS Vita Port v1.2.0
body:
# Zenonia 4 PS Vita Port v1.2.0 — Multi-Core Sprite Rendering

**Release Tag:** `1.2.0`

---

## 🚀 What's New in v1.2.0

- **🧵 Uses all 3 CPU cores for sprite drawing.** Large sprites are split into horizontal bands and drawn on cores 0, 2 and 1 at the same time, producing exactly the same pixels as the original renderer. The game now shows **15–20 FPS in combat (was 10–12)** with AUTO frame skip, and ~17 FPS with frame skip OFF. Game speed stays at the original 23. Audio keeps priority on its core.
- **⚙️ Frame skip in the options menu.** START + SELECT now has Frame skip, Frame rate and On-screen buttons, each with its shortcut shown. The frame skip choice is saved too.

## ⚠️ Known Limitations

- The heaviest scenes can still dip to ~12 FPS.
- All three CPU cores show high usage while playing, which is expected: the helper threads wait for sprites without sleeping, to react instantly. They sleep when the game isn't drawing.
- START + SELECT doesn't exit the game; use the PS button.

## ⚙️ Defaults

| Setting | Default | Change with |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Frame skip | **AUTO** | R + SELECT, or START + SELECT menu |
| FPS | **23** (original speed) | L + SELECT, or START + SELECT menu |
| On-screen buttons | **Shown** | R + L, or START + SELECT menu |
| Button layout | Cross = Attack/OK, Circle = Back, Triangle = Skip, Square = Map, L = Save | START + SELECT |

On-screen messages only appear when you change a setting. Settings are saved in `ux0:data/zenonia-4/config.txt` and `controls.txt`.

## 📦 Installation

1. Install `zenonia_4_pace_nologs.vpk` with **VitaShell** (it updates v1.1.0 in place; your saves and settings are kept).
2. First install only: copy `libgameDSO.so` (from the APK's `lib/armeabi/`) and the APK's `assets/` folder into `ux0:data/zenonia-4/`.
3. Launch **Zenonia 4** from LiveArea.

## 📁 Downloads

- **`zenonia_4_pace_nologs.vpk`** *(recommended)*: no logging, no SD card writes.
- **`zenonia_4_pace.vpk`**: same build with logging to `ux0:data/zenonia-4/logs/log_NNNN.log` (for bug reports).

---

## Previous release: v1.1.0 — Original Game Speed, Options Menu & Remapping

**Release Tag:** `1.1.0`

---

### What was new in v1.1.0

- **⏱️ Correct game speed.** Zenonia 4 was designed to run at **21 FPS in menus and 23 FPS in gameplay** (the Android game asks for it itself). Earlier builds ignored that, so menus ran too fast, combat ran in slow motion and the fixed frame-skip patterns made characters stutter while walking. The game now always runs at its original speed.
- **🎞️ AUTO frame skip (default).** It skips drawing a frame only when the game falls behind, so movement speed stays constant even in heavy fights. OFF draws every frame, but the game slows down in heavy scenes.
- **⚡ Optional 30 FPS mode** (Zenonia 2/3 style): the whole game runs about 1.3x faster.
- **🎮 PS Vita options menu (START + SELECT)**, ported from the Zenonia 3 port: remap every action, change FPS, show or hide the on-screen buttons. The game pauses while it's open.
- **👆 Hide the on-screen buttons (R + L).** They still respond to touch, and the game runs noticeably faster with them hidden.
- **🕹️ Left stick moves**, and input no longer lags or gets stuck (all queued button events are now handled every frame).
- **🖼️ Faster framebuffer upload.** Down from ~17 ms to ~1.6 ms per frame (3-texture ring instead of vitaGL's copy-on-write).

Performance, controls and quality-of-life update. Installation is unchanged from v01.30 (the UI assets `drawable/` and `html/` still come from your own APK). This VPK contains no copyrighted game assets.

* **Combat lag fixed:** the 30 fps cap no longer drops to 20 fps whenever a frame takes slightly longer (the vsync wait now runs on vitaGL's display thread). Input events are no longer limited to one per frame, so movement and attacks respond immediately and no longer get lost.

* **Left stick** now moves the character.
* **Main menu navigation:** the d-pad / stick moves a highlight over the six buttons, Cross presses it.
* **Faster Continue loading:** logging no longer forces a memory-card write per line.
* **Logs:** `ux0:data/zenonia3/logs/log_001.log` … `log_999.log`, timestamped lines.

### Changed
* **Start + Select no longer quits** — it opens the options menu. Use the PS button to exit.

name: Zenonia 2: The Lost Memories - PS Vita Port v1.3.0: Smooth Combat, Sharper Image & Control Remapping
body:
### Description

This release answers community feedback about lag in combat, slow movement, and a blurry image. The game now holds a steady 30 FPS in combat, the picture is noticeably sharper, and every control can be remapped from an in-game menu.

What's New:

• Steady 30 FPS in Combat: The engine advances one logic tick per frame, so any frame drop made the whole game run slower. The graphics library is now built specifically for this port with faster texture uploads, the game and audio run on separate CPU cores, and memory routines use the Vita's native implementations. Confirmed at a sustained 30 FPS on hardware.
• Sharper Image: The 400x240 game frame is upscaled 2x with nearest-neighbor before the final smooth stretch to the screen, so text and sprites look much less blurry.
• Better Input: All button presses in a frame are now delivered (previously multi-button input could lag behind), and the left analog stick moves your character.
• Control Remapping: Press Start+Select to open the controls menu (the game pauses). Assign any action to one or more buttons, including the rear touch panel (four quadrants), toggle touch controls, choose the frame rate, or restore defaults. Settings are saved to `ux0:data/zenonia-2/controls.txt`.
• Toggle Touch Controls: Press L+R to show or hide the on-screen D-pad and buttons.
• Frame Rate Mode: Press Select+R to switch between 30 FPS (default) and ORIGINAL, which follows the game's own speed setting (10–22 FPS) like the Android version.
• Logs are now saved as numbered files in `ux0:data/zenonia-2/logs/` (001.log, 002.log, ...).

Notes:
• Start+Select no longer exits the game. Use the PS button instead.
• Game data in `ux0:data/zenonia-2/` is unchanged from v1.2.0. Just install the new VPK.

Known Issues:
• The experimental post-process shader build may show a black screen after the menu. Use the standard VPK.

name: FINAL FANTASY VII for PS Vita — v1.2.0
body:
This update adds selectable encounter calculation multipliers to the port menu,
with separate field and world-map handling, saved settings and runtime diagnostics.

## What's new

- **Gameplay > ENCOUNTER RATE** replaces the ON/OFF option with **0 (OFF)**,
  **1 (NORMAL)**, **2X** and **4X**. Changes apply without restarting the game.
- Field encounters scale their probability parameter during the original check,
  then restore it. World-map encounters scale the original effective rate after
  the game's Enemy Lure/Away calculation. Movement speed is unchanged.
- The selected setting is saved in `ux0:data/ffvii-vita/cheats.txt`. Existing
  `encounters 0` and `encounters 1` configurations remain compatible; the default
  is NORMAL.
- The optional Android touch button still shows ON/OFF. Turning encounters back
  on resumes the last active multiplier during the current session. Restarting
  with OFF saved resets the next activation to NORMAL.
- **ENCOUNTERS BUTTON: SHOW/HIDE** remains independent of the encounter rate.
- Runtime logs now include the selected factor, field/world hook call counts
  and the original/effective rates, making device reports easier to verify.
- If multiplier hooks are unavailable for an unsupported library layout, the
  menu falls back to OFF/NORMAL.

## How 2X and 4X behave

**These labels multiply the game's encounter calculation parameters, not the
number of battles per minute or per distance traveled.** The original game
accumulates danger and uses random checks, so battle frequency is not linear.

A deterministic ARM simulation of 10,000 world-map checks on the same terrain,
modeling a battle return by resetting danger, produced:

| Setting | Encounters | Relative to NORMAL |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1 (NORMAL) | 1,005 | 1.00× |
| 2X | 1,459 | 1.45× |
| 4X | 2,096 | 2.09× |

These are simulation results for one setup, not guarantees for other areas or
hardware measurements. A first device log confirmed hook installation, but did
not record enough information to verify the active rate during walking.
Confirmation of the frequency changes on Vita remains pending.

## Update / installation

Install **`ff7_vita_v1.2.0.vpk`** with VitaShell over the previous version.
Keep existing game data and settings; back up `ux0:data/ffvii-vita/save/` before
updating. No replacement APK or OBB is needed.

New installations require a homebrew-enabled PS Vita, `kubridge.skprx`,
`libshacccg.suprx`, and the user's own Android FINAL FANTASY VII **v1.0.29**
data, copied intact to:

```text
ux0:data/ffvii-vita/base.apk
ux0:data/ffvii-vita/main.30.com.square_enix.android_googleplay.FFVII.obb
```

See [the installation guide](https://github.com/ggdrn/METEOR-VII-VITA/blob/main/docs/DATA.md).

## Controls

Hold **L + R** and press **Start** to open the port menu. Select **Gameplay**
with **L/R**, select **ENCOUNTER RATE** with **Up/Down**, then use **Left/Right**
or **Cross** to cycle settings. Press **Circle** to close.

## Validation and known limitations

- Host tests cover rate selection, settings compatibility and persistence,
  touch OFF/ON behavior, independent button visibility, field rate restoration
  and world-map multiplication.
- ARM tests verify the original field probability comparison, Enemy Lure/Away
  rates and the world-map danger accumulation/random comparison.
- Release build and package checks passed; the VPK contains no game data.
- Multipliers retain the original encounter rules. On-device frequency and
  transition validation remain pending.
- Snowboard music remains silent. Some scenes may expose background or geometry
  limitations in widescreen; switch back to 4:3 if needed.

See [the validation record](RELEASE-v1.2.0-VALIDATION.md). For bug reports, include
the location, selected encounter rate, steps to reproduce, and
`ux0:data/ffvii-vita/logs.txt` plus `logs_anterior.txt`. To test rate handling,
walk in the same area with NORMAL and 4X before collecting the logs.

## Credits

Port by **Gustavo Garcia (ggdrn)**, with AI-assisted development.
Thanks to the contributors behind soloader-boilerplate, so-util, FalsoJNI,
vitaGL, VitaSDK, kubridge and the Vita homebrew community.

The VPK contains the port only. Game data must be supplied by the user.
FINAL FANTASY VII © SQUARE ENIX. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed
by Square Enix.

name: Carnivores: Ice Age for PS Vita — v1.2
body:
# Carnivores: Ice Age for PS Vita — v1.2

PS Vita port of *Carnivores: Ice Age* (Android 1.5.4). This version adds native PS Vita trophies and fixes the
menu cursor jumping the wrong way.

**The game files are not included.** You need your own Android APK (1.5.4, `armeabi`) and, for zones 2–5, its
Google Play expansion file. Installation, controls and options are in the [README](README.md).

## Download

- `carnivoresiceage.vpk` — install with VitaShell (over v1.1 is fine, save data is kept).

Requires `kubridge.skprx` and `libshacccg.suprx` (ShaRKBR33D). Trophies need `NoTrpDrm.suprx` under `*main`.

## What's new in v1.2

- **Native PS Vita trophies**: the game's 18 achievements (First Blood, Sharpshooter, Marathoner, Collector…)
  plus Platinum, with the system notification. Progress from v1.1 save data counts. Without NoTrpDrm the game
  runs as before with trophies off. On the first launch the screen stays black for a few seconds while the
  trophies install.
- **Fixed: menu cursor moving the wrong way.** Pressing Left / Right in a vertical list could jump to the
  button above or below. The cursor now only moves to buttons that are really in the pressed direction;
  Up / Down still reach corner buttons such as Back.

## What works

- Boot, menus, hunting in all five zones (with the OBB), weapons, calls, map, binoculars, save data.
- Physical controls for everything, menus included, plus the original touch controls.
- Audio (FMOD) through the Vita's audio output.

## Highlights

- **Right-stick camera** that feeds the game's own camera input: fast and independent of the frame rate
  (`look_sensitivity` in `config.txt`, 10–400 %).
- **FPU instead of software floating point** for both the game and FMOD (the APK is old `armeabi` code).
  Initial load: ~31 s → ~17 s.
- **No freeze on missing weapons**: without the OBB the shotgun has no model; such a weapon keeps its stats
  and uses another weapon's model instead of locking up the game.
- In-game touch buttons drawn at 1 % opacity (`hud_opacity`, 0–100) since every one has a physical button;
  the compass stays fully visible. Circle is the animal call.
- Settings in `ux0:data/carnivoresiceage/config.txt`: language, content packs, camera speed / inversion,
  anti-aliasing (`msaa`), FPS / timing log (`show_fps`).

## Known issues

- 3D scenes run well below 60 FPS (menus run at 60). Try `msaa 0`.
- Without the OBB only the first zone is available and the shotgun uses another weapon's model.
- Online features (Facebook, Google Play Games, ads, purchases) are disabled.
- No in-game exit dialog: quit with the PS button.

## Reporting bugs

Open an issue with `ux0:data/carnivoresiceage/logs/carnivoresiceage_NNN.log` (the newest one) and, for a crash,
the `.psp2dmp` file from `ux0:data/`. `engine_log 1` in `config.txt` adds the game's own messages.

## Credits

soloader-boilerplate and FalsoJNI (Volodymyr Atamanenko, after TheFloW and Rinnegatamante), vitaGL and vitaShaRK
(Rinnegatamante), kubridge (TheFloW). *Carnivores: Ice Age* © Tatem Games; this project is not affiliated with
Tatem Games.

name: Carnivores: Dinosaur Hunter — PS Vita · v1.2.0 "Trophies"
body:
**Native PS Vita trophies, and the game boots again with NoTrpDrm installed.**

## What's new since v1.1.0

### Trophies
- **26 native PS Vita trophies**: the game's 25 awards (First Blood, T-Rex Hunter, William Tell,
  Guru...) plus a Platinum. They install on first launch and unlock with the system notification.
  Requires `NoTrpDrm.suprx` under `*main` in `ur0:tai/config.txt` (reboot after editing).
- **Fixed: with NoTrpDrm installed the game didn't boot.** v1.0.0 and v1.1.0 shipped without a
  trophy pack; with the plugin, the trophy setup step had nothing to install and never finished.
  The pack now ships in the VPK, and trophy setup is skipped (the game boots without trophies) if
  the pack is missing or setup takes longer than 30 seconds.
- Without NoTrpDrm the game runs as before, with trophies off.

### Menus
- The button-navigation highlight is now four translucent white corner marks instead of a filled
  yellow box that covered the item.

## Requirements

- PS Vita / PS TV with HENkaku/Enso (3.60–3.74 with a kernel plugin loader).
- `kubridge.skprx` in `*KERNEL` of your taiHEN config.
- `libshacccg.suprx` in `ur0:data/` (use ShaRKBR33D).
- Optional, for trophies: `NoTrpDrm.suprx` under `*main` in your taiHEN config.
- Your own copy of the game APK (Android **1.3.1**, `com.tatem.dinhunter`, `armeabi`).

Not compatible: **Carnivores: Dinosaur Hunter HD** (`com.tatem.dinhunterhd`, 1.6.5) and its OBB
(`main.423.com.tatem.dinhunterhd.obb`). That is a newer OpenGL ES 2 engine with a different
asset layout and formats; this port can't use any of it.

## Install / upgrade

1. Install `carnivoresdinosaurhunter.vpk` with VitaShell (over an earlier version is fine: saves and
   packs are kept). Install the full VPK, not just `eboot.bin`: the trophy pack lives in
   `sce_sys/`.
2. Create `ux0:data/carnivoresdinosaurhunter/` and copy into it:
   - the APK, named `CarnivoresDinosaurHunter.apk`
   - `libdinHunter.so` and `libfmodex.so` from the APK's `lib/armeabi/`
   - optional, the two content packs (separate apps on Android):
     `CarnivoresBundleOne.apk` renamed to `bundle1.apk` and `CarnivoresBundleTwo.apk` renamed to
     `bundle2.apk`
3. Launch. The first load takes about 30 seconds on a static screen; that is normal.

A `controls.txt` from v1.0.0 is replaced by the new defaults on first boot.

## Controls

| Vita | Action |
|---|---|
| Touch screen | Original touch controls |
| Left stick | Move |
| Right stick | Look (frame-rate independent) |
| R | Fire (draws a holstered weapon first) / take photo |
| Cross | Jump |
| Square | Draw / holster weapon |
| Triangle | Next weapon |
| L | Binoculars |
| Circle / D-pad up | Call dinosaurs |
| Select / D-pad down | Map |
| D-pad left / right | Weapon list / photo zoom in |
| Start | Pause / back |
| Start + Select | PS Vita controls & camera menu (Select alone in menus) |

## Options

Most are in the in-game menu (Start + Select). By hand, in
`ux0:data/carnivoresdinosaurhunter/config.txt`: `look_sensitivity` (10–400), `invert_look_y`,
`invert_look_x`, `swap_sticks`, `msaa` (0 off / 1 2x / 2 4x), `hud_opacity` (0–100, default 1),
`engine_log`, `vfp_float`. See the README for details.

## What works (confirmed on hardware)

- Boot, full asset loading straight from the APK, menus at 60 FPS.
- Map loading and hunting in the 3D maps; a tester reports 30–60 FPS while hunting.
- FMOD music and sound effects.
- Content packs (**Pack 1**: areas 3–4 + sniper rifle; **Pack 2**: area 6 + double-barrel shotgun
  + crossbow), unlocked only when their APK is present.
- Saved games load on the next boot.
- Touch screen with the original controls, left/right stick movement and camera.

## Earlier fixes (v1.0.0)

Five bugs stood between the APK and a playable game, each found on real hardware:

- **The game couldn't read its own APK.** With SceLibc I/O, `fopen`/`fread` went to SceLibc while
  `fseeko`/`ftello`/`clearerr` still went to newlib with a SceLibc `FILE*`, so libzip computed a
  garbage archive size and every asset came back "not found". Those three now go through the
  SceLibc bridge too.
- **Permanent black screen at 60 FPS.** The prebuilt `libvitaGL.a` in VitaSDK is not built with
  `SOFTFP_ABI=1`, but the loader is softfp, so GXM's viewport received its floats in the wrong
  registers and every draw, even plain clears, landed off screen. vitaGL is now vendored and built
  with the softfp ABI.
- **GPU crash as soon as a hunt started.** vitaGL's `DRAW_SPEEDHACK` hands vertex arrays above a
  size threshold straight from game memory to the GPU. Menu sprites are small and got copied, but
  the terrain is not, and the GPU faulted reading memory it has no mapping for. The speedhack is off.
- **Black screen on the second launch.** The engine opens its save file and never closes it, so once
  a save exists the APK gets a different `FILE*`. The libzip inside the game was built for Android
  and checks `ferror()` by reading a bionic `FILE` field directly; on a SceLibc `FILE` that field
  is meaningless. With the first `FILE` it happened to read as "no error", with any other one the
  archive failed to open and nothing loaded. The five inlined checks are patched out. This is also
  what lets the content-pack APKs open next to the main one.
- **Crash in FMOD when a sound file is missing.** `Sounds_AddSound()` doesn't check whether the
  file was found, and passed leftover stack data to FMOD as the sound buffer. A missing file now
  gives FMOD an empty buffer, which it rejects cleanly.

Performance work:

- The engine is `armeabi` (ARMv5TE), so all of its float/double math goes through libgcc's software
  emulation. 32 of those helpers are redirected to the Vita's VFP; every hook was checked against
  the real `.so` with objdump.
- The engine's own logging is dropped before formatting (it wrote several lines per asset while
  loading and forced memory card flushes).
- MSAA off by default, Release build, vitaGL with error checking off and FFP shader cache on.

## Known issues

- **Black screen while trophies install (first launch with NoTrpDrm).** The screen stays black for
  a while with no progress indicator before the game starts. Don't close the game or turn the
  console off during this step. A loading screen for it is planned.
- **Frame rate:** 20–30 FPS has been reported while hunting, dropping when dinosaurs are on screen.
  Not fixed yet; it needs profiling on hardware first.
- Trophy unlocks and the Platinum have not yet been checked one by one on hardware; please report
  any award that shows in game but doesn't pop the trophy.
- The first load is a ~30 s static screen with no progress indicator.
- Many `FMOD error 'An invalid parameter...'` messages while loading dinosaur sounds. They don't
  crash, but some sounds may be missing.
- The FMOD missing-sound fix has not been through a very long session yet.
- Exiting is done from the PS button (the Android "Exit?" dialog from the main menu is skipped).

name: BombSquad Vita Alpha 0.95
body:
BombSquad 1.8.7 on PS Vita: a much faster start-up with a picture instead of a black screen, and the app now updates itself.

## Install

1. Install BombSquad-Vita-Alpha-0.95.vpk with VitaShell (it installs over Alpha 0.9 or 0.8)
2. Launch with Wi-Fi on. On a first install, press X to download BombSquad from its official server

Needs kubridge.skprx, libshacccg.suprx, the correct date and time, and about 400 MB free. See the README for details and known issues.

`app-update.txt` and `eboot.bin` are what the app downloads when it updates itself. You don't need to install them by hand.

### Much faster start-up

- The menu appears in about 30 seconds instead of about 54, measured on a Vita memory card. The first launch after an install takes a few seconds longer while it saves its start-up caches
- The bubble's picture stays on screen with moving dots until the menu is ready, instead of a black screen
- Python no longer reads every game module twice, generated code is kept between launches, and the game's check of its cached assets takes about 1.5 seconds instead of 6
- A launch that fails to start clears these caches, so they can't cause a second failure

### App updates

- The app now updates itself: once a day on launch it checks its GitLab releases, and if you accept it downloads the new program, checks its size and SHA-256, swaps it in and restarts
- A new version that doesn't finish starting is replaced by the previous one automatically and isn't offered again
- This is the last VPK you need to install by hand, unless a later release changes the bubble's art

### Faster installs and updates

- The install takes about 2 minutes instead of 6: game data goes into one archive instead of also being written as about 2300 loose files
- Interrupted downloads continue from the partial archive
- Updates and rollbacks keep the game's downloaded assets (about 140 MB), so they aren't downloaded again and the game reaches the menu in under a minute after an install instead of over six
- New BombSquad releases are checked for once a day instead of on every launch, which saves about a second

```text
BombSquad-Vita-Alpha-0.95.vpk
SHA-256 37CC2F23EBE351284E5802085BE7C700B7C92BC214ED1833D766793D53D28D95
```

name: TwinsanityEvolved v0.9.3
body:
# TwinsanityEvolved 0.9.3 -- what's new

Crash Twinsanity as a native game for Windows, macOS, Linux and the PS Vita: the twinsanity-reversed decompilation running
on the NativeEE engine. **No game data is included: you play with your own disc image.**

## New in 0.9.3

- **Crash's shadow on crates.** His shadow now falls on the tops of crates as well as the ground, so jumps onto them
  are easier to judge (the PS2 drew none there; `video.shadows_on_crates = off` in `ps2r.ini` goes back to that).
- **32:9 screens.** A new 32:9 aspect ratio, and with the game's own Widescreen option on, the wide shapes show more
  of the world at the sides while the HUD, the pause page and the fps counter stay in the middle 16:9.
- **Gameplay fixes:** at 60 Hz a knee slide no longer swings far past the stick's direction at the end of its steering
  (`game.slide_steering = retail` keeps the original swing); in Bandicoot Pursuit, Evil Crash no longer gets stuck where
  his route data misses a step; a level select warp from inside a level no longer brings a second character along.
- **New option:** `game.invincible_to_explosions = on` in `ps2r.ini` lets the third Aku Aku mask protect Crash from nitro
  and TNT explosions too, as in the classic games (off by default: the original game lets explosions through).
- **Smoother pictures:** textures are prepared before they are first needed on every system (no hitch when a new one
  appears), and particles and skies cost less to draw at the high resolutions.
- **PS Vita:** a new LiveArea background and logo.

Save states made with 0.9.2 do not load in 0.9.3 (a save state belongs to the build that made it); memory card saves
are not affected.

## New in 0.9.2

- **Skip more in-game cutscenes with X.** Most of the game's scripted cutscenes can now be skipped too (45 of the 51
  checked), not only those with a skip of their own: a skip plays the cutscene's remaining frames through at once, so
  the characters, the camera and the level end up exactly where watching it would leave them. The few that cannot be
  skipped that way yet still play to their end.
- **Faster loading screens.** A level's parts are put in place as soon as they are read, so the loading picture is up
  for well under a second on a computer.
- **PS Vita: walls no longer vanish** in tunnels and corridors (the Boiler Room and others): a model wholly in view is
  always drawn.
- **PS Vita: smoother Rooftop Rampage** and faster heavy scenes; the parts of the level ahead are read from the
  memory card in advance, and the game no longer waits for the card while you play.
- **PS Vita: one package.** `twinsanityevolved-<version>-vita.vpk` now runs the game's code natively on the console; the
  separate `-vita-native.vpk` of earlier releases is gone. Installing it over an earlier package keeps
  `ux0:data/twinsanity/`.
- **New mod: infinite lives** (Options > Mods): a death costs no life, so a checkpoint restart never ends in a game
  over. Saves made with it on go to the mods memory card.

Save states made with 0.9.1 do not load in 0.9.2 (a save state belongs to the build that made it); memory card saves
are not affected.

## New in 0.9.1

- **Skip in-game cutscenes with X.** A cutscene played from its cutscene file can now be skipped the first time you see
  it, not only on a second viewing (a skipped cutscene counts as seen). Scripted scenes that have a skip of their own
  in the game's level scripts (switched off in the original release) now end when you press X; scripted scenes without
  one still play to their end.
- **Drowning in 10th Dimension:** a dark Crash-shaped shadow no longer shows under the water while he sinks (the real
  game shows none there).
- **High and uncapped frame rates:** objects are no longer briefly paired with their neighbours between pictures, no
  gap opens at the bottom of the screen while running and the shadows no longer draw thin lines.
- **Frames between pictures are off by default.** The smoothing frames the game adds between its own pictures at high
  frame rates are now off unless you turn them on (`video.interp = on` in `ps2r.ini`); they also resume correctly
  after loading a save state.

Save states made with 0.9.0 do not load in 0.9.1 (a save state belongs to the build that made it); memory card saves
are not affected.

## Install

1. Download the zip for your system from this release (the table at the end names each file), or the launcher (see
   Play below), which does every step for you.
2. Unzip it anywhere, on any drive (Windows: right-click the zip > *Properties* > tick **Unblock** first, so SmartScreen
   does not warn about the unsigned program).
3. Run `twinsanityevolved` (`twinsanityevolved.exe` on Windows; on macOS, the first time, right-click it > **Open**). The
   first time it asks for your disc image: your own Crash Twinsanity `.iso`, the European (PAL) or the North American disc.

Nothing is installed and nothing else is downloaded. Requirements: a graphics driver with OpenGL 4.1 (any current NVIDIA,
AMD, Intel or Apple GPU); keyboard and mouse or a gamepad (Space = cross, Left Shift = square, right mouse = circle,
E = triangle, W A S D = left stick, mouse = camera, Y = start, Tab = select).

## Play

- **The launcher installs the finished game.** It no longer makes the game from its source on your computer: it
  downloads the game for your system from the newest release, checks it against the release's checksums and puts it in your game folder. Its
  first run is one sheet of four questions -- where your game is, where it should live, where you will play (this
  computer, a PS Vita or another computer), then the download with its size and speed -- with Back on every step and
  nothing to type.
- **It finds your disc for you.** It looks in Downloads, Desktop, Documents, its own folder and any removable drive, and
  recognises the disc by what is on it (see Discs). Drop the file on the window if it is somewhere else. A disc you remove
  from the list stays off it on later searches.
- **One game folder holds everything.** `~/Games/Crash Twinsanity` (`%USERPROFILE%\Games\Crash Twinsanity` on Windows)
  unless you choose another: the game, your settings (`ps2r.ini`), your memory cards (`memcards`) and your mods (`mods`).
  Move the folder and everything moves with it: the game reads the `ps2r.ini` beside it first (on macOS, beside the app).
- **Pages: Games, Mods, Settings, About.** Games shows your discs, each with **Play** and, when a new version is out,
  **Update**; an update never overwrites your settings, saves or mods. Settings is the game's own Options in plain words --
  the same `ps2r.ini` the in-game menu writes, so a change in one is a change in the other. About can remove what the
  launcher keeps and says what it could not remove.
- **Launchers for every desktop.** A portable zip for Windows, a `.dmg` for macOS and, new, an AppImage for Linux.
- Quitting the launcher during a download is safe: nothing half-downloaded is left in your game folder.
- Every release zip also holds the mod tool and the Arabic language pack (see Mods and Languages).

- **Save states:** F5 saves the running game to `savestates/slot0.ps2st` in the game folder and F8 loads it back where it
  was; the game says so on screen. On the PS Vita the folder is `ux0:data/twinsanity/savestates/`.

## Discs

- **The European (PAL) disc** (SLES-52568) plays as before.
- **The North American disc plays** (SLUS-20909 v2.00, the "Action Pack" release): choose it and play. It runs at 60
  frames a second (its console's rate), in English with its own voices and movies, and keeps its own memory card
  (`memcards-SLUS-20909` beside `memcards`), so the two discs never overwrite each other's saves. Its program's own code
  changes are played the European way.
- **Every disc is identified by its content**, compared with the known dumps of the original discs (redump.org): the
  launcher shows `PAL · original disc`, `NTSC-U · original disc`, `PAL · modified disc` (the original program with other
  files, such as a translation patch -- it plays like the original) or `PAL · unrecognised version` (accepted with a
  warning). It reads the whole image once, a few seconds, and remembers the answer. The game checks the size at every
  start; `--verify-disc` checks the whole image.
- The Japanese disc and the first North American release (v1.00) are recognised but **not playable in this version**:
  each needs an address map, which `twinsanityevolved-modtool region-map` makes from the two discs for someone who has
  both.

## Mods

- **Mods packaged as Mod Crates are supported** -- the community's usual shape (a `.zip` or a folder with
  `ModCrateInfo.txt`, `layer0/` and `layer1/`), including large ones of over a gigabyte (about half a minute to add). The
  author's notes are shown under the mod.
- **Also taken as they are shipped:** a patched disc image (only the files that differ from your disc are kept), an
  xdelta, PPF or BPS patch made against the original disc, a folder of files laid out like the disc (or a loose
  `CRASH.BD` + `CRASH.BH`), and one file of the game's archive passed around on its own (such as a `Default.rm2`), placed
  by its name.
- **The launcher's Mods page:** drop a mod on the page (or **Add a mod…**) and it is added to your mods folder; each mod
  has a switch, a line saying what it changes and its region; drag the mods into order (the lower one wins where two
  change the same file); **Remove** deletes one after asking. Adding a mod you already have (a new version) asks first,
  then replaces it and keeps its switch and its place. A change takes effect the next time the game starts.
- **The mod tool** (`twinsanityevolved-modtool`, in every zip) does the same on the command line: `import`, `inspect`
  (what a file is, without adding it) and `verify` (every file of a mod checked byte for byte).
- **A mod is checked against your disc.** A mod records the disc it was made over; the game leaves out a mod made for
  another disc and says so in its log, and the Mods page says "Left out on this disc: made for the North American disc."
  where that applies. A loose archive file made for the other release is refused when you add it.
- While any mod is on, the game saves to its own memory card (`memcards-mods`): your normal saves are never touched.
- In the game, OPTIONS > MODS now lists the built-in mods (level select, speedrun mode); the mods of your mods folder are
  switched on the launcher's Mods page.
- **What cannot apply:** code changes in a mod's modified game program (its data changes -- tables, texts, numbers -- do
  apply; the code changes are listed under the mod); Crate Mod Loader's game-code settings (a crate carrying
  `ModCrateSettings.txt` is refused with the reason; settings a crate's notes ask for are named in a warning); xdelta
  patches made with secondary compression; RAR / 7-Zip archives, CHD / CSO / ECM images, `.cue` sheets, UPS / IPS patches;
  emulator texture packs and cheat codes.

- **Where a mod is switched:** a mod that changes the disc's files is switched on and off in the launcher only and is in
  place when the game starts; the game's own OPTIONS > MODS page keeps the two built-in mods (level select, speedrun mode),
  which work while you play. A mod made for the other region's disc is left out, and the launcher's row says so.
- **On the PS Vita** the switch is the `mods.<id>.enabled` line in `ux0:data/twinsanity/ps2r.ini` (the launcher writes it
  into the PS Vita folder; VitaShell's text editor changes it on the console); the mod's files stay on the card either way,
  and modded saves live on their own memory card (`memcards-mods/`).

## Languages

- **The text and the speech are two settings:** GAME OPTIONS > TEXT LANGUAGE and SPEECH LANGUAGE (and the launcher's
  Settings). Any text with any speech: Portuguese text with Spanish voices, Arabic text with French voices. The text
  languages are recognised by what the disc's text banks contain, so on a translated disc "english" is still English. The
  movies' sound and the title cards follow the speech. An older `game.language` setting keeps working.
- **Arabic:** every menu, notice and hint (305 texts, our own translation), drawn right to left in Arabic letters made in
  the game's lettering style. It comes with every zip and the launcher places it in your mods folder; there is nothing to
  switch on: TEXT LANGUAGE offers **arabic** after the disc's languages. It translates the European disc's English texts
  and is offered on a disc that carries them (not on the North American disc); the speech is any language your disc
  speaks.

- **A language pack is not a mod:** the Arabic text is one entry of the TEXT LANGUAGE row, like French or German; it has no
  switch anywhere and never moves your saves to the modded memory card.

## PS Vita

- **A PS Vita package in every release** (`twinsanityevolved-<version>-vita.vpk`): install it with VitaShell, copy your
  disc image to `ux0:data/twinsanity/game.iso`, and make sure the system's shader library `ur0:data/libshacccg.suprx` is
  present (the usual homebrew step). The package carries the game's GPU programs ready-made, so the first start does not
  stop to prepare them.
- **The launcher makes a ready-to-copy PS Vita folder** in your game folder (`vita/`: the package, the steps, and
  `ux0/data/twinsanity/` with your settings, the language pack and the mods you switched on). Two disc images can sit side
  by side on the console; `ux0:data/twinsanity/disc-image.txt` names the one the game starts. The North American disc
  plays on the PS Vita too (at 60). Mods are added on a computer and copied over.
- **The PAL console's 50 Hz game loop by default:** the game ticks 50 times a second as the PAL game did. GAME RATE in
  Options > graphic options switches between `60` and `50 hz (pal)` from the next start.
- **FRAME RATE auto:** the game runs at the full rate while it keeps up and otherwise holds a steady 25 (at 50 Hz) or 30
  (at 60 Hz) frames a second, so the picture moves evenly instead of swinging; `60` / `30` (`50` / `25`) fix the rate.
- **Fixed on the PS Vita:** the movies play (the boot logos and the story movies did not play at all); the intro movie
  of a new game is no longer corrupted; shadows are drawn; the title sequence's iceberg and logo draw cleanly; Cavern
  Catastrophe's puzzle crystals are visible; at 50 Hz the game no longer runs in slow motion with the sound running ahead
  of it; the GAME RATE setting takes effect.
- **Faster:** the drawing, the GPU work per picture, the geometry and the game code itself were all made quicker,
  measured scene by scene.
- **Still limited:** the heaviest levels and fights fall back to a steady 25 (at 50 Hz) or 30 (at 60 Hz; 20 in the very
  heaviest scenes) frames a second; importing mods is done on a computer.

## The launcher keeps itself up to date

- The launcher checks the releases when it starts (and from About): a newer launcher is offered on the Games page with one
  button; it downloads it, checks it against the release's SHA256SUMS, swaps itself and reopens. Your games, settings, saves
  and mods are not touched. The game's own **Update** button is unchanged. On the PS Vita the Installed list's **Update**
  fetches the new package into the PS Vita folder for you to install with VitaShell.
- The Mods page explains the PS Vita: switch mods here, press **Make the PS Vita folder**, copy `ux0/data/twinsanity` to the
  card. The folder's README names the disc file to copy and how two discs (European and North American) live side by side.

## PS Vita: faster in the heavy levels

- The refractive ice's frame copies (Ice Climb) are taken only when needed and only for the region drawn since the last
  one, with the same pictures: on the emulator the copy passes' pixels per picture fell from 6.1 M to 0.27 M.
- **The PS Vita package runs the game's code natively** on the console's ARM processor instead of through a translation
  layer: `twinsanityevolved-<version>-vita.vpk` is still the one package, and its hot functions have about half the
  instructions. It is the same title: installing it over an earlier package keeps `ux0:data/twinsanity/`, and your memory
  cards load in it (a card written by either package loads in the other).

## Fixes

- Depth: surfaces drawn on top of other surfaces -- the light patterns on cave walls, the ripple rings around floating ice,
  decals -- no longer flicker or vanish in pieces as the camera moves. The game's depth values are kept exactly (the PS2's
  24-bit depth) instead of being rounded, so the depth test gives the PS2's answer everywhere (every system).
- PS Vita: entering a new area or loading a level no longer stalls the picture for whole frames: a chunk's textures are
  decoded and its meshes prepared in the background as the chunk arrives, instead of in the first frame that shows it.
- At 50 Hz (`game rate: 50 hz (pal)`), on every system, the game no longer plays in slow motion: the game and its sound
  run at real speed at 50 and at 60.
- A settings file holding the game folder's own keys (`paths.memcards`, `paths.mods`, `mods.order`) is read instead of
  being refused whole.
- A disc this version cannot play is refused at the start with a sentence saying why, instead of failing on a missing
  file.
- An update by the launcher keeps an older game folder's language setting (`game.language`).

## The files of v0.9.3

No file of this release contains game data: every one passes the repository's asset scan.

name: Prince of Persia Classic — PS Vita Port v01.55
body:
# v01.55 — Native Trophies & Coin Store

**PS Vita trophies now install and unlock, and potions/revives are bought with coins earned in-game.**

---

## 🇪🇸 Novedades

### Trofeos nativos de PS Vita
- 18 trofeos (17 + Platino). La primera vez que abres el juego se instalan, y al conseguir un logro salta la notificación del sistema.
- **Requisito:** `NoTrpDrm.suprx` en `ur0:tai/` y bajo `*main` en `ur0:tai/config.txt`. Reinicia la consola después de editarlo.

### Tienda sin dinero real
- Las pociones de vida y las resurrecciones se compran con monedas, y las monedas se ganan jugando: cada punto de puntuación = 1 moneda. Se acreditan al abrir el menú principal o el menú de pausa.
- Solo cuenta tu mejor puntuación por nivel: superar un nivel por primera vez o mejorar tu récord da monedas nuevas.
- Las pantallas de compra con dinero real (Google Play) ya no aparecen; te llevan a la tienda de vidas con monedas.

### Instalación
1. Instala `popclassic.vpk` con VitaShell (se conservan las partidas guardadas).

---

## 🇬🇧 Release Notes

### Native PS Vita trophies
- 18 trophies (17 + Platinum). They install the first time you launch the game, and the system notification pops when you earn one.
- **Requirement:** `NoTrpDrm.suprx` in `ur0:tai/` and under `*main` in `ur0:tai/config.txt`. Reboot the console after editing it.

### Store without real money
- Life potions and revives are bought with coins, and coins are earned by playing: each score point = 1 coin. They are credited when the main menu or the pause menu opens.
- Only your best score per level counts: clearing a level for the first time or beating your record gives new coins.
- Real-money (Google Play) purchase screens no longer appear; they take you to the coin-based lives store instead.

### Installation
1. Install `popclassic.vpk` with VitaShell (save data is kept).
