name: VitaKotor2 v0.5.8
body:
# VitaKotor2 v0.5.8 — More cores, and long sessions fixed

This release puts the Vita's other two cores to work: the AI now runs beside
the drawing, and the game's GL translation runs on the GL worker. It also
fixes saving and the save list failing after a long session with a voice
pack, and a crash in Telos's cantina. The new threading was played for
several hours on a physical Vita; the two last fixes were checked in Vita3K.

## Faster

Hardware, Telos; each change was measured on and off in alternating 10 s
windows.
- **The AI runs on core 1 while the scene is drawn:** 22.3 against 19.5 FPS.
  Wherever the AI reaches into the client side, it waits for the drawing to
  end, so the two never touch the same data.
- **The game's GL translation (ASLgl) runs on the GL worker:** 18.4 against
  14.6 FPS.
- **Text widths are cached, and animated textures (water, ripples) are rebuilt
  on core 1:** 21.5 against 17.5 FPS.
- **Smaller savings:** light lists without repeated scans (about 1.5 ms a
  frame), and creatures not drawn in a frame animated one frame in three
  (about 0.7 ms).
- **A periodic hitch in Telos:** a creature with no clear path re-planned it
  every few seconds, about 110 ms a try. Searches that fail on the walkmesh
  alone are now remembered until the next load: worst frames of 60–92 ms
  instead of 165–194 ms.
- **Large fights:** compiled scripts stay in memory instead of being read
  again on every run. In the battle of Khoonda on Dantooine (TSLRCM, 20+
  fighters; [issue #4](https://github.com/pyjabox/VitaKotor2/issues/4)) this
  halves the AI's work: 55% more creatures are updated each frame, and frames
  take 158 instead of 192 ms. The battle is still slow (see below).

## Fixed

**Saving, the save list and the voices failing after a long session with a
voice pack.** After one to two hours, saving failed, Load Game listed no
saves, and the voices switched to English. The game forgets to close the file
of every dialogue line it plays. v0.5.6 kept loose voice lines in RAM, which
only delayed the problem: after about 512 lines, all 64 files a Vita app may
hold were taken. The loader now closes what the game forgets. Voices from
the game's archive (English) leaked too, more slowly.

**A crash in Telos's cantina,** which looked like a black screen at 30 FPS
with no sound, and made saves in that module look as if they would not load.
The game asked the loader for a C library function by name (`wcslen`), which
the loader did not provide. Saves made there were never damaged.

## Installation

1. Install `KOTOR2.vpk` with VitaShell. The title ID is `KOTR00002`.
2. Create `ux0:data/kotor2/`.
3. Copy from your own copy of the Android version **2.0.4**, using the 32-bit
   libraries from the APK's `lib/armeabi-v7a/` folder (the README lists each
   file's exact size and SHA-256):
   - `libkotor2.so`
   - `libObbVfs.so`
   - `libc++_shared.so`
   - `libminiz.so`
   - `libLzmaLib.so`
   - `main.213.com.aspyr.swkotorii.obb`
   - `patch.14.com.aspyr.swkotorii.obb`
   - the APK `assets/` directory
4. Install and enable `kubridge.skprx`.
5. Place `libshacccg.suprx` in `ur0:data/`.
6. Optionally, mods in `ux0:data/kotor2/mods/` and voice packs in
   `ux0:data/kotor2/localized/` (see the README).

**Upgrading from v0.5.2 or later:** install the VPK over the old one.
Game data, saves, mods, voice packs, the chosen language and the shader cache
stay as they are.
From v0.5.1 or older, see also the v0.5.2 notes: the first launch asks for a
language.

## Known issues and limitations

- **Very large fights are slow:** the battle of Khoonda with TSLRCM runs at
  about 6 FPS. The engine gives its AI 10 ms a frame; in such fights that runs
  out, and creatures of lower priority act only every few frames, so some
  seem idle. `ai_mode.txt` containing a number of milliseconds (1 to 65)
  raises the budget, at a cost in frame rate.
- **The menu before the game is in English.**
- **Mods in another language:** what a mod has only in English shows in
  English, voice lines added by mods are English (they were never dubbed), and
  a mod's own voice-line and lip-sync files are used instead of a voice pack's
  (TSLRCM: 4 lines and the lip sync of 9 areas). Details in the README.
- **With mods, launches take about 1 s longer** while they are indexed, and the
  first launch in a new language about 2 s more to build its talk table.
- **Noise behind the sound in busy scenes,** such as Telos. The decoders and
  the mix were checked and are clean; the cause is not known yet
  ([issue #5](https://github.com/pyjabox/VitaKotor2/issues/5)).
- **About one launch in three takes about 11 s longer,** in the engine's scan of
  `dlc/`. The cause is not known yet.
- **Shorter hitches remain** (usually 0.12–0.23 s, occasionally more) when new
  content is first read from the memory card, at about 10 MB/s: the minimap's
  first draw, dialogue entries and their voices, creatures spawned by scripts.
- **Loading-screen images** still take about 0.1–0.35 s each.
- **Heavy scenes remain CPU-bound,** mostly in the engine's per-object rendering
  work.
- **Visual changes:** no dynamic shadows and no bloom passes. Rooms keep their
  baked lighting.
- **Idle objects update less often:** idle creatures, placeables, doors and
  items get their AI update every third frame, and creatures not drawn in a
  frame are animated one frame in three. Nothing was noticed in testing.
- **One frame of extra latency:** the GL worker lets the game run up to one
  frame ahead, and the AI's decisions reach the screen one frame later. An
  object stepping out from cover can appear up to three frames late
  (occlusion culling).
- **Touch:** only the front touchscreen is used. The game keeps its controller
  layout, so its touch-only on-screen controls are not shown.
- **First launch:** it can take about two minutes while archives are scanned
  and shaders compile, and the loading screen can sit still for much of it.
- **Shader cache:** if a warm launch black-screens, remove
  `ux0:data/shader_cache/KOTR00002/` and relaunch.
- **No complete playthrough certified yet.** Trophies, cloud saves and online
  features are unavailable.

## Switches

Create the file in `ux0:data/kotor2/` and relaunch; delete it to go back.
- **New:** each of these files containing `0` turns one v0.5.8 change off,
  going back to how v0.5.7 did it:
  - `ai_thread.txt`: the AI on the game thread.
  - `aslw_mode.txt`: ASLgl on the game thread.
  - `offload_mode.txt`: text widths and animated textures on the game thread.
  - `scene_mode.txt`: the engine's own light lists, and every creature
    animated every frame.
  - `path_mode.txt`: no failed path search remembered.
  - `script_mode.txt`: scripts read from the archive on every run.
- `ai_mode.txt` containing `0`: the game's own AI loop, with no throttle and no
  AI caches (slower in busy areas). Containing a number from 1 to 65: the AI's
  time budget in milliseconds (the engine's is 10).
- `touch_mode.txt` containing `0`: buttons only, as in v0.4.2.
- `loadscreen_mode.txt` containing `0`: black screen until the legal screen, as
  in v0.4.2.
- `patcher_mode.txt` containing `0`: vitaGL's vertex-program requests go
  straight to the shader patcher and nothing is freed, as in v0.4.2 (the pool
  stays at 4 MB).
- `fps_cap.txt` containing `0`: no 30 FPS cap. `LockFramerate=1` under
  `[Graphics Options]` in `swkotor2.ini` then caps again, and `V-Sync=0` turns
  vsync off.
- `room_distance.txt` containing a distance in metres: rooms beyond it are not
  drawn (up to about 25% faster where long views open, with distant geometry
  missing).
- `glw_mode.txt` containing `0`: vitaGL on the game thread, as in v0.2.0.
- `dxt_mode.txt` containing `0`: DXT textures decoded on the CPU, as in v0.3.0.
- `mipgen_mode.txt` containing `0`: every mip chain built by the engine, as in
  v0.3.0.

This release contains no copyrighted game code or data.

`KOTOR2.vpk` SHA-256: `a8dddf4ac000e38afd25dd07afcf5421443cd0be99ee6520ecc6643204f66950`

name: Halo CE for PS Vita 1.1.2
body:
# Halo CE for PS Vita 1.1.2

File Share with friends, a lot more Forge, touch on the Vita, and crossplay
with today's PC servers (OpenCE 40 and 41). Install
`halo-ce-vita-1.1.2-vita.vpk` with VitaShell over your current Halo CE; maps,
saves and settings carry over. In-game updates: Settings > Game > Updates
(from 1.1.1 on, the update is signed and checked before it is kept).

## New

- **File Share with friends.** FRIENDS > a friend who is online > FILE SHARE:
  browse the map variants and game variants they share and download one (you
  are asked first). Share your own files, stop sharing, or send one to a friend
  (they are asked before anything arrives). Friends only; every file is
  checked before it is saved and a downloaded variant never replaces yours.
- **Touch.** Drag a menu list to scroll it. In Forge: drag an object or a spawn
  point to move it; a second finger down while carrying turns it. Works in
  network Forge games. Settings panel: Touch in Forge.
- **Forge.** Teleporters (sender and receiver on a channel), your own game type
  spots (CTF flags, King hills, Oddball spawns, Race checkpoints), object
  physics (Normal, Fixed, Phased), nudge in 1, 5, 10 or 25 cm steps, magnets
  that snap blocks flush, and a position readout. Players on 1.1.1 can't join a
  Forge game whose map uses the new features; they are told they need a newer
  Halo CE. Maps without them still work.
- **Crossplay.** OpenCE network versions 40 and 41 join from the server
  browser, with their refusal reasons shown in words. A signed version list can
  add future PC versions without a game update (Settings > Vita and PC > PC
  versions list: Auto or Built-in).
- **Setup for PC.** The install helper is a standard wizard: pick the
  platform, then Automatic (your MCC) or Manual (Xbox files + Custom Edition),
  and it downloads, verifies and installs the signed PC build.
- Classic+ menus fixed up: no cut or crowded text, English and Spanish.
- The tester's flaming helmet list is updated.

## Fixes

- The live menu background ("The live background could not be made") fits in
  memory again. The first start takes a few minutes to prepare it; after that
  it is quick.
- Touch drags in the menus follow your finger: the highlight moves with it, and
  the server browser's list scrolls with it.
- Forge: a respawn point or spawn marker you hold stands on the crate or ledge
  you aim at, instead of falling to the floor under it.
- Forge: shots pass through PHASED objects, a rejoin no longer ends the host's
  game, a game doesn't end when one team is left, flags and checkpoints stand on
  the ground, and CTF works on a variant with the flags on the "wrong" sides.
- Forge menu controls shown in full in Spanish.
- Online and installer security fixes. The installer no longer picks up a VPK
  by itself; the signed download is the default.

## Known issues

- Two-finger turn in Forge is new; tell us how it feels.
- A Vita behind a VPN or a datacenter address can't join a default OpenCE
  server of version 40 or more (the game says so).
- Roll in Forge still needs the buttons.
- PC builds are still experimental.

## Files

- `halo-ce-vita-1.1.2-vita.vpk` - the Vita game (install with VitaShell)
- `halo-ce-vita-1.1.2-pc-windows.zip`, `halo-ce-vita-1.1.2-pc-linux.tar.gz` - PC builds (experimental)
- `HaloCEVitaInstaller.exe` - the Windows install tool (ffmpeg 9.0.2, GPL v3, is bundled; its source is linked in README-installer)
- `halo-update.txt` + `.sig`, `halo-update-pc.txt` + `.sig` - signed update manifests
- `SHA256SUMS`

name: Hollow Knight V1.0
body:
**Changelog:**

- Greatly reduced loading times between rooms (from 20+ seconds down to a few seconds in most areas, "depending on free ram availability")
- Reduced CPU usage of enemies, NPCs and overall world objects
- Reduced lag spikes when hitting enemies and breaking objects
- Reduced lag spike when character was simply moving/jumping/etc
- Fewer out-of-memory crashes during long play sessions
- Lightened certain heavy particle effects to avoid unnecessary cpu usage
- Fixed hit effects and other effects sometimes disappearing
- Replaced the garbage collector with an incremental one, which spreads it's work over many frames instead of causing freezes
- Removed unnecessary memory cleanups during room transitions/respawns, which caused longer loading times
- Game data is now packed as compressed archive, which roughly halves the install size.
- Language fonts are now loaded only when that exact language is selected (Which saves ~20MB of ram depending on the language)
- Assets from the previous areas are now properly freed when they're no longer needed and we've got small amount of ram available
- Fixed front touch buttons (Quick Cast and Quick Map) which did not function as intended before
- Fixed appearing/dissapearing grass texture
- Improved sound effect & music quality
- Backported many fixes and improvements from the latest PC version of Hollow Knight

body:
The game now raises the PS Vita's CPU clock to 444 MHz itself, so the sound no longer crackles at the stock clock.

- **No more crackling.** The game started at 333 MHz, where the audio mixer's core ran 92-95% busy on the Bridge and audio crackled. You had to overclock in PSVshell to get rid of it. The game now sets the CPU to 444 MHz, the most an application may set, and the GPU to 222 MHz. There the mixer's core is about 74% busy, and walking holds 60 fps where it fell to about 44. A higher clock you set in PSVshell is kept.
- **The build includes a small native plugin** (`DrifterClock`) that sets the clocks. It is compiled with the PS Vita SDK that setup installs, so building works as before.

name: Shadow Fight 2 for PS Vita v1.0
body:
The first release of Shadow Fight 2 for PS Vita: the full single-player game, with physical controls in fights.

**This contains no game files.** You need your own APK of Shadow Fight 2 **1.9.38** (versionCode 1000109, armeabi-v7a), and a PC with Python 3 to prepare the game data. The tool also downloads about 300 MB of content packs from Nekki's servers, so that step only works while they keep serving them.

## Installing

Full instructions are in the [README](../../#installing). In short:

1. Set up the Vita: add `kubridge.skprx` to your `config.txt`, then run ShaRKBR33D to get `libshacccg.suprx`.
2. Install `ShadowFight2.vpk` with VitaShell.
3. Run `make_game_data.py` on your APK and copy the `shadowfight2` folder it makes to `ux0:data/`.
4. Start the game.

**Close the game and start it again at least once before the second act.** The content packs are only picked up from the second launch on. Once is enough, and your progress is kept.

## Files

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `ShadowFight2.vpk` | The port. Install this on the Vita |
| `make_game_data.py` | Makes the game data from your APK. Run this on a PC |
| `ShadowFight2-Vita-v1.0.zip` | Both of the above, with short instructions |
| `SHA256SUMS.txt` | Checksums |

## Known limits

- Offline only.
- A PlayStation TV isn't supported, because menus need the touchscreen.
- The cheats panel is on by default. Set `cheats` to `0` in `controls.txt` to turn it off.

name: v2.0.9h - speed like a pegasus
body:
## Changes

- Fixed a crash on every door with dynamic shadows turned off (sprite shadows). Link's shadow tried to remove itself from the previous map after that map had already been unloaded. This is the "every door crashes after the Dungeon 3 bell" report.
- Fixed stutters of almost a second in Dungeon 3, 6 and 8. The Dodongo Snakes created a new collision box every frame, and every box stayed attached to the snake, so the game produced more and more temporary data the longer you stayed in the dungeon. After a few minutes the memory was full and the game had to clean up in the middle of play. This bug is also in the original game.
- With dynamic shadows turned off (sprite shadows), the overworld no longer produces temporary data on every frame: each shadow created a new position object per frame just to copy its coordinates. This also led to clean-ups during play in longer sessions.
- The overworld no longer gets slower the longer you play. Monkeys from the bridge piled up on every return to the overworld, and leftover enemy shadows were still processed every frame after their enemy was gone. The frame rate on the overworld now stays at 60 fps over long sessions.
- The overworld now also stays in memory while you are in a dungeon, not only in houses and caves. Coming back from a dungeon or after an instrument restores it instead of loading it again (about 0.26 s instead of about 0.4 s on the Vita).
- The last eight houses, caves and dungeon rooms you visited are kept ready, so going back into them loads faster. Long sessions need fewer garbage collections (9 instead of 13 in a full stress test, 6.8 s instead of 10.9 s in total).
- Menus and the inventory now run at a steady 60 fps. While the game is paused, the world is drawn once and reused instead of being redrawn every frame.
- The map in the inventory is shown larger: it grows to the biggest size that fits on the screen.
- Button prompts use the Vita labels by default (face symbols, L/R, Select/Start).
- Saves are safer: the previous save is kept as a backup and used automatically if a save file is missing or damaged. A failing autosave no longer stops the door transition.
- The intro now starts at 60 fps right away instead of running at 30 fps for the first seconds.
- Writing the log no longer causes short stutters; it is written in the background.
- Colour correction and the pixel grid no longer switch the whole frame to the PC rendering path. The pixel grid is drawn as an overlay on top of the frame.
- New for testers: Cheats > Stress Test plays through all dungeons, every overworld door, the whole overworld and repeated save loads, cycling through several settings and game scales, and writes a summary with frame rates per setting and scale to the log. It also stays 30 seconds in the busiest room of every dungeon and warns when normal play produces more than 2 KB of temporary data per frame. Saving is blocked while it runs and your settings are restored afterwards.

## Known Limitations

- At game scale 1x the overworld runs at 30 fps. That scale shows nine times as much of the world as 3x, which is more than the Vita's CPU and GPU can draw at 60 fps. Houses, caves and dungeons run at 60 fps at 1x.
- With colour correction turned on, the game runs at 30 fps. The correction is an extra full-screen pass that costs about 8 ms of GPU time per frame.

This release was brought to you by: @NateXS, @gradylink, @NishiOwO, @luarpri, @MikeDev101, @Dogo6647, @Mistium, @ZacharyLeahan, and @PwLDev

name: VitaKotor v0.5.1-multicore.2 — tuned for every graphics option on
body:
A test pre-release from the `multicore` branch, aimed at playing with Shadows, Grass, Frame Buffer and 32-bit textures all on. It builds on multicore.1: the AI now runs alongside the 3D scene far more of the time, and one graphics stall the port caused itself is gone.

## What changed

- **The AI waits far less for the scene.** In multicore.1 the AI often had to stop partway and wait for the drawing to finish, mostly when it started a character animation or loaded a script. Animations are now queued and played the moment the drawing is done, and script loading shares the game's resource manager through a lock instead of stopping. In the Upper City the wait after each frame's drawing dropped from 3.8 ms to 2.0 ms; in the Lower City to 0.2 ms.

- **A texture update no longer stalls the frame.** The game updates one texture every frame, and each update made the game core wait for the graphics core to finish everything before it: up to 3 ms a frame. It is now queued like every other draw call.

- **New option: `ShadowDistance`.** How far away, in metres, creatures still cast shadows when Shadows is on. The default is the original `35`; `20` saves about 1 ms in the Upper City crowds.

- **KOTOR-nolog.vpk**: an optional build with diagnostic logging disabled. Install it in place of `KOTOR.vpk` if you prefer not to have a log file written.

### What to expect

With every graphics option on and 32-bit textures, the Taris Lower City now averages about 34 ms a frame, right at the edge of the 30 fps lock: most frames make it, some show for an extra refresh. The Upper City South crowds still run at about 17 fps and the Undercity at about 19: those areas draw 500 to 800 objects a frame, and that work is the game's own code on one core, whatever the settings. With FrameLock at 30, frames that miss the lock are shown for an extra refresh; `FrameLock=20` gives an even 20 in those areas if you prefer steady to fast.

## Updating

Install `KOTOR.vpk` over your current one. Your files in `ux0:data/kotor/`, your saves and your mods stay as they are. If anything goes wrong, set `ServerOverlap=0` under `[Vita Options]` in `swkotor.ini`, or reinstall multicore.1 or v0.5.0 from the releases page.

## Honest limits

- **Tested for one evening in Taris.** Several sessions in the Upper City, Lower City and Undercity with every graphics option on, with no crashes. The last small widening of the animation and lock changes has not been played yet.

- **32-bit textures fill the Vita's video memory** in the busy Taris areas, and the rest spills into regular memory. It has not caused trouble so far, but the bigger outdoor areas have not been tried at 32-bit.

- **Mod sets have not been tried with this build.**

- **The loading screen runs twice when you load a save** (issue #13), and **the rare crash after an area-change auto-save** (issue #12) is still open.

## Everything else from multicore.1 still applies

The AI runs on its own core while the scene draws, the graphics calls run on another, and `ServerOverlap=0` turns the AI overlap off.

## You need your own copy of the game

This is a loader, not a game. It needs the Android release's `main` and `patch` `.obb` files, which you must own.

## Something broken?

Open an issue with `ux0:data/kotor/log.txt` attached, say where in the game it happened, and whether it still happens with `ServerOverlap=0`.

name: v0.2.3
body:
Stable release of the 0.2.2 and 0.2.3 betas (details in their entries
below).

- **More headroom in crowded fights**: the game's locks and clock reads are
  3–4× cheaper on a real console (Act V patrol: 6 % less work per frame).
- **No more sound crackle or dropouts** in crowded fights (output limiter,
  audio thread moved off the graphics core).
- **Short presses are no longer lost when the frame rate drops**, and a
  quick tap of the aim button attacks/clicks once (reported fixed by a
  player on console with 0.2.3-beta).
- The app version shown by the Vita now follows the release (`APP_VER`
  00.23 instead of 00.00).

name: N.O.V.A 2 Vita v1.0.2
body:
# N.O.V.A 2 Vita v1.0.2

This is a wrapper/port of **N.O.V.A. 2 – Near Orbit Vanguard Alliance HD** (Gameloft) for the PS Vita.

## Changelog

- v1.0.2: Exit fix.
  - **Exiting from the main menu now returns to the LiveArea.** The game's exit button
    calls Android's `GLGame.Exit()`, which the port left empty, so the game froze on a
    black screen. It now closes the app like on Android.
  - **If the game suddenly crashes at boot after working fine before**, check that
    `ux0:data/nova2/libnova2.so` is intact by copying it again from the APK
    (`lib/armeabi-v7a/libnova2.so`). On my own console, 56 KB of that file got corrupted
    on the memory card, which made the game crash at startup with no code change.
    The same kind of corruption can also damage the `.gla` data files or the saves.

- v1.0.1: Save hotfix.
  - **Progress now saves on a fresh install.** The game saves to its Android data folder,
    which the port maps to `ux0:data/nova2/saves/`. The game never creates that folder
    (on Android it always exists), and the old README said it was created automatically.
    If it was missing, every save failed silently, so after a restart there was only
    "New Game" and no "Continue". The port now creates `ux0:data/nova2/saves/` at startup.
  - **Already playing?** Just install the new VPK. If `ux0:data/nova2/saves/` already
    existed on your card, your progress was being saved and is kept.
  - Note: like on Android, the game only saves at checkpoints and when a level is finished,
    not when pausing or quitting.

- v1.0: Initial release.
  - **Plays at 60 FPS at native 960x544**, 1:1 with the Vita screen. The engine is given the
    real resolution, so the 3D game and HUD fill the screen without scaling. The static 800x480
    loading/title backgrounds are stretched to fullscreen at sprite level.
  - **Intro video plays unconverted.** `GLVideo.mp4` (H.264 Baseline 640x360 @ 60 fps + AAC
    44.1 kHz) is played exactly as shipped with the game. SceAvPlayer refuses this file, so the
    port uses its own MP4 demuxer with the Vita's **hardware H.264 decoder** (`sceAvcdec`) and
    software AAC audio. Skip it with Cross or Start.
  - **Full physical controls.** Every visible HUD button is mapped to a physical button, using
    the button positions read from the game's own code:
    - Left stick: move. Right stick: camera.
    - R: fire (hold). L: special power. Cross: jump.
    - Circle: reload. Triangle / D-Pad Up: next weapon. D-Pad Down: previous weapon.
    - D-Pad Left / Right: change special power. Square: grenade. Start: pause.
  - **Virtual touch controls at 1% opacity.** The joystick, fire, jump and special-power buttons
    are nearly invisible but still respond to touch. The HUD that shows ammo and grenades stays
    fully visible.
  - **Smooth camera with adjustable sensitivity.** The right stick works like a continuous finger
    drag: hold it to keep turning, light tilt for precise aiming. Press **Select + D-Pad Up/Down**
    to set the sensitivity (1-10, default 4). A bar at the top of the screen shows the level, and
    the setting is saved in `ux0:data/nova2/camera_sens.txt`.
  - **Performance fixes.** Removed per-frame log writes and per-sound log spam. Added a negative
    cache for missing files: the engine looks for a loose `.wav` that does not exist before every
    footstep or gunshot, and that used to stall a frame each time.
  - Software ATC texture decoding, Vox audio through `sceAudioOut`, Gameloft DRM bypassed, and
    save/data paths remapped to `ux0:data/nova2/`.

## Setup Instructions

In order to properly install the game, you'll need to extract the data from the original Android game.

1. Install the `kubridge` and `fd_fix` plugins on your PS Vita.
2. Install `libshacccg.suprx`, if you don't have it already, by following [this guide](https://samilops2.gitbook.io/vita-troubleshooting-guide/shader-compiler/extract-libshacccg.suprx).
3. Obtain the original APK of N.O.V.A. 2 HD (`NOVA-2-HD-v1-0-5.apk`) and its game data folder (`/sdcard/gameloft/games/GloftN2HP/` from an Android device where the game was installed and run once).
4. Extract the `.apk` using any zip extractor.
5. Place `libnova2.so` (from `lib/armeabi-v7a/` inside the APK) in `ux0:data/nova2/`.
6. Place `assets/data.save` from the APK in `ux0:data/nova2/assets/`, and the APK's `res/raw/` files in `ux0:data/nova2/res/raw/`.
7. Copy the whole `GloftN2HP/` data folder (the `.gla` files, `sounds_hi.glza`, `oconf.bar`, `GLVideo.mp4`, ...) to `ux0:data/nova2/GloftN2HP/`.
8. Download and install `nova2.vpk` on your PS Vita.

`libStormGLOFT.so` and `libmthook.so` are not needed.

## Controls

- **Left Analog** - Move
- **Right Analog** - Camera (hold to keep turning; light tilt = precise aim)
- **R** - Fire (hold)
- **L** - Use special power
- **Cross** - Jump
- **Circle** - Reload
- **Triangle / D-Pad Up** - Next weapon
- **D-Pad Down** - Previous weapon
- **D-Pad Left / Right** - Change special power
- **Square** - Grenade
- **Start** - Pause
- **Select + D-Pad Up / Down** - Camera sensitivity (1-10)
- **Touch Screen** - Original touch controls (drawn at 1% opacity)

## Known Issues

- Only the boot intro video is supported. Any later video request is skipped.
- Pause, weapon and grenade touch spots were measured from screenshots (they are 3D HUD nodes). If one of them misses on your console, please report it with a log.
- Very heavy combat may still show small hitches on slow memory cards (sound effects are streamed from `sounds_hi.glza`).

## Troubleshooting

**"Looks like you haven't installed the data files" on boot:** `ux0:data/nova2/libnova2.so` is missing or in the wrong folder.

**Black screen / crash while loading:** check that `ux0:data/nova2/GloftN2HP/` contains all the `.gla` files and `sounds_hi.glza`, and that `kubridge`, `fd_fix` and `libshacccg.suprx` are installed.

**If it still crashes**, please report it with:

1. The newest `ux0:data/nova2/logs/nova2_NNNN.log` (from the time of the crash; do not delete it).
2. The newest `ux0:data/psp2core-*-eboot.bin.psp2dmp` core dump.
3. A note on exactly when it happens (boot, intro, menu, which level).

## Credits

- TheFloW for the `so_loader` wrapper and Android porting boilerplate.
- Rinnegatamante for `vitaGL` and porting tools.
- v-atamanenko for `FalsoJNI` and the soloader boilerplate.
- Gameloft for the original game.

name: Half-Life 2 for PS Vita 0.1.3-beta
body:
Water reflections, sharper textures, smoother lighting, and nine community fixes.

**Download `hl2_vita-0.1.3-beta.zip` below** and install `hl2_vita.vpk` over your current version: your saves, settings and compiled shaders stay. The new water needs a few new shaders: they compile the first time water appears, or choose Prepare shaders > Prepare again in the main menu. New to the port? Follow [INSTALL_VITA.md](https://github.com/LargeVegetable/source-engine/blob/vita/INSTALL_VITA.md).

### New

- **Texture detail** (Options > Video): Medium is now the default texture setting. It makes walls, floors and characters sharper. The low setting uses less video memory and looks like 0.1.2. A change applies at the next map or save load.
- **Water reflections**: water reflects the sky and its surroundings instead of being dark and flat. The reflections come from pre-made cube maps, so they don't show characters or moving objects.
- **Water splashes are back**, with their sound, from objects, the buggy's wheels and bullets. Bullet splashes are thinned out (one every quarter second, nearby only) to keep their cost down.
- **Smoother lighting on characters and objects**: it now changes gradually as they move between light and shade, instead of in steps. Muzzle flashes, the flashlight and explosions still light them instantly.

### Fixed

- **Music resumes when you load a save** made while music was playing. Loading also no longer warns that the save file is suspect. Saves made with 0.1.2 benefit too.
- **A likely cause of freezes while loading the next map** ([#5](https://github.com/LargeVegetable/source-engine/issues/5)) is fixed ([#14](https://github.com/LargeVegetable/source-engine/pull/14)).
- **Playing right after Prepare shaders could crash** a few minutes in; preparing shouldn't cause this any more ([#17](https://github.com/LargeVegetable/source-engine/pull/17)). Restarting the game after preparing is still recommended.
- **No more stutter a few words into G-Man's opening speech**: long voice lines and large sounds now play in pieces instead of loading whole ([#16](https://github.com/LargeVegetable/source-engine/pull/16)).
- **A short freeze when Kleiner first appears** in the opening is gone; the same fix covers Breen, Eli and the Vortigaunts set up the same way later ([#15](https://github.com/LargeVegetable/source-engine/pull/15)).

### Faster

- Background threads now sleep when they have nothing to do instead of checking for work every millisecond ([#19](https://github.com/LargeVegetable/source-engine/pull/19)), and drawing skips a needless system call each time it locks a material ([#20](https://github.com/LargeVegetable/source-engine/pull/20)), for a slightly higher frame rate.
- Game data now loads in the background on the second processor core instead of the busy main one, so sounds and models arrive sooner and hold up the game less often ([#21](https://github.com/LargeVegetable/source-engine/pull/21)).
- Saving is faster, so the pause at autosaves is shorter: 193 ms down to 144 ms on one train station map ([#23](https://github.com/LargeVegetable/source-engine/pull/23)).
- The menu font is read once at startup instead of ten times, saving about half a second and some memory ([#22](https://github.com/LargeVegetable/source-engine/pull/22)).

### Thanks

Thanks to [highda](https://github.com/highda) for all nine of the changes linked above, each one carefully measured and tested on a Vita.

### Known issues

- Rarely, the game can crash or freeze while loading the next map. If it freezes, wait a minute before closing it: it writes a report to the boot log. Save often.
- Cube map reflections are off on surfaces other than water, and the intro videos don't play.
- kubridge has known offsets only for firmware 3.60 and 3.65; on others it warns that crashes may occur.
- Half-Life 2 only: no Episodes, Lost Coast, multiplayer or mods.

### Reporting bugs

Open an [issue](https://github.com/LargeVegetable/source-engine/issues) with `ux0:data/hl2_vita_boot.txt`, `ux0:data/halflife2/engine.log`, `crash.log` if there is one, your firmware and model, any plugins you run, where you were in the game, and the version (top right of the menus). README_VITA.md has the details.

Not affiliated with or endorsed by Valve or Sony. Free, and it must stay free.

SHA-256 of the zip: `be1dd4eb481ca8c0c8d42f8fe9d3332ed976578a8818080cb16812408f0d1dc0`

name: v1.0.1
body:
Fixes for crashes and freezes that show up after long play sessions. Same files and installation as v1.0.0: only `sh4vita.vpk` changes (the `eboot.bin` inside). The data preparers are unchanged. If you already prepared your game files, you do not need to do it again: install the new VPK over the old one with VitaShell and keep `ux0:data/sh4/` (saves included).

## What changed

- **Memory:** the game kept every unread SDL input event in memory, about 4.6 MB of the host heap after 25 minutes. They are now discarded.
- **Out of memory in long sessions:** the game's own linear memory reservation is now 56 MiB instead of 64 (the highest use we measured was 47.5 MiB). This avoids `guest memory exhausted` crashes seen after about 50 minutes, for example in the hospital. If a scene ever misbehaves, `SH4_ARENA_MB=64` in `ux0:data/sh4/env.txt` restores the original size.
- **Render freeze:** fixed a race between two threads sending drawing commands, which could freeze the game after 1 to 2 hours. A watchdog now also releases stranded commands.

## Files

| File | For |
|---|---|
| `sh4vita.vpk` | PS Vita (install with VitaShell) |
| `sh4prep-windows.exe` | Windows |
| `sh4prep-macos-app.zip` | macOS, Apple Silicon: run with double-click app |
| `sh4prep-macos` | macOS, Apple Silicon: run with terminal version |
| `sh4prep-linux-x86_64.AppImage` | Linux x86-64: run with double-click version |
| `sh4prep-linux` | Linux x86-64: run with terminal version |

SHA-256 of `sh4vita.vpk`: `1ba609c01dc004435386a2ed7314db7246f3160ae4b3291c2f5796102918ec88`

Full installation steps are in the [README](https://github.com/vallfrr/sh4vita#install). You need your own copy of Silent Hill 4 from GOG ("1.0 gog v5"); no game file is included.

## Known limitations

- The long-session freeze fix was tested for about four hours of continuous play. Please save often.
- If you get a full-console freeze, please open an issue with `sh4log.txt` and `sh4log.txt.01` from `ux0:data/sh4/`.
- Continue on the title screen stays greyed out: use Load.
- Heavy scenes can drop below 30 fps; the first visit to a room can pause for about a second.

The code is under GPL-3.0 (see `LICENSE`). The source of this release is the tag `v1.0.1` of this repository.

name: Pikmin Vita v0.0.1
body:
# Pikmin for PS Vita v0.0.1

First PS Vita release of Open Nectar, a native port of Pikmin built on the decompilation.

You need your own Pikmin (USA) disc image. No game data is included.

## Install

1. Install `Pikmin-Vita-v1.0.vpk` with VitaShell.
2. Copy your Pikmin (USA) disc image to `ux0:data/Pikmin/`.
   Supported: `.iso`, `.gcm`, `.rvz`, `.wia`, Dolphin `.ciso`.
3. Launch Pikmin from the home screen.

Requirements: HENkaku/Ensō, game ID `GPIE01` (revision 1), about 1.5 GB free on `ux0:`.

## Features

- Full game, all areas, 30 fps target
- 16:9 widescreen
- Attract movies and cutscenes with full audio
- Saves are standard GameCube `.gci` files in `ux0:data/Pikmin/`, compatible with Dolphin and real hardware
- Loads disc images directly, including compressed RVZ
- Vita button prompts and an in-game options menu

## Known issues

- Materials without a baked shader fall back to a slower generic one, or outright break. send me log and .bin filesgenerated from game

## Reporting problems

Please attach `ux0:data/Pikmin/nectar.log`. If you can, also attach
`ux0:data/Pikmin/tev_keys.bin` and `ux0:data/Pikmin/vs_keys.bin` so missing shaders can be added.

## Credits

Open Nectar and the Pikmin decompilation projects.
Rinnegatamente for VitaGL.
Pikmin is a trademark of Nintendo. This project is not affiliated with Nintendo or Sony.

# ShotgunKing2Vita 0.78 alpha

## Español

**Aviso legal:** proyecto no oficial, sin relación con los autores del juego. No incluye ni distribuye archivos del juego. Requiere una copia legal y propia, en la versión correcta: The Final Checkmate 1.623b para Steam. No se da soporte a copias piratas ni otras versiones.

Primer Borrador de Shotgun King 2 Vita, funciona correctamente entre 30~60fps, solo dando bajones en el codex y ciertas partes del juego, funciona con MODS, pero es un poquito andar ajustandolos, todadia ando mejorando eso.

**VIBECODING al 100% si tienes un problema con las cantidades industriales de VIBECODING que le meti, bueno.... no lo bajes.**


SGKV00002 (Steam, título ShotgunK2Vita). Para Steam instala el VPK y copia solo data.sgr a ux0:data/shotgunk2vita_steam/; el primer arranque prepara los datos. 

Incluye instalador SGR, Vorbis, APIs de mods, controles y touch: un dedo mueve; mantener quieto y mover arrastra; dos dedos hacen clic izquierdo. Panel trasero L1/R1 para páginas; L/R físicos envían L2/R2. Mapas originales en español e inglés. Para SGK Extra instala también glac terminal, extra features y glacies collection.

Estado alpha: cobertura parcial de SUGAR; mods y hardware pendientes de aceptación. No admite saves cifrados de Steam ni servicios online. Los VPK públicos llevan cero parches privados: no se redistribuye el antiguo code_patches.h ni su historial. Los resultados PC no prueban FPS ni estabilidad en Vita.

Adjuntos: únicamente los dos VPK. Guarda un respaldo y comprueba primer arranque, movimiento/disparo, touch, audio, pausa/reintento y guardar/reabrir.

## English

**100% VIBECODING—if you have an issue with the industrial-sized quantities of VIBECODING I’ve packed in here, well... then don’t download it.**

**Disclaimer:** unofficial project, not affiliated with the game authors. No game files are included or distributed. Requires your own legally obtained copy in the correct version: The Final Checkmate 1.623b for Steam. Pirated copies and other versions are unsupported.

SGKV00002 (Steam; LiveArea title ShotgunK2Vita). Steam needs only the VPK and your data.sgr in ux0:data/shotgunk2vita_steam/; first boot prepares resources. 

Includes SGR installation, Vorbis, mod APIs, controls and touch: one finger moves; hold still then move to drag; two fingers left-click. Rear touch sends L1/R1 for pages; physical L/R send L2/R2. Original bilingual control maps. SGK Extra also needs glac terminal, extra features and glacies collection.

Alpha: partial SUGAR coverage, hardware and full mod compatibility pending. Steam encrypted saves and online services are unsupported. Public VPKs contain zero private patches; neither the old code_patches.h nor its history is distributed. PC checks do not establish Vita stability or FPS.

Only the VPK are attached. Back up userdata; test first boot, movement/shooting, touch, audio, pause/retry and save/reopen.


Validación local / Local validation: both ARM builds; common ASan/UBSan; 29 Python tests; Steam install/menu/game/touch and offline Vorbis checks. Hardware pending.

name: Zombie Infection (PS Vita) — Release v1.1
body:
# Zombie Infection (PS Vita) — Release v1.1

Release **v1.1** of the native iOS **Mach-O loader** port of *Zombie Infection* (Gameloft) for the PlayStation Vita. This release introduces hardware-accelerated H.264 cutscene video playback, eliminates visual glitches in in-engine cutscenes, overhauls the physical control mappings with dedicated buttons for holstering, jumping, healing and reloading, fixes edge-case crashes, activates triple buffering and shader patcher caching, and provides cross-platform compilation tooling.

---

## 📦 Release Package Contents

1. **`zombieinfection.vpk`** (v01.10): PlayStation Vita application package containing the updated Mach-O loader, hardware video decoder integration, optimized vitaGL renderer, and complete physical input handling.
2. **`rebase.bin`**: Binary relocation table (**61,828** absolute 32-bit memory pointers) for the iOS ARM executable of *Zombie Infection* 1.0.0.

---

## 🚀 Key Improvements in v1.1

### 🎬 Hardware H.264 & AAC Video Player Subsystem
- **Hardware-accelerated cutscenes**: Implemented a complete MP4/ISO-BMFF demuxer paired with the PS Vita hardware video decoder (`SceVideodec` / `sceAvcdec`), rendering directly into vitaGL CDRAM memory textures with 16:9 letterboxing.
- **High-fidelity audio decoding**: Software AAC-LC decoding powered by FFmpeg (`libavcodec`, `swresample`, `libavutil`) streaming on a dedicated thread via `SceAudioOut`.
- **Integrated playback**: Cutscenes (`cinematic_02_lab.m4v`, `cinematic_03_fin.m4v`) trigger seamlessly via `MPMoviePlayerController` and can be skipped at any time by pressing **Cross (✖)**, **Circle (●)**, or **Start**.
- **Bundle path probe**: Automatic detection of video file extensions (`.m4v`, `.mp4`) when queries omit extensions.
- **Debug shortcut**: Press **L + R + Triangle** during gameplay to trigger video playback verification.

### 🎨 Visual Glitch Elimination & vitaGL Optimizations
- **No speedhack regressions**: Cleaned vitaGL compilation flags, removing `DRAW_SPEEDHACK` and `SAMPLERS_SPEEDHACK` which were causing polygon tearing, flickering and distorted textures during in-engine cutscenes.
- **Shader Patcher Cache (`patched_vprog_cache`)**: Added a 64-entry cache in `ffp.c` for GXM patched vertex programs, reusing compiled shaders in 0 ms and avoiding hundreds of redundant `sceGxmShaderPatcherCreateVertexProgram` calls per frame.
- **Compiler Null Safety**: Guarded `shark_compile_shader_extended` against failed allocations, preventing `memcpy(NULL)` crashes and providing automatic fallback to the last valid shader in cache.
- **Expanded Matrix Stack**: Raised `GENERIC_STACK_DEPTH` from 2 to 16 in `vendor/vitaGL/source/shared.h`, preventing matrix stack overflow in complex camera/lighting transformations.
- **Triple Buffering**: Enabled `vglUseTripleBuffering(GL_TRUE)` to eliminate VBlank waiting stalls.
- **Memory thresholds**: Reallocated memory pools with `vglInitWithCustomThreshold` reserving 32 MB RAM heap, 16 MB CDRAM, and 8 MB PHYCONT for smooth level transitions and video buffers.

### 🎮 Dedicated Controls Overhaul
- **D-Pad Down**: Dedicated to **Holster / unDraw weapon** (`{0x2c, 0x3c}` → `PlayerTest::unDrawWeapon` / Back).
- **Triangle (▲)**: Dedicated to **Jump** (`0x64`).
- **D-Pad Left**: Dedicated to **Heal / Use Medikit** (`0x68`).
- **D-Pad Right**: Dedicated to **Reload weapon** (`0x98` / `MultiElement::ReloadBullets`).
- **L Trigger**: Contextual **Dodge** (`0x60`), with automatic fallback to **Reload** (`0x98`) when dodge is inactive.
- **Start / Select**: Clean pause menu and game resume (`CLevel::SetResume`).
- **Select + D-Pad ↑/↓**: Real-time right-stick camera sensitivity adjustment (levels 1–10, saved to disk).
- **L + R (held)**: Virtual on-screen touch controls hidden at 0% opacity by default for an unobstructed screen; hold L+R to toggle visible.

### 🛡️ Crash Fixes & Disk I/O Optimization
- **`PlayerTest::isCarryingVaccineTank` hook**: Intercepted with `macho_hook` to add NULL pointer validation, fixing the crash when toggling pause/resume via Start/Select in menus or opening scenes.
- **Disk I/O latency resolved**: Silenced thousands of missing texture probes (`.tga`, `.bmp`, `.gif`) in `d_fopen` and disabled `fflush` on `DEBUG` lines, eliminating severe stuttering and micro-freezes caused by synchronous memory card writes.

### ⚙️ Multiplatform Build System
- New `build.sh` script with automatic detection of `VITASDK` on macOS (`/Users/...`, `$HOME/vitasdk`) and Linux (`/home/...`).
- Portable multi-core parallel builds (`sysctl -n hw.ncpu` / `nproc`).
- Clean handling of `debug` and `release` build targets.

---

## 🎮 Complete Controls Reference

| PS Vita Input | Action | Behavior / Engine Mapping |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Front Touchscreen** | Touch UI | Full touchscreen input for menus and virtual buttons |
| **Left Analog Stick** | Movement | Drives game's HUD virtual analog stick (`0x18`) |
| **Right Analog Stick** | Camera look | Continuous touch-drag emulation with custom response curve |
| **Cross (✖) / R1** | Attack / Shoot | Primary attack (`0x74, 0x1c, 0x84, 0x80`) |
| **Square (◼)** | Secondary attack | Melee / secondary attack (`0x20`) |
| **Circle (●)** | Contextual action | Interact, pick up items, open doors (`0x24, 0x28, 0x30, 0x34`) |
| **Triangle (▲)** | Jump | Jump over obstacles (`0x64`) |
| **D-Pad Down (↓)** | **Holster weapon** | Guardar arma (`{0x2c, 0x3c}` → `PlayerTest::unDrawWeapon`) |
| **D-Pad Left (←)** | **Heal (Medikit)** | Usar botiquín de primeros auxilios (`0x68`) |
| **D-Pad Right (→)** | **Reload weapon** | Recargar munición (`0x98`) |
| **D-Pad Up (↑)** | Quick Turn | Giro rápido de 180° (`0x78`) |
| **L Trigger** | Dodge / Reload | Esquivar si hay esquive activo (`0x60`), o recargar arma (`0x98`) |
| **Start / Select** | Pause / Resume | Menú de pausa y reanudar partida |
| **Select + D-Pad ↑/↓** | Camera sensitivity | Ajuste de sensibilidad 1–10 (guardado en `camera_sens.txt`) |
| **L + R (held)** | Toggle HUD visibility | Alternar visibilidad de botones táctiles en pantalla (0% / 100%) |

---

## 🚀 Player Installation Guide

1. **PS Vita Requirements**:
   - Custom Firmware (**Enso 3.60 / 3.65** recommended).
   - `kubridge.skprx` installed under `*KERNEL` in `ur0:tai/config.txt`.
   - `libshacccg.suprx` present in `ur0:data/` (obtainable via **ShaRKBR33D**).

2. **Game Assets Setup**:
   - Extract `Payload/ZombieInfection.app/` from your decrypted iOS 1.0.0 `.ipa`.
   - Copy it to `ux0:data/zombieinfection/ZombieInfection.app/`.
   - Copy `rebase.bin` to `ux0:data/zombieinfection/rebase.bin`.
   - Required directory layout:
     ```text
     ux0:data/zombieinfection/
     ├── ZombieInfection.app/
     │   ├── ZombieInfection (original iOS binary)
     │   ├── data.pack, audio_*.pack, gll_font.pak, ...
     │   └── *.png, *.plist, cinematic_*.m4v, ...
     ├── rebase.bin
     ├── saves/ (created automatically on first launch)
     └── logs/  (created automatically, one log per run)
     ```

3. **Install the VPK**: Transfer and install `zombieinfection.vpk` (v01.10) using VitaShell.

---

## 📋 Changelog History

### v1.1.0 (2026-10-29)
- **Cutscene Video Player**: Added hardware H.264 video decoding (`SceVideodec`/`sceAvcdec`) and software AAC-LC decoding (`libavcodec`). Cutscenes `.m4v` play smoothly with audio and skip support.
- **Rendering & Cutscene Artifact Fix**: Removed `DRAW_SPEEDHACK` and `SAMPLERS_SPEEDHACK`, increased `GENERIC_STACK_DEPTH` to 16, and implemented 64-entry `patched_vprog_cache` in vitaGL.
- **Controls Refinement**: Reassigned D-Pad Down to weapon holstering, Triangle to Jump, D-Pad Left to Medikit heal, D-Pad Right to Reload, and L Trigger to contextual Dodge/Reload.
- **Crash Prevention**: Hooked `PlayerTest::isCarryingVaccineTank` with null safety.
- **Disk I/O Optimization**: Removed excessive logging in `d_fopen` and disabled `fflush` on debug lines.
- **Build System**: Added multiplatform `build.sh` supporting macOS and Linux. Bumped SFO version to `01.10`.

### v1.0.0-beta (2026-10-19)
- Initial native iOS Mach-O loader port reaching gameplay.
- 61,828 rebase words applied at `0x98000000`, 7,358 import slots resolved, 366 global constructors executed.
- GLES 1.x over vitaGL with `SOFTFP_ABI=1`, 960×544 presentation.
- OpenAL audio via openal-soft, FreeType font rendering, and analog stick camera look emulation.
author: MetalSyntax
homebrew_description: iOS to PS Vita port of Zombie Infection Gameloft
homebrew_long_description: An unofficial, native iOS-to-PS Vita wrapper port of Zombie Infection (originally developed by Gameloft). Unlike the Android ports, there is no .so here: this port ships its own Mach-O loader that maps the official iOS ARM executable (ZombieInfection, from the 1.0.0 IPA) into PS Vita RAM and replaces the Apple frameworks it uses (Foundation, UIKit, CoreGraphics, CoreAudio, OpenGL ES) with native implementations on top of vitaGL, OpenAL Soft, FreeType and the Vita system libraries. The game itself is built on the Irrlicht engine, which the loader runs untouched.

name: Strikers Vita 1.5.0
body:
## Strikers Vita 1.5.0

### Fixed
- **Pipeline Central running at 3-5 FPS.** Players who updated the VPK but kept an older `strikers.ini` still had settings that switched off the 1.4 performance profile, and Pipeline Central was hit hardest. 1.5 comments those outdated lines out automatically the first time it starts (the original lines stay in the file, with a note). Measured in Pipeline Central with a 1.3 `strikers.ini`: 6.4 FPS on 1.4, 48.9 FPS on 1.5.

### New
- **Menu language selector.** Set `language` in `strikers.ini` to `english`, `german`, `french`, `spanish` or `italian` (European disc), or `japanese` (Japanese disc). Left empty, the game follows the Vita's system language when the disc has it. The American disc is English only.
- **GameCube boot animation** while the game starts, rendered live with vitaGL and with its original music. Press X, O or Start to skip the rest once the game is ready; `vita_gc_intro = 0` turns it off.
- **Local multiplayer on PS TV** (or a Vita running MiniVitaTV): paired DualShock 3/4 controllers are assigned to players 1-4. **Not tested on hardware yet** — please report how it goes.

### Install
1. Install `strikers_vita.vpk` with VitaShell.
2. Back up `ux0:data/strikersVita/strikers.ini`, `cardA/` and `cardB/`, then copy this release's `strikers.ini` to `ux0:data/strikersVita/strikers.ini`. If you keep your own file, 1.5 still fixes the outdated performance settings in it.
3. The game requires your own `ux0:data/strikersVita/sms.psarc`, prepared as described in [ASSET_SETUP.md](https://github.com/robin994/strikersVita/blob/main/ASSET_SETUP.md). No game assets from the disc are included.

[CapUnlocker](https://github.com/GrapheneCt/CapUnlocker) is recommended (see the README).

### Credits
The boot animation uses the [gcintro](https://github.com/vaexenc/gcintro) recreation (MIT) through Rinnegatamante's vitaGL custom splash screen sample. The GameCube logo and jingle belong to Nintendo.

### Known limitations
- Stable 60 FPS is not certified in every scene: The Palace measures about 59 FPS, Pipeline Central about 46-49 FPS.
- Stadium intros and replays run at 30 FPS by design.

### Checksums (SHA-256)
- `strikers_vita.vpk`: `971af6b6514abcf7eeac5d385de8348e1f56cd970f5a154d69018714670616be`
- `strikers.ini`: `efdd23540d891ee7f96e0bebcea92e7c6c95a7521e4f75ae5ee418f538291f78`

name: v1.1
body:
Install `Tenkaichi3Decomp-Vita.vpk` with VitaShell. It installs over 1.0: your saves and settings in `ux0:data/bt3/` are kept, and the game files stay where they are. Setup is unchanged from 1.0 (see the README).

### New

- **Two players on a PS TV**: a second DualShock plays as player 2 (Versus Menu → Multiplayer). On by default;
  Options → Controller → Vita Settings → 2nd Pad turns it off. A DualShock's own L2, R2, L3 and R3 buttons work.
- **Clashes with Square**: beam struggles and rush clashes are won by pressing Square again and again instead of
  turning the left stick, and the prompt shows Square. Vita Settings → Clashes → Stick goes back to the stick.
- **Vita Settings** (Options → Controller): where L2, R2, L3 and R3 are on the touch panels (rear pad, the
  screen's corners, or off), Clashes, 2nd Pad and Mods.
- **Mods**: files in `ux0:data/bt3/mods/` replace the disc's (a single file of an archive, a whole archive, or a
  mod's own folder holding a modded disc's `DATA` folder). Vita Settings → Mods shows what is in use and turns them
  off. A mod that changes the game's program, like Budokai Tenkaichi 4, is left out with a message instead of
  crashing the game. See the README.

### Fixed

- The game no longer freezes after about 18 minutes of play (the picture stopped while the music went on).
- The space stage near Frieza's ship: parts of the red planet's clouds no longer vanish for a frame while the fighters
  move (it looked like flickering patches).
- The "ObjSeam" crash with Videl, the Great Saiyaman, Hercule and other characters (Majin Buu saga, Galactic
  Crisis, Makyo Star, some special attacks).
- Freezes from invalid maths results the PS2 never produces.
- Story mode: a won battle that opens a new saga always lists it.
- Dragon World Tour: no crash while Yamcha's invitation is pending.
- Long fights: no giant triangles or white lines when the graphics memory filled up; no wrong colours from mixed-up
  palettes.
- Coming back from the LiveArea or sleep: the game's speed is restored, and its files are reopened if the system
  closed them (glitches, slowdowns and crashes after resuming).
- A finger resting on the rear touch pad no longer holds L3 or R3.
- Setup: the game's files are found in more folder layouts, and the error lists what was found.
- When the picture stops, the game writes `ux0:data/bt3/hang.txt` for bug reports.

### Known issues

- On Namek, the ground under the water flickering while the fighters move
- Ad-hoc and online play between two Vitas are not implemented yet.

name: JAVITA 1.1.0
body:
Changelog:

Thanks for participating in the playtest!

## Highlights

- **Multiplayer.** `JAMPVITA.vpk` 
- **Improved booting speed.**.
- **Improved level loading times**, SP and MP.
- **Pre-built texture cache.** The first visit to a level no longer has to be slow. A PC
  tool (`tools/texbake`) builds the whole cache in seconds and copies one file to the card.
  Lowering texture detail no longer throws the cache away either.

## Performance

- Bug fixes, little performance improvements

## Fixed

- **Game closing on multiplayer join.** A load error during a join could shut the game
  down to the LiveArea. It now returns to the menu with a message. The same fix applies
  to single-player level loads.
- **Sound effects** load faster and a little cleaner.
- **Silent lightsaber after reloading a save.** Loading a save a second time muted the
  saber ignition sound until enough game time had passed. Force power screen tints could
  also get stuck after a reload.
- **Map downloads on weak Wi-Fi.** Blocks that arrive after a lost packet are kept instead
  of thrown away, roughly doubling download speed on a lossy connection. (Still slow, prepare assets on PC and copy over instead)
- **Server list on slow DNS.** Master server lookups wait as long as the Vita's own apps do.

## Install

1. Install `JAVITA.vpk` (single-player) and/or `JAMPVITA.vpk` (multiplayer) with VitaShell.
2. Copy the four `assets*.pk3` files to `ux0:data/JAVITA/base/` if you have not already.
3. Optional: run `tools/texbake` on your PC and copy its `pack.bin` to
   `ux0:data/JAVITA/texcache_dxt/` to skip the first-visit texture wait entirely.

Controls and settings are in the [README](https://github.com/NDRWhun/JAVITA#readme).

## Source

GPLv2 — full source for this build: https://github.com/NDRWhun/JAVITA

body:
# MKW Vita 1.4.2

Closer to the Wii: laps and Lakitu, the end of a race, course objects, item boxes and menus. Only the VPK changes: your 1.4.0 game files keep working.

>[!NOTE]
>**Coming from 1.4.x? Just install the new VPK.** 1.4.2 uses the same game files, so there's nothing to rebuild or copy.
>
>Coming from 1.3.0 or older? Rebuild your game files as described in the [1.4.0 release](https://github.com/boomannotjeff/mkwiita/releases/tag/1.4.0).


## What's new

### Racing

- **Lap counter and Lakitu.** Backing over the finish line no longer lowers your lap or brings Lakitu down with the lap sign.
- **Finish.** Lakitu flies in with the flag and follows your kart, like on the Wii.
- **End of race.** Racers who have finished lose their items. The out-of-bounds fade now draws under the HUD and results instead of over them.
- **Place number.** The black drop shadow behind your position is back.
- **Blue Shell.** It keeps facing forward instead of spinning like a Green Shell.

### Courses

- **Koopa Cape.** The tunnel glass draws over karts and items instead of under them. The same goes for every course's see-through parts.
- **Lava.** N64 Bowser's Castle lava columns and Grumble Volcano lava poles only show while erupting. Grumble Volcano's falling rocks vanish when they land.
- **Toad's Factory.** The falling crates show only while they're live, and they turn into iron boxes in Time Trials.
- **Cannons.** DK Summit, GCN DK Mountain and Maple Treeway cannons play their animation once per launch instead of looping.
- **Delfino Square.** The drawbridge animation follows how far the bridge is tilted.
- **SNES Ghost Valley 2.** The blocks rest, tumble and disappear like on the Wii.
- **Item boxes.** On Grumble Volcano, boxes on the falling rocks ride them down. On Wario's Gold Mine, the boxes along the cart line trail the carts.

### Menus

- **Main menu.** The frames no longer flash when selected (the Wii never selects them), and the titles have their glow back.
- **Drift page.** The flag no longer shows through the button movies, and the unselected movie is dimmed like on the Wii.
- **Sounds.** Pressing buttons during a page transition no longer plays button sounds.
- **Character on the kart.** Seated drivers blink and look ahead instead of staring at the camera.

Everything above is in the Retro Rewind edition too.

## Install

1. Install `mkw.vpk` (or `mkw-retro-rewind.vpk`), attached below, with VitaShell.
2. That's it if you're on 1.4.x. From an older release, rebuild your game files first (see the [1.4.0 release](https://github.com/boomannotjeff/mkwiita/releases/tag/1.4.0)).
3. Make sure `ur0:data/libshacccg.suprx` exists (run ShaRKF00D once).

Your licenses, times and ghosts stay.

The VPK contains no Nintendo game files. Please don't share your built game files.

## Building it yourself
- `Build MKW Vita.bat` builds the game files and the VPK (needs VitaSDK).
- `Build Game Files.bat` builds only the game files.
- See [BUILDING.md](BUILDING.md) for details.

name: GMCA v1.4.0
body:
### Added

- **Audio files from Files play in the music player (#33).** An audio file
  picked in Files opens Now Playing and the persistent mini-bar, like a Plex,
  Jellyfin or Emby track. The folder's audio files become the queue, in the
  order shown. Title, artist, album and length come from the file tags.
- **Search and Files can be reordered and hidden (#34).** They move and hide
  like libraries. Home and the profile stay in place, and the settings screen
  is renamed Sidebar.

### Fixed

- **Offline sidebar (#34).** Offline, library tabs follow the order and
  visibility saved for the server, and Jellyfin and Emby show Favorites
  instead of Watchlist.
- **Offline details of Jellyfin and Emby downloads.** A movie or show
  downloaded from Jellyfin or Emby now keeps its summary, poster, backdrop,
  cast and versions offline, plus the show, season and episodes for an
  episode. Downloads made before this release keep their minimal details.
- **Jellyfin and Emby versions.** The Version selector reads
  "1080p · HEVC · 1.4 Mbps" on every backend, and Download takes the version
  picked in the selector, like Play.
- **Resumed Plex transcodes (#72).** The OSD shows the resume time, chapter
  markers sit in the right place, and seeking works anywhere, before the
  resume point too.
- **FTP folders (#54).** Folders on FTP servers without MLSD (vsftpd,
  busybox, most routers) open again. On those servers a non-media file such
  as `readme.txt` shows as a folder.
- **Edit and Delete in the server menu (#54)** open their screen again.
- **macOS: crash at launch when the active server does not answer.** Errors
  from the C++ standard library escaped the app's error handling.
- **Rounded icon on the sign-in screens.** The icon on the connection type,
  sign-in and hint screens was clipped at its corners.
- **Server image paths.** An image path from the server that does not start
  with `/` is refused, so the access token cannot be sent to another host.

body:
# Ignition Vita v1.1

*(Español primero · English below)*

## 🇪🇸 Español

**Ignition Vita** es un port no oficial, de aficionados y sin ánimo de lucro, de *Ignition* (1997) para **PlayStation Vita**.

> **Este paquete NO contiene el juego.** Debes aportar los archivos de tu propia copia legal de *Ignition*. El proyecto no está afiliado ni respaldado por los propietarios de *Ignition* ni por Sony.

### Novedades de v1.1

- Corregido el cuelgue que podía producirse al terminar un campeonato y restaurado su avance normal.
- Corregidos el desbloqueo y la persistencia de vehículos, dificultades y pistas.
- Verificados en una PS Vita real: primer campeonato completo, coche **Banana**, dificultad **Amateur** y una pista adicional, conservados tras guardar y reiniciar.
- Carrera rápida y Persecución terminan correctamente y vuelven al menú.
- Guardado atómico: el progreso se escribe primero en un archivo temporal para reducir el riesgo de corrupción.
- Controles predeterminados mejorados: **✕ acelera** y **□ frena / marcha atrás**.
- Los botones de Vita pueden configurarse desde **Opciones → Jugador 1 → Configurar teclado** y las asignaciones persisten al reiniciar.
- Diversas mejoras de estabilidad. Objetivo de 30 FPS, con posibles caídas en zonas exigentes.

### Actualización desde v1.0

1. Haz una copia de seguridad de ux0:data/ignition/ign_3dfx.btz.
2. Instala IgnitionVita_v1.1.vpk encima de la versión anterior con VitaShell y homebrew inseguro activado.
3. No borres ux0:data/ignition/: ahí están los datos del juego, progreso y opciones.

### Limitaciones conocidas

- Pantalla dividida y multijugador online/en red están visibles pero desactivados.
- Los campeonatos posteriores al primero usan la misma ruta de progresión, pero sus premios no se han verificado uno por uno.
- PlayStation TV no está probado.

### Verificación

- VPK: IgnitionVita_v1.1.vpk
- Tamaño: 2.136.458 bytes
- SHA-256: fda91c1b687c7b5e76e9ec2e7b95668d93350ba7d54092dec7bf68b7a1795d50
- Código fuente correspondiente: IgnitionVita_v1.1_corresponding-source.tar.xz
- SHA-256 del paquete de fuentes: 290701fffba027dd8a902e0f12bf1ce71d275f932690d98d73c3c22572a24d27

Para informar de errores, abre un *Issue* e incluye modelo de Vita, modo, pista, vehículo, dificultad, frecuencia, pasos para reproducir y los logs de ux0:data/ignition/logs. No adjuntes archivos del juego.

---

## 🇬🇧 English

**Ignition Vita** is an unofficial, fan-made, non-commercial port of *Ignition* (1997) to **PlayStation Vita**.

> **This package does NOT contain the game.** You must provide files from your own legal copy of *Ignition*. The project is not affiliated with or endorsed by the owners of *Ignition* or Sony.

### What is new in v1.1

- Fixed the crash that could occur at the end of a championship and restored normal championship progression.
- Fixed unlocking and persistence of vehicles, difficulties and tracks.
- Verified on real PS Vita hardware: first championship completion, **Banana** car, **Amateur** difficulty and one additional track, all retained after saving and restarting.
- Quick Race and Chase now finish correctly and return to the menu.
- Atomic saves: progress is written to a temporary file first to reduce corruption risk.
- Improved defaults: **✕ accelerates** and **□ brakes / reverses**.
- Vita buttons can be remapped through **Options → Player 1 → Keyboard config**, and assignments persist after restarting.
- Several stability improvements. The target is 30 FPS, with possible drops in demanding areas.

### Updating from v1.0

1. Back up ux0:data/ignition/ign_3dfx.btz.
2. Install IgnitionVita_v1.1.vpk over the previous version with VitaShell and unsafe homebrew enabled.
3. Do not delete ux0:data/ignition/: it contains game data, progress and settings.

### Known limitations

- Split screen and online/network multiplayer remain visible but disabled.
- Later championships use the same progression path, but their rewards have not been individually verified end to end.
- PlayStation TV has not been tested.

### Verification

- VPK: IgnitionVita_v1.1.vpk
- Size: 2,136,458 bytes
- SHA-256: fda91c1b687c7b5e76e9ec2e7b95668d93350ba7d54092dec7bf68b7a1795d50
- Corresponding source: IgnitionVita_v1.1_corresponding-source.tar.xz
- Source package SHA-256: 290701fffba027dd8a902e0f12bf1ce71d275f932690d98d73c3c22572a24d27

Please report reproducible problems through *Issues* with your Vita model, mode, track, vehicle, difficulty, clock frequency, exact steps and logs from ux0:data/ignition/logs. Do not attach game files.

Full source, licenses and detailed documentation: https://github.com/Zeusthenen/Ignition-Vita

homebrew_description: Unofficial PlayStation Vita port of Ignition (1997)
homebrew_long_description:
Ignition (1997) is a PC arcade racing game. Ignition Vita lets you play the original Windows game on a PlayStation Vita.

It is not a rewrite or a remake. The port loads the original Ign_3dfx.exe (the 3dfx/Glide version of the game), runs its x86 code on the Vita through a dynamic recompiler (x86 → ARMv7), and provides, in native Vita code, everything the executable expects from Windows: files, timers, DirectInput, DirectSound, the Windows message loop, MCI CD audio and the Glide 3D API (translated to OpenGL calls on the Vita's GPU with vitaGL).

name: Mario Strikers Charged 1.1
body:
The performance update.

**Smoother play**
- Matches run at up to 60 fps. The Frame Rate setting is now **AUTO** by
  default: 60 when the Vita can keep up, a smooth 30 when it can't. Prefer a
  locked 30? Choose **30 FPS** in Settings.
- Mega Strikes run at a steady 30 fps at full resolution (about 15 fps
  before). Their glowing haze is drawn at a lower resolution and blended over
  the sharp, full-size scene.
- Snappier controls: a third less delay from button to screen, about a
  tenth of a second in normal play. Stick and touch respond faster in Mega
  Saves and other heavy scenes too.
- The picture size adapts to the load: effects soften first and the scene
  only slightly, so the frame rate holds without the game looking rough.
- Fewer hitches from those size changes: they now happen at the cuts into
  and out of a Mega Strike, not a few seconds into play, and a size used
  recently is switched back to quickly.

**Better picture**
- A light sharpening filter is on by default (Settings > Sharpness: SMOOTH).
  OFF, CRISP and CRISP+ are still there.
- SMOOTH also softens jagged character outlines, at almost no cost.
- Optional HD characters and ball: sharper faces, kits and ball in close-ups
  (Mega Strikes, celebrations, menus), made on your computer from your own
  game files with `tools/hdtex` and copied to `ux0:data/mscharged/hdtex.pack`.
  In normal play the game draws the same detail as before, so it costs no
  frame rate.
- When there's time to spare, the game is drawn above native resolution for
  cleaner edges.
- New optional **Distant Textures** setting for sharper ground and walls at an
  angle (experimental, off by default).

**Controls and gameplay**
- Tap anywhere on the title screen to start.
- All seven camera zoom levels are on the Options > Visual slider.
- The CPU plays just as well when your camera is zoomed in close.
- Quick screen taps are never missed, and button presses are never lost or
  repeated after a system pop-up.
- The stick moves the glove three times faster in Mega Saves by default, so
  you can reach the far side of the goal in time (Settings > Mega Save Speed:
  3x, 4x, 2x or ORIGINAL). Optional rear-touch aiming is in Settings too.

**Under the hood**
- Fixed a crash when starting a match after the picture size had changed a
  few times: unused graphics buffers are now freed, and the game only draws a
  larger picture when there is graphics memory to spare.
- Mega Strikes no longer drop to a low resolution when that would not make
  them any faster.
- More of the game's graphics come prebuilt, so a goal replay no longer stops
  for a loading bar the first time.
- Fixed new graphics effects never being built on the console (a fault in
  the shader cache code), which kept the sharpening and the lighter Mega
  Strike glow from switching on.
- More reliable shader cache and graphics memory recovery.
- Faster texture uploads and less background CPU use.
- The game's 3D models are rebuilt less often after loading screens and
  pauses (improvements shared with the Super Mario Galaxy port).
- Players' faces in celebrations, replays and cut-scenes are skinned on the
  graphics chip like the rest of the body, so those scenes give the CPU less
  to do.

Technical details for developers are in
[Technical Notes](docs/TECHNICAL.md#version-11-changes).

name: v1.3.0
body:
## v1.3.0

**Real 60 fps**
- Picture > Frame rate now offers **60**: the game's own logic runs at 60 fps, not frames drawn in between. On a real Vita it held 58-60 fps for about 95% of an hour of play; the heaviest scenes (the rainy bar entrance) drop toward 30, always at the right speed. It can be switched while playing. Off by default.
- Things that counted frames instead of time were fixed so 60 plays exactly like 30: Windy's leaping creatures, a sound fade that never ended, falling drops, stuns, moving scenery and gravity steps.
- The interpolated mode is gone from the menu (if you had it on, 60 is on now).

**Camera**
- New option, Sticks and aiming > Camera: **Avoids walls**. The camera pulls in towards Conker instead of ending up behind a door, a pillar or a corner, and keeps the widescreen view from cutting into side walls. Only the follow camera in play; cutscenes are untouched. Off by default.

**The B pads**
- The context-sensitive B pads carved on the ground (wood and stone) now show the Vita control you bound to B, carved in the same style, and follow your remapping.

**Faster**
- Texture loads that repeat within a frame are skipped (a few percent less work in heavy scenes).

Updating keeps your saves and settings. On 1.0.0-1.2.0 the game offers this update at start-up (needs Enable Unsafe Homebrew).

name: Wonder Boy: The Dragon's Trap - Vita 0.35-rc1
body:
Unofficial PlayStation Vita port of **Wonder Boy: The Dragon's Trap**, based on the Android ARMv7 version.

Download **wonderboy-vita-0.35-rc1.zip** below. It contains the Vita application, logo, and license notices. Installation instructions are in the [README](https://github.com/Cynostial/wonderboy-vita/blob/v0.35-rc1/README.md). GitHub's automatic source archives are for development.

### Installation

1. Install `wonderboy.vpk` through VitaShell. The port requires **kubridge** and **libshacccg.suprx**; see the README for setup.
2. Place exactly one supported Android **1.1.0 / version code 105 / ARMv7 APK** and its **main.103 OBB** in `ux0:data/wonderboy/import/`. Any filenames work with the `.apk` and `.obb` extensions.
3. Launch Wonder Boy and press **START** to prepare the files. Press **START** again at **Ready to play**.

Allow about **3 GB free before copying the inputs**. APK, OBB, and Android game libraries are not included. Compatibility with files currently delivered by Google Play has not been verified; check the supported files in the README.

### Features

- Physical Vita controls and PlayStation button prompts; both touch panels disabled.
- On-device import with pause/resume, verification, and optional confirmed removal of the APK and OBB afterward.
- Skippable intros, modern/retro graphics and audio switching, and an optional bottom-left FPS counter that starts disabled.
- Frame-pacing improvements and restored central LiveArea artwork.

### Release-candidate status

Gameplay has been tested on a real Vita. Occasional stalls and frame-time spikes remain; a locked 60 FPS throughout the entire game has not been verified. Final clean-install and post-village save/resume checks remain pending.

For updates, install the new VPK over the existing app and preserve `ux0:data/wonderboy/`. There is no automatic updater.

Report problems through [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/Cynostial/wonderboy-vita/issues), including the port version, device/firmware, location, and reproduction steps. Copy `ux0:data/wonderboy/run.log` after closing the app and before launching again.

### Checksum

SHA-256 of `wonderboy-vita-0.35-rc1.zip`:

```text
7e0a3f9e0dedd13d4b439d89106786d7e2567a550f2b1aebecf48bcc0e716699
```

Thanks to Lizardcube, Dotemu, the original Wonder Boy team, and the contributors to VitaSDK, VitaGL, soLoader, kubridge, SDL, and the bundled libraries. See the README and included licenses for credits.

name: Hungry Shark Evolution 01.00
body:
# Hungry Shark Evolution Vita — Version 1.0

The first public release of **Hungry Shark Evolution Vita**, an unofficial native PlayStation Vita port based on the original **Hungry Shark Evolution 6.4.2 (Android build 228)**.

Swim, hunt, evolve, and explore the ocean with adapted PS Vita controls, touchscreen support, original gameplay, audio, and save/load functionality.

### What's included

- Native PlayStation Vita version with original shark gameplay and progression
- Shark selection, evolution menus, and special sharks
- Analog stick, D-pad, button controls, and touchscreen support
- Game audio and save/load functionality
- Custom PS Vita LiveArea presentation, with artwork by [BetterWinds](https://github.com/BetterWinds)
- Windows reconstruction utility to generate your VPK from your own supported Android APK

### Requirements

- A PlayStation Vita able to install VPKs through VitaShell
- **Windows 64-bit** with **.NET Framework 4.8**
- **At least 2 GB of free disk space**
- Your own **unmodified Hungry Shark Evolution 6.4.2 (build 228) APK**

**Required APK SHA-256:**
```text
52b7d8754ab8fec75c3b656a0dc5ec8dc849565adc402487a3ac093f6a481f7a
```

**Required APK size:** `104296014` bytes.

### How to install

1. Download **`HSEVita_v1.0_Windows.zip`** from the Assets section below.
2. Extract **all files** into a writable folder on your Windows PC.
3. Drag your original **6.4.2 (228)** APK onto **`HSERebuild.exe`**, or open the program and select it.
4. Wait for the **`PASS`** message. The tool generates **`HungrySharkEvolutionVita_1.0.vpk`** next to your APK.
5. Transfer the completed VPK to your Vita and install it using **VitaShell**.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Do not install `HSEVita_Stub.vpk`**. It is an incomplete base used by the reconstruction process. Install **only the finished VPK** produced by the utility. Back up your save data before updating or reinstalling.

The download **does not include the original APK or a complete ready-to-install VPK**. You do not need to install Python, Unity, or any SDK.

### PS Vita controls

| Input | Action |
| :-- | :-- |
| Left stick / D-pad | Move your shark and navigate menus |
| Hold **R** | Boost |
| **✕** | Confirm / select |
| **○** | Back / cancel |
| **□** | Missions |
| **△** | Map |
| **START** | Pause / resume |
| Touchscreen | Touch controls and on-screen interactions |

### File verification

**Release ZIP SHA-256:**
```text
89aea8f6747101b0b2bffcdca2bcdfff5d29786d36f63fa7c2867aba05a1821a
```

**Expected reconstructed VPK SHA-256:**
```text
03f752c91d936765c20d9b7494deae319486763f4bf4f4005dbff45353fe2f9b
```

If your APK is rejected, check the exact version and hash. If a component is missing or verification fails, extract the entire ZIP again. The reconstruction tool will not overwrite an existing output VPK.

### Credits

- **Port:** [VegettoSan](https://github.com/VegettoSan)
- **LiveArea artwork:** [BetterWinds](https://github.com/BetterWinds)
- **xdelta3:** [Joshua MacDonald](https://github.com/jmacd/xdelta)

For more information, see the [README](https://github.com/VegettoSan/Hungry-Shark-Evolution-Ps-Vita#readme) or [report an issue](https://github.com/VegettoSan/Hungry-Shark-Evolution-Ps-Vita/issues/new/choose).

*Hungry Shark Evolution and its original content belong to their respective rights holders. This unofficial community port is not affiliated with or endorsed by Ubisoft or the original developers.*
