name: Asphalt 6 - PS Vita Port v0.2.1
body:
# Release Notes

Versioned snapshots of this port's status. Every claim here is backed by a real console
log/crash-dump in [`port_progress.md`](port_progress.md) — nothing in this file is
speculative. See the [README](README.md#-known-issues) for the always-current summary of
known issues; this file is the dated, per-release history.

---

## v0.2.1-beta — 2026-09-26

**Status: Public beta (not yet verified on console).** Fixes a crash when you continue after
winning a race and reduces stutter during races. No data changes are needed.

### Fixed

- Crash when pressing "Next" after winning a race. The pack file for one car doesn't open with
  this game data, and the next race could pick that car as a rival. The game now uses a car
  whose pack loads, and the log names the missing pack.
- Heap overflow in vitaGL when a shader binds more than 16 attribute names.
- Vertex attributes read from the wrong place for some mesh layouts. This could explain some
  flickering or wrong textures on 3D models.
- Shaders that define their own `lerp()` no longer fail to compile.

The last three fixes come from the vitaGL changes in
[9mm-vita](https://github.com/iwannagooutside/vitaGL), which uses the same Glitch engine.

### Performance

- Mutex locks are much cheaper. Each lock used to scan a 1024-entry table under a global lock.
- The sound archive (`file00a.bin`, 143 MB) is opened once instead of on every sound, about
  twice per second in races.
- Large texture re-uploads during races (60–77 ms stutters) are logged, and redundant
  empty re-uploads are skipped.

### Known issues

- Races still run at about 20–30 fps. The engine is CPU-bound.
- The large texture uploads during races aren't fully explained yet. The new `[texup]` log
  lines will show what causes them.

---

## Versioning

This project doesn't follow strict SemVer yet — version numbers track port maturity
(`0.x.y-alpha` while core systems were being stabilized, `0.x.y-beta` now that the game is
playable end to end). A `1.0.0` tag will only be
cut once the known-issues list above is empty and a full race, menu-to-menu, has been
verified glitch-free on real hardware.

name: NFS II SE Recompiled v1.00
body:
# NFS II SE Recompiled v1.00 — PS Vita

The first public release of **NFS II SE Recompiled** brings Need for Speed II: Special Edition to PS Vita as part of **Classic NFS Saga for PS Vita**.

Built on **zaps166's NFSIISE wrapper and C++ game translation**, this adaptation uses **vitaGL** for GPU rendering through the game's Glide interface. Gameplay, controls, installation and the custom LiveArea presentation have been tested on real hardware.

## Included in v1.00

- Single-player racing, menus, sound and video playback.
- A custom launcher with game-language selection, display settings and configurable controls.
- Classic and modern control presets, with separate menu and race mappings.
- Internal resolutions of 320x240, 480x360 and 640x480.
- Original 4:3 or stretched full-screen presentation.
- Optional FPS counter, VSync and CPU/GPU performance profiles.
- Custom bubble, LiveArea and startup artwork.

## Download and install

**Players need both files:**

1. `nfs2se-vita-v1.vpk` — install with VitaShell.
2. `nfs2se-vita-runtime-v1.zip` — extract and copy its `ux0/data/nfs2-recomp` folder into `ux0:data/` on the Vita.

Then copy your own PC **Need for Speed II: Special Edition** `fedata` and `gamedata` folders into:

```text
ux0:data/nfs2-recomp/game/
```

All game-data files and directories must have lowercase names. The standard edition is not supported. The port also requires `ur0:data/libshacccg.suprx`. Original game data and the shader compiler module are not included.

See the repository README for the complete installation guide and data preparation helper. Launch **NFS II SE Recompiled**, choose your settings and press Start or select **Guardar y jugar**. Hold L when opening the app to show the launcher again if hidden. Launcher labels are currently in Spanish; game language is configurable.

## Performance and limitations

Reported performance is approximately **15–50 FPS**, depending on the scene and settings. This release does not guarantee stable 40 or 60 FPS. Improving the slowest scenes is the next NFS II milestone.

Multiplayer is disabled. Full-screen mode stretches the original image; true widescreen, HD texture packs and proportional analog steering are not implemented.

## Source code and contributions

The repository contains editable source files and build instructions so developers can fork, inspect and contribute. `nfs2se-vita-source-v1.zip` provides a versioned source snapshot; players do not need it to install the game. `SHA256SUMS.txt` contains checksums for all three release downloads.

Please preserve upstream credits and applicable licenses. For bug reports, include the track, car, display settings, control profile, reproduction steps and `boot.log` from `ux0:data/nfs2-recomp/`.

## Classic NFS Saga for PS Vita

- **NFS II SE:** first playable release; continued performance and usability work.
- **NFS III: Hot Pursuit:** separate port research and graphics adaptation in progress.
- **NFS IV: High Stakes:** a future investigation after NFS II and III.
- **Porsche Unleashed / Porsche 2000:** a longer-term feasibility goal.

These are development goals, not release-date promises. This package runs NFS II SE only.

## Thanks

Thanks to **zaps166 / Błażej Szczygieł**, **Rinnegatamante and the vitaGL contributors**, **vitaShaRK**, **SceShaccCgExt**, **VitaSDK**, **SDL2**, and everyone whose work makes this port possible. Full upstream links, revisions and license notices are in the repository.

Need for Speed and its original game content belong to their respective owners. This is an unofficial community project, unaffiliated with Electronic Arts or Sony.

name: Dungeon Hunter 2 — PS Vita · v1.1.0
body:
# Dungeon Hunter 2 — PS Vita · v1.1.0 

> Paste the section below into the GitHub release description. The title above goes in the
> release-title field; suggested tag: `v1.1.0`.

---

**All physical buttons now work — movement, attacks, skills, potion, pause and character menu —
and saves/options finally persist across reboots.**

## Physical controls, finished

Every action button now works, including the three that never did: **Circle** (skill 3),
**START** (pause / in-game menu) and **SELECT** (character screen). They were dead on every prior
build even though the previous attempt's synthetic touch events provably reached the engine.

The real cause: the touch layer (`TouchScreenBase`) indexes its slot array as `this + 48 *
pointer_id` **with no bounds check**, and its `clear()` loops exactly 8 times — so only pointer
ids `0..7` are valid. Circle/START/SELECT were assigned ids 7/8/9; the last two wrote past the
array and clobbered the engine's own touch counter, which is why the tap "arrived" in the log but
never did anything. Coordinates were never the problem — the previous synthetic-touch approach had
a structural ceiling.

Fixed by dropping synthetic touch for these three entirely and calling the engine directly instead,
mirroring exactly what its own Flash HUD buttons do (reverse-engineered from the HUD's own
ActionScript bytecode):

- **Circle** → the same `CTRLIsAllowed` → `SG_GetSkillInSlot` → `Cmd_BeginSkill`/`Cmd_EndSkill`
  sequence the skill-3 HUD button makes.
- **START / SELECT** → `MenuBase::FS_PushState("menu_Ingame" / "menu_CharacterMenu")`, and if the
  menu is already open, the same button closes it (`MenuFX::PopAll`) — one press to open, one to
  close.
- **L + R** → new combo, toggles the bottom HUD controls' opacity between 1% (default — play with
  physical buttons, HUD stays out of the way) and 100% (to use them with touch again).

The left stick and D-pad also got a real fix this release: instead of faking a touch drag on the
Flash virtual joystick (which GameSWF's hit-test never reliably accepted), the loader now writes
the engine's own `HUDControls` movement fields directly every frame, the same fields its own touch
handler fills in when a real finger drags the stick. Confirmed on hardware: both D-pad and analog
stick move the character correctly.

## Saves and options now persist (verified on hardware)

Progress, settings and language previously died in RAM: the game played fine in-session but
rebooted to an old save, always in English. Three separate causes, all fixed and confirmed with a
save → reboot → load cycle on a real Vita (Spanish kept, character level and items intact):

- **The port forced English on every boot.** The loader rewrote the saved language to English for
  the first 180 frames of each launch, so changing language could never stick. Now the saved
  language is read once and only reset if out of range.
- **The async save queue was never guaranteed to reach disk.** Player/level saves are queued in
  RAM (`Savegame::saveAll → AddJob`) and drained by fire-and-forget worker threads — and quitting
  with START+SELECT skipped `Application::Quit`, the only synchronous drain, entirely. The queue is
  now also drained on a timer when jobs are pending and unconditionally at exit.
- **Stale read cache.** The file cache never invalidated on write/delete, so a freshly written save
  could still load pre-save bytes in-session. Writes, deletes and renames now invalidate.

## Also fixed

- **Crash on quitting while a sound was playing.** `Application::Quit` stops every sound with a
  0ms fade, which frees its audio objects synchronously on the main thread — racing the engine's
  own audio thread, which was iterating that same list at the same moment. Confirmed from a crash
  dump (prefetch abort through a freed vtable). Level-transition sound stops already used a 500ms
  fade and never crashed, so quit-time stops now take the same safe path; nothing audible changes,
  and level transitions are untouched.
- **A long-standing source of multi-second freezes: every localization file was silently failing
  to load.** Every `text/<zone>.spanish`/`.symbols` lookup this whole project was hitting a
  relative path that resolves under `assets/` on the real device, which holds nothing but the save
  file — the actual files live under `data/text/`, and unlike other asset types, this one had no
  retry-on-failure path anywhere in the engine. A burst of ~12-18 of these misses in the same frame
  window was directly responsible for multi-hundred-millisecond stalls (one measured at 834ms
  average over 60 frames). Now redirected to the correct path on first failure, same pattern
  already used for a couple of other asset types.
- **vitaGL's CPU-only speedhacks are now baked into every build by default** (`MATH_SPEEDHACK`,
  `CIRCULAR_POOL_SPEEDHACK`, `NO_TEX_COMBINER`) — previously only in the opt-in `--hack-safe`
  variant. Confirmed via `nm -D` that this engine imports zero fixed-function GL entry points (100%
  GLSL), so the two math-related flags are free no-ops here and the real, measured win comes from
  `CIRCULAR_POOL_SPEEDHACK`'s vertex-data pooling. The plain `dungeon_hunter_2.vpk` build now
  performs the same as the old `_hack_safe` variant; `--hack-safe` is kept only for compatibility.
- Log files are now `.log` instead of `.txt`.

## Performance: 5-6 FPS → ~20-25 FPS in gameplay, ~60 in menus

This is unchanged since the last notes and remains the honest headline: sustained combat is
~20-25 FPS (up from 5-6), menus and light scenes reach ~60. **The GPU was never the bottleneck** —
`eglSwapBuffers` costs ~0.2ms per frame throughout, while CPU-side work (the engine tick) was
120-185ms. Two independent resolution-reduction tests changed combat FPS *not at all*, ruling out
fill-rate directly rather than assuming it. See `PORTING_PLAN.md` Phase 23 for the full write-up.

## Known issues

- **Framerate is ~20-25 FPS in gameplay, not 60.** The dominant remaining cost is understood but
  not fixed: the engine's real frustum culling has to stay bypassed (see below), so it animates and
  updates the *entire level* every frame regardless of the camera.
- **The engine's frustum culling is bypassed.** This is what makes enemies render reliably, but
  it's also the main remaining performance waste. Naively re-enabling it (`--culling-test 2`)
  measured *slower* and brings back the invisible-enemy bug, so the real fix is the stale bounding
  box (or a second, object-level visibility gate — see `PORTING_PLAN.md`) that made the bypass
  necessary in the first place.
- **Some enemies still render invisible** (health bar and aggro ring show, no model). The opacity
  hypothesis has been ruled out with hard evidence (52/52 sampled enemies at full opacity); the
  current leads are all culling-related.
- The repeating HUD icon column is still unresolved.

## Installing

You need to **legally own Dungeon Hunter 2 HD for Android.** This repository and this release contain
**no** Gameloft assets, APK, or `.so` binaries — only the loader/bridge. You supply the game data
yourself.

1. Install [taiHEN](https://github.com/yifanlu/taiHEN)'s `kubridge.skprx`, and place Sony's
   `libshacccg.suprx` under `ur0:data/` (obtained separately — it is Sony's binary and is not
   redistributed here).
2. Install the `.vpk`.
3. Stage the game's asset files as loose files under `ux0:data/dungeon-hunter-2/`. See
   `PORTING_PLAN.md` Phase 8 for the exact layout the asset bridge expects.

## For contributors

`PORTING_PLAN.md` documents every hypothesis tried for the open issues above, what was ruled out
and how, and exactly which diagnostic hooks are already wired up and waiting for a fresh hardware
log. If you have a physical Vita and want to help, that's the place to start.

## Credits

Built on [SoLoBoP](https://github.com/v-atamanenko) (Andy Nguyen, Rinnegatamante, Volodymyr
Atamanenko) and [FalsoJNI](https://github.com/v-atamanenko/FalsoJNI), rendering through
[vitaGL](https://github.com/Rinnegatamante/vitaGL) built from source. Particular thanks to the
**Asphalt-5-Vita** and **Asphalt-6-Vita** ports, whose own performance write-ups pointed directly
at several of the fixes in this and the previous release — they are the closest comparable ports
and their notes were worth more than any amount of guessing.

Dungeon Hunter 2 is © Gameloft. This is an unofficial, non-commercial fan port, not affiliated with
or endorsed by Gameloft. The loader/bridge source in this repository is MIT licensed; that covers

name: v1.01-release
body:
# Bully Vita v1.01

The first release since the 2021 port, and the first with a version number that was chosen rather than defaulted. LiveArea shows **01.01**.

Everything below was measured on hardware. The headline figure: a **13-hour session** with 4,869 textures evicted and restored, zero lost, zero corrupted, no allocation ever refused, and no crash.

## The crash after long sessions is fixed

The original port crashed after an hour or two of play. It was three separate leaks, none of them in the game's own logic:

- **vitaGL was quietly taking the game's heap for textures.** Its allocator falls back to the game's own memory once video memory is full, and reports that memory as zero to anything asking how much is left. The heap climbed to 155 MB while every reading said there was room to spare. That fallback is now off, so texture pressure shows up where the loader can act on it.
- **The streamer never freed anything.** `CStreaming::IsThereEnoughFreeMemory` compared the request against a hardcoded 10 MB and said yes to everything — fine on a phone with gigabytes spare, fatal here. It now sees the real heap, so streamed models and textures are released when memory gets tight, through the game's own machinery that was never being asked.
- **Every vertex buffer kept a full CPU-side copy of its mesh forever.** 33 MB by the end of a session, never falling once. Those copies are released once the data is on the GPU and put back if the game locks the buffer again.

On top of that, the loader runs a **texture cache**: once textures no longer fit in video memory, the ones the game has stopped drawing with are dropped and brought back the moment they're needed. A dropped texture is never lost — its bytes are parked in RAM or written to `ux0:data/Bully/textures`, and the store survives between runs so revisiting an area costs nothing. The cache refuses to drop anything it cannot put back.

## It renders on current vitaGL

The port was released against a 2021 vitaGL that renders nothing on current firmware. Moving it forward exposed two problems that each produced a black screen with no error:

- **The viewport was being corrupted at build time.** vitaGL's `SOFTFP_ABI` option double-moved the viewport arguments on this port's softfp toolchain, so every primitive — including the clear — was clipped away. A fifteen-line program that only cleared the screen red came out black. The option is not used.
- **Shaders are compiled at runtime now**, the way gtasa_vita does it, instead of loading precompiled `.gxp` files that current vitaGL silently misparses. **This makes `libshacccg.suprx` a requirement.**

MSAA is 2x rather than the original 4x: the traces showed CDRAM with no free headroom at all.

## An audio crash before the first frame

Building OpenAL with a current compiler surfaced a latent alignment fault in openal-soft: a 16-byte-aligned store to a stack slot that the ABI only guarantees 8-byte alignment for. The 2021 binary survived by luck of frame layout. openal-soft is now built from source, pinned, with the offending alignment lowered so the store is one the stack always satisfies.

## Memory returned to the game

The original held two 16 MB FIOS RAM caches in front of a file API the game never reads through. Measured across two sessions on the same route, the run without them was slightly faster per megabyte and ended 35 MB lower on the heap. They're gone.

## Threads

The game's main thread has a core to itself. It previously shared core 0 at equal priority with the display queue — the thread that presents finished frames — which cannot be moved. So the game moved instead.

## Loader safety

- A recursive lock serialises everything the loader does to vitaGL. Without it, an eviction's `glBindTexture` could land between the game's own bind and upload and free a buffer the game was writing into — a heap corruption that took nine hours to surface and was traced from a core dump.
- Functions the loader hooks are checked before hooking: the prologue must relocate cleanly and the function must take four or fewer argument words. Anything that fails is left alone and named in the log rather than guessed at.
- A texture that can't be safely restored is never dropped. Freeing one you can't put back is how the ground and the buildings went black in earlier builds.

## Requirements

- `libshacccg.suprx` installed — new; shaders compile at runtime
- Space on `ux0:` for `ux0:data/Bully/textures`; with too little free the loader runs without the card tier and keeps every texture resident, which is the original behaviour

## Building

The original no longer compiles against a current VitaSDK. This release builds against current VitaSDK, vitaGL, vitaShaRK and openal-soft, each pinned by revision in the CI workflow, and CI builds the VPK on every push.

## Known limits

Two things this release does not fix, stated plainly so the word "fixed" above doesn't hide them:

- **Frame rate.** The game runs its own limiter at roughly 28 fps and drops to around 21 in crowded areas. Both were measured to the millisecond. The crowd cost is per-pedestrian AI on one core, and the engine's world update is built around global state that cannot be split across cores. This is what the engine does on this hardware.
- **Area transitions.** Loading a new area takes around 13 seconds, 91% of which is memory-card I/O — the game reopens its two archive files thousands of times per load. Measured, not yet addressed.

# Golden Balloon 1.7.2

*Released 2026-09-17.*

## PS Vita

- Retains the committed gameplay-jingle ownership fix: spatial ambience must
  not stop silver-coin or key ditties. Normal audio and silver-coin pickup
  jingles were confirmed on real Vita hardware using the reverted working
  baseline for this release. The unsuccessful experimental audio rewrites are
  not included.
- Uses native 960x544 rendering with 2x anisotropic filtering in Restored and
  Remastered. The Vita backend enforces an effective 1x render scale.
- Skips the unsupported RemasterFX output post-processing shader before
  compilation, avoiding the shader-compiler failure that affected subsequent
  shaders. Incompatible RL-5 per-pixel lighting remains disabled. Restored is
  recommended; the full desktop Remastered effects are not available on Vita.
- Adds Vita Rice/GLideN64 pack discovery, an in-game pack toggle, and ZIP
  extraction with a visible progress screen and Vita-compatible directory
  installation.
- Loads Rice replacements asynchronously when decode helpers are available.
  Adds `tools/ricepack/vita_optimize_pack.py` and `.vtex` loading for RGBA8
  textures with prebuilt mip chains. Converted packs must be supplied by the
  user and are not included in the VPK.
- Excludes the uncommitted per-scene texture-preload work and its related cache
  changes. That WIP remains local pending HD-pack/audio testing. Ordinary
  on-demand async texture loading is retained. **Texture pop-in remains a
  known issue**, and audio performance with heavy enabled packs has not been
  separately qualified.
- Includes opt-in Vita profiler/DebugNet lifecycle and renderer/texture metrics
  for development. The published VPK is built with both debugger and profiler
  disabled.

The audio implementation is unchanged from the hardware-confirmed baseline.
Runtime code is taken from committed `ec64a161`, without the local preload WIP;
the release adds version and documentation updates only. The earlier full
Adventure completion remains evidence for the Restored baseline, not a newly
completed 1.7.2 playthrough. If a heavy pack causes audio or frame-time problems,
disable the pack when troubleshooting.

Install `GoldenBalloon-Vita-v1.7.2.vpk` over the existing `GBLN00001` application.
Back up saves and retain `ux0:data/goldenballoon/`, including your own ROM and
optional packs. The VPK includes the 98-trophy pack and LiveArea artwork, but
no ROM or gameplay assets. NoTrpDrm remains optional for trophies.

The compiled version and Vita package metadata use `MDKR_VERSION` `1.7.2`
and `APP_VER` `01.72`. Source is tagged `v1.7.2` on the `optimization` branch.

name: ViTube v2.0
body:
## ViTube 2.0 — hardware decoder no longer needs a system-wide plugin

**Fixes #2 and #5** (VitaDB and Green Vita crashing after ViTube): ViTube
bundled `reAvPlayer.suprx` (SonicMastr's ReAvPlayer), a taiHEN plugin that
patched five syscall stubs inside `SceAvcodecUser`, a module every process
on the console shares. When ViTube was closed from the LiveArea, the
process was killed and the plugin's cleanup never ran, so the patches stayed
in place and crashed the next app that touched the hardware H.264 decoder —
until the console was rebooted.

The plugin is gone. The decoder now calls `sceAvcdecDecodeAuInternal` and
`sceAvcdecDecodeGetPictureWithWorkPictureInternal` directly — the same pair
the plugin's hook used to redirect to — so nothing outside ViTube's own
process is touched anymore.

**If you're updating from 1.2 or earlier**, reboot the console once after
installing. ViTube 2.0 itself doesn't need it, but a hook left behind by an
older ViTube session survives until the next reboot regardless of which
version replaces it.

No changes to playback quality, sign-in or networking. Saved settings stay
valid.

### Install
Download `ViTube.vpk` and install it with VitaShell (requires HENkaku/Ensō).
Existing installs are updated in place. The corresponding source for this
build (GPL-3.0 §6) is this repository at tag `v2.0`.

name: Asphalt 8 Vita v0.3
body:
# Asphalt 8 Vita v0.3

This update improves race loading, reduces shader-related pauses and adds
further stability and compatibility fixes.
Your existing game files, saves and settings remain compatible.

### Improvements

- **Fewer shader-related pauses.** Bundled shader programs cover shared track
  and vehicle effects from their first use, with broader coverage for equivalent
  variants used throughout the game.
- **More reliable shader reuse.** Fixed a cache-length issue that could cause a
  complete cached program to be rejected and compiled again.
- **Faster race loading.** Race loading shares the OBB directory data
  between active scans instead of repeatedly reading the same large directory.
- **Loading recovery.** Added targeted recovery for a stalled loading stage
  that could prevent the game from finishing a load after time spent idle.
- **Audio compatibility.** Improved PCM sample-rate handling and read-only Vox
  state queries, avoiding unnecessary waits in those queries.
- **Further session-stability fixes.** Improved cleanup of the game's thread
  synchronization objects when their memory is freed, and synchronized shader
  program deletion with outstanding GPU work.
- **Broader shader compatibility.** Improved handling of shaders that exceed
  the usual varying slots, plus validation and serialization of cached programs.
- **Clearer setup errors.** An APK size mismatch now names the supported
  v2.0.0e APK instead of referring to an internal development build.
- **Updated presentation.** Includes the new bubble icon and LiveArea artwork.
- **Easier Windows setup.** File pickers and a guided USB or PC-folder option
  handle file preparation and verification. FTP remains available.

The update retains traffic, breakables, collision behavior, car damage,
particles and the existing graphics presets.

The recurring in-race pauses improved in Tokyo, Iceland and Nevada testing.
Bundled programs cover their matching effects on first use, including the
first run of a new installation. Effects outside that coverage still use the
normal shader compiler; this is not a promise of hitch-free play on every track.

### Updating

Install the new VPK over your existing installation. Keep your game-data folder
and saves; there is no need to copy the APK/OBB again or clear the shader cache.

### Known issues

- The pause when finishing a race remains
- Heavy scenes can still slow down; 60 FPS and hitch-free play are not guaranteed
- Premium-currency cars, car packs, online services and gyro steering remain
  unavailable
- Only the exact supported Android v2.0.0e game files are supported

## Downloads

- **[Install package](https://gitlab.com/sexcurrybeats/asphalt8-vita/-/releases/v0.3/downloads/Asphalt8Vita_v0.3.zip)** — playable VPK, guided Windows setup, and instructions.
- [Source ZIP](https://gitlab.com/sexcurrybeats/asphalt8-vita/-/releases/v0.3/downloads/asphalt8-vita-v0.3-source.zip) — source snapshot with its integrity manifest. Building is optional.
- [SHA-256 checksums](https://gitlab.com/sexcurrybeats/asphalt8-vita/-/releases/v0.3/downloads/SHA256SUMS.txt).

Supply your own exact supported v2.0.0e APK and OBB. See [installation instructions](https://gitlab.com/sexcurrybeats/asphalt8-vita/-/blob/v0.3/docs/INSTALL.md), [compatibility](https://gitlab.com/sexcurrybeats/asphalt8-vita/-/blob/v0.3/docs/COMPATIBILITY.md), and [shader provenance](https://gitlab.com/sexcurrybeats/asphalt8-vita/-/blob/v0.3/docs/SHADER_PROVENANCE.md).

name: Skyrift v1.3.0 — sharper claws, deeper story
body:
**Skyrift v1.3.0** — by Onur Kuru. Bug fixes, real difficulty, story beats, and a full visual pass.

Download **`skyrift.vpk`** below and install with VitaShell (X → Install).
Requires a homebrew-enabled Vita. Desktop players can build from source
(see the README).

### Fixed
- Void-fall "penalty" used to heal instead of hurt (subtracted 1 AFTER a
  full heal) - it's now capped at the HP you actually fell with, never a
  free heal, still never lethal
- Stomp now always one-shots non-boss enemies - isle 6+ eagles at 4 HP
  (breed bonus) used to survive a stomp, breaking the taught "land on foes
  to squash them" rule
- Fixed a frog telegraph animation desync on late isles, a three-part
  lightning lifecycle bug (bolts during death fades, frozen through
  hit-stop, popping across pause), and sparse weather at isle start
- weather/difficulty tables moved into the generated level config instead
  of hard-coded level indices in the engine - reordering isles can no
  longer silently misattach them

### New: difficulty & reward
- Rift-touched eagles (isles 9-10) telegraph a dive attack: a hover-flash
  warning, then a fast dive at wherever you're standing
- **FLAWLESS bonus**: clear an isle with every gem and zero damage for
  +500 score - now tracked live in the HUD, not just revealed at the door

### New: story
- A short lore beat between each of isles 2-10, setting up what's ahead

### New: visuals

body:
# VagaChatVITA Alpha 0.1.0

Primera versión alpha pública de VagaChatVITA para PlayStation Vita.

## Novedades

- Chat compatible con APIs OpenAI mediante `chat/completions`.
- Respuestas progresivas por streaming.
- Historial local de conversaciones.
- Biblioteca de juegos instalados en la Vita.
- Chats contextuales por juego con sugerencias automáticas.
- Preguntas rápidas seleccionables con pantalla táctil y botones:
  - `ARRIBA/ABAJO` para navegar.
  - `IZQUIERDA/DERECHA` para cambiar de pregunta.
  - `CRUZ` para enviar.
- Renderizado Markdown básico en las respuestas.
- Interfaz disponible en español, inglés e italiano.
- Configuración web local desde Ajustes.
- Servidor web protegido por contraseña.
- API key oculta en la interfaz y sin guardarse en texto plano.
- Iconos y recursos LiveArea incluidos.
- Paquete VPK listo para VitaShell.

## Instalación

1. Descargar `VagaChatVITA.vpk`.
2. Copiarlo a la Vita mediante USB o FTP.
3. Instalarlo desde VitaShell.
4. Abrir `VagaRoute AI` desde el LiveArea.
5. Configurar el endpoint y la API key desde Ajustes o Configuración web.

## Notas

- La Vita y el PC o teléfono deben estar conectados a la misma red Wi-Fi para usar la configuración web.
- El servidor web utiliza HTTP local y debe usarse únicamente en una red de confianza.
- Esta versión es alpha y puede contener errores.
- Se recomienda realizar copias de seguridad de `ux0:data/VagaRouteAI/`.

name: Barony Vita v0.0.2-5.0.2
body:
# Barony Vita v0.0.2

Online multiplayer, a global leaderboard, achievements, and a batch of fixes.

## Online multiplayer
- Host or join games over the internet through the community master server, with
  automatic NAT traversal and a relay fallback when a direct connection fails.
- Local ad-hoc play, and LAN over Wi-Fi, no router or internet needed.
- Set a room password when hosting.
- In-progress online games are saved for the next time your party plays together.

## Global leaderboard
- A worldwide board tied to your console, username set via settings page.
- Your best run is submitted when you open the board, whether it came from
  single-player, an online game, or a save you are still playing.
- Shows the top 20, and adds your own row at the bottom with your real rank
  when you are not in the top 20.
- Every entry carries the full run: class, stats, cause of death, and the
  character's gear.

## Online account
- Your online identity and leaderboard progress live in one key file on the
  console: ux0:data/Barony/config/gossip_id.json.
- Updating the game keeps it. Installing a newer VPK over your current install
  does not touch ux0:data/Barony, so your account, saves, and leaderboard entry
  all carry over.
- Deleting that file, or wiping the game's save data, permanently unlinks your
  online account and its leaderboard entry. It cannot be recovered.
- A fresh account is created automatically the next time you launch, and you
  set your name again. Reusing your old name may show as name#2, since the
  orphaned entry still holds the original.

## Achievements
- Achievements now track and unlock during play, saved on the console and online.

## Fixes
- Lighting: removed the rainbow specks along shadow edges, lifted
  pitch-black shadows so you can see in the dark (gamma slider), and smoothed the fade-to-black
  banding.
- Enemies roam, infight, and give chase again instead of freezing at a distance.
  This also fixes bosses appearing without their body parts.
- Torches and flames no longer drift or jitter.
- Digging or breaking a wall no longer leaves a see-through gap.
- Better handling when the console sleeps and wakes during a game.
- Stability fixes across the math and lighting code.

## Install
- Download barony-blank.vpk and install it with VitaShell.
- Barony's game files are not redistributable, so generate your own data from a
  PC copy and copy it to ux0:data/Barony on the Vita. See the README for the
  one-step tool.
- Cross-play with PC is not supported. Play Vita to Vita.

Built from Barony 5.0.2. GPLv3.

body:
Hi everyone! Big update here, since I got my SD2Vita I have been doing a lot of optimization.
I bumped the resolution of the Vita port to 480x272, so it is just a little bit more clearer, the HUD will always be Native resolution, so it doesn't become blurry.
I added a optimizer, that let's you cache the textures before hand, which improves loading times substantially, this can be skipped, and only needs to be done once!
I have made a lot of optimizations with the frame rate, and stutters. I will admit that the game is not smooth 30fps all the way through, but it is much better than it was at last release! Notable, audio, like the thunder, doesn't freeze the game for a good second, which you would notice right away at the start of the game, that is NO MORE.
There is still quite a bit of work that could be done, and I wouldn't mind if anyone would like to contribute, feel free to make pull requests. I also added a updater for the Vita, which should check on startup if you have internet, if there is a new update, you can skip it if you like, it might need more testing and refining though.

QoL improvement, I have added Hint sizes, I noticed while testing a bit, I felt the hints could be a bit hard to read at it's original size, so I have added Hint sizes, this can be changed in the gameplay options, for the Vita it's default on Medium.

I have also made the port more accessible on Android, no longer requiring Vulkan 1.3, should work on Android devices that support Vulkan 1.1+

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/FridiNaTor1/HPL2-handyman/compare/1.3...1.5

Planned features:
Controller detection for Android and PC, where the controller glyphs change depending on which type of Controller you are using, automatically, and getting rid of Controller hints when you are using Keyboard and Mouse only!
Improving the Vita control scheme, there is a part of the game where you should be using the directional button to do a puzzle, which is currently mapped incorrectly, sorry!
Improving the Android control scheme, and make it aware of desktop mode, as in when you connect the phone to a TV, the game should take advantage of that, and remove the touch only control scheme, and be able to be played with Mouse and Keyboard, or a Controller.
Better options for every platform, like keybinds/sensitivity, etc.

Known Issues:
Android stutters, this will be looked into!
Vita unstable FPS, yeah obviously, but it's a bit better now atleast!
Android running is awkward, I'll try to make it better!
Vita's inventory, pause menu, and journal, doesn't fade the background.

# Changelog

All notable changes to vitastremio (PS Vita Stremio client + middleware).

## [1.3] - 2026-08-27

**Update both halves.** Reinstall the VPK *and* restart the middleware.

### Fixed

**Sound and picture drifting apart after about 35 minutes.** Long films would
play perfectly and then, always at roughly the same point, the picture would
jump ahead of the sound and never settle again. The app was losing track of
time once playback passed 35 minutes and 47 seconds, which is why it happened
at the same moment every time. It now keeps time correctly for far longer
than any film.

### Added

**A proper loading screen.** Starting something used to show a black screen
while it buffered, which was hard to tell apart from the app having frozen.
You now get the film's artwork, its title, and a spinner while it gets ready.

### Worth knowing

- Artwork comes from your addons, so titles without it will show the title on
  a plain background instead. Nothing else changes.

# FileManager Vita v0.6.2 This release focuses on stability, touch input and visual refinements. ## Highlights - Added two color themes: **Dark**, with a black and dark-gray palette, and **Pink**, with hot-pink and light tones. - Refined **Grid view** with the standard font size, centered file/folder names and width-aware ellipsis for long names. - The dedicated **Icons** set is now always active and its redundant selector was removed from Settings. - Added Wi-Fi and Bluetooth status icons. They are shown only when the corresponding connection/feature is active. - Added touch input to controls that previously only displayed a button hint, including the **OK** button in file properties. - Single-item copy, move and delete dialogs now show the selected file/folder name; multi-item actions retain the compact count summary. ## Stability fixes - Limited and periodically cleaned the Recent directory, removing stale entries to prevent excessive directory growth. - Added a five-second directory-read safeguard that returns to the default root when a directory stalls. - Fixed IME lifecycle and buffer handling issues that could crash rename/input operations. - Hardened VPK installation and progress-thread synchronization to prevent stalls around extraction and promotion. - Removed the GIF background from the VPK after identifying excessive decoded-frame memory use as a potential source of freezes during installation. - Fixed invalid touch routing while modal dialogs are open and other crash-prone edge cases found in collected logs. ## Installation Copy `FileManager_v0.6.2.vpk` to your PS Vita and install it with VitaShell or another VPK installer. name: Immortal Dusk — PS Vita Port v1.0
body:
# ⚔️ Immortal Dusk — PS Vita Port v1.0

First official release of **Immortal Dusk** for the PlayStation Vita and PlayStation TV!

This port brings Gamevil's classic action RPG to the PS Vita natively via dynamic ARM shared library loading (`.so loader`), `FalsoJNI`, and `vitaGL` hardware scaling.

---

## ✨ Features & Highlights

- **🚀 Native 60 FPS Performance:** Internal 800x480 RGB565 software rasterizer hardware-scaled to full screen (**960x544**) with bilinear filtering via `vitaGL`.
- **🎮 Full Physical & Touch Controls:** Complete dual-input support:
  - 8-direction movement via **Left Analog Stick** and **D-Pad**.
  - Face buttons and triggers mapped for fast combat, skills, and item shortcuts.
  - Full **Front Touchscreen** support for menus, inventory, and HUD navigation.
- **🔊 Low-Latency Multi-Voice Audio Engine:** Powered by `sceAudioOut`, supporting 12-voice polyphonic WAV PCM sound effects and memory-streamed looping MP3 background music (`minimp3`).
- **💎 Offline Cash Shop & K-Point Emulation:** Built-in local simulation of Gamevil's legacy server protocol, preventing infinite loading hangs and allowing purchases of potions, resurrection stones, teleport scrolls, and bag/storage expansions completely offline.
- **🖼️ High-Quality LiveArea:** Custom icon, startup gate, and background remastered with 8-bit indexed palettes matching PS Vita OS standards.

---

## 🕹️ Controls

| PS Vita Button | In-Game Action |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Left Stick / D-Pad** | 8-Direction Character Movement |
| **Cross ($\times$)** | Primary Attack / Talk / Confirm |
| **Square ($\square$)** | Skill 1 |
| **Triangle ($\triangle$)** | Skill 2 |
| **Circle ($\bigcirc$)** | Skill 3 / Cancel / Back |
| **R1 Trigger** | Skill 4 |
| **L1 Trigger** | Quick HP Potion |
| **SELECT** | Quick MP Potion |
| **START** | In-Game Menu / Pause |
| **Front Touchscreen** | Direct touch interaction across menus, inventory, and HUD |

---

## 📦 Requirements & Installation Guide

> **Legal Disclaimer:** This release only provides the loader executable (`.vpk`). No copyrighted assets or proprietary binaries are included. You must supply files from a legally acquired copy of **Immortal Dusk v1.0.2** for Android.

### 1. Prerequisites on your PS Vita
Ensure you have the following plugins installed:
- [kubridge.skprx](https://github.com/TheOfficialFloW/kubridge/releases)
- [fd_fix.skprx](https://github.com/TheOfficialFloW/FdFix/releases) (or rePatch)
- `libshacccg.suprx` (installed in `ur0:data/` via *ShaRKBR3ED* or *CrystalPSM*)

---

### 2. Setup Steps
1. Download and install **`immortal_dusk.vpk`** on your PS Vita using **VitaShell**.
2. Obtain your legal **`Immortal Dusk_1.0.2.apk`** file and rename/extract it as a `.zip` archive.
3. Extract and copy the following files to `ux0:data/immortaldusk/`:
   - Copy `lib/armeabi/libaist-jni.so` $\to$ `ux0:data/immortaldusk/libaist-jni.so`

name: Cordless v1.0.0
body:
# Cordless 1.0.0

A native Discord client for the PlayStation Vita. It talks straight to Discord over TLS, so there's no bridge server and nothing to self-host.

## Features
- Servers, DMs, group DMs, and threads
- Send, edit, reply, react, and forward; scroll up to load history
- Images, GIFs, WebP, and video / voice-message playback
- Emoji, live presence, typing indicators, friends, and profile popouts
- Join by invite, block users, and multiple accounts
- Settings: light/dark theme, accent color, font size, compact mode, 12/24h clock, and a low-battery mode

Voice channels are still a work in progress and are turned off in this build.

## Logging in
No password either way. Two options:

- QR code: scan the on-screen code with the official Discord mobile app. It's the quick path, but Discord sometimes asks for a captcha during QR sign-in that the Vita can't complete. If that happens, use the token method.
- Token: put your Discord user token on the card once. The full walkthrough (a one-click bookmarklet, the browser Network tab, or by hand) is in docs/login.md. (https://github.com/Brendonm17/Cordless/blob/main/docs/login.md)

## Terms of service
Using a user token with a third-party client is against Discord's Terms of Service. Cordless is built for personal use and interoperability, not automation, and you run it on your own account at your own risk. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Discord or Sony.

AI was used for API research and live area assets.

## Install
1. A Vita or PS TV on HENkaku / h-encore2 (firmware 3.60 to 3.74) with unsafe homebrew enabled.
2. Copy Cordless.vpk to the Vita and install it in VitaShell.
3. Launch it, then follow docs/login.md to add your token.

Logs are written to ux0:data/cordless/log.txt.

name: VitaBrightEX v1.3 + LUT Editor v4.2
body:
## VitaBrightEX v1.3 + LUT Editor v4.2

### Critical fixes in this release

**OLED: presets no longer destroy screen colours**

The previous OLED screen filter applied CCT/gamma/contrast math directly
to the panel's 21-byte LUT rows. Those bytes are panel hardware control
registers — not linear RGB pixel values. Applying a colour matrix to them
produced wrong results and made every single preset look worse than the
default. This is now fully fixed.

The OLED LUT is left completely untouched by the filter system. Your
screen colour is set by the calibrated per-panel LUT file
(vitabright_lut_p5.txt etc.) loaded at boot — which already has the
correct white-point for your specific panel. Factory reset restores
this clean state instantly.

**Tab switching now works reliably**

The app was using sceCtrlPeekBufferPositiveExt2 which remaps the
physical L/R shoulder buttons to different bit positions (L1/R1 DS4
style) that the code wasn't reading. Fixed: uses plain
sceCtrlPeekBufferPositive so the physical L/R buttons correctly
switch tabs.

---

### What each part now does

**Plugin v1.3**
- OLED colour is controlled by the per-panel LUT file only
- Filter math (CCT/gamma/contrast) is NOT applied to OLED — it was
  the wrong architecture and destroyed calibration
- Hardware invert (sceDisplaySetInvertColorsForDriver) still works
- LCD filter (IFTU CSC matrix) unchanged — works correctly

**App v4.2 on Vita 1000 (OLED):**
- Tab 1: Invert toggle + Factory reset — the only safe options
- Tab 2: Invert only, with explanation of why CCT/gamma/contrast
  are not shown (to prevent accidentally breaking colours)

**App v4.2 on Vita 2000 (LCD):**
- Tab 1: Full CCT preset list (6500K–1200K) + IPS/sRGB/Night/Boost
  enhancements — correct because IFTU CSC applies to pixel data
- Tab 2: Temperature / Gamma / Contrast / Brightness / Invert sliders

**Factory reset (Triangle):** Calls vitabrightOledReload() to restore
the clean panel LUT from the panel-specific file on disk, then clears
invert. Restores original colours immediately without a reboot.

---

### Installation
1. Extract VitaBrightEX-v1.3.zip and copy all files to ur0:/tai/
2. Add ur0:/tai/vitabright.skprx under *KERNEL in ur0:/tai/config.txt
3. Reboot
4. Install VitaBrightEX-LUT-Editor-v4.2.vpk via VitaShell

If ux0:/tai/ exists on your memory card it takes priority over ur0:/tai/.

---

Based on vitabright by devnoname120 (https://github.com/devnoname120/vitabright).
Screen filter inspired by Luma3DS Rosalina (https://github.com/LumaTeam/Luma3DS).

name: MCSM Vita 1.11 — Public Prerelease
body:
## MCSM 1.11 — public prerelease

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **This is a fix pass, not a confirmed-working pass.** Everything below was
> traced from code, disassembly, or a device `loader.log` and fixed on that
> basis — none of it has been confirmed by a full playthrough yet. In
> particular, this release does **not** claim choices or settings now save
> correctly; it describes the specific mechanisms that were found broken and
> what changed. If a problem persists, the logging build exists to find out
> why instead of guessing again.
>
> **The VPK on this release is a LOGGING build (`MCSM-1.11-logging.vpk`).**
> It writes a diagnostic log to `ux0:data/mcsm/loader.log` while you play,
> and it runs slower than a normal build because of it — please don't report
> its framerate as a performance bug. A non-logging build
> (`MCSM-1.11.vpk`) is also attached.
>
> ### How to send a log
>
> 1. Play until the problem happens.
> 2. Close the game. If it is frozen: press **PS**, then close it from the LiveArea.
> 3. **Do not launch the game again yet** — the log is wiped at the start of every
>    launch, so relaunching destroys what you just captured.
> 4. Copy `ux0:data/mcsm/loader.log` off the Vita — open VitaShell, press **SELECT**
>    to start its FTP server, and copy the file from a PC.
> 5. Attach it to a [bug report](../../issues/new?template=bug-report.yml) or post it
>    in the [Discord](https://discord.gg/spjFgQUGmE). Zip it if it is large.
>
> To turn logging off without changing builds, create an empty
> `ux0:data/mcsm/settings/nolog.txt`.

> **Use Data Builder v1.9** (unchanged from 1.10 — same file, reused as-is).

This release contains the PS Vita loader with community LiveArea artwork and trophy support, the Windows data builder, and the corresponding source code. It does **not** contain the Android APK, OBBs, episodes, native game libraries, or gameplay archives.

Questions, test results, and bug reports are welcome in the [MCSM Vita Discord](https://discord.gg/spjFgQUGmE).

### Downloads

- **MCSM-1.11-logging.vpk** — complete Vita loader, **logging build** (see the box above); install with VitaShell.
- **MCSM-1.11.vpk** — the same loader without logging, for normal play once a problem is no longer being chased.
- **MCSM-Vita-Data-Builder-v1.9.exe** — unchanged from 1.10; builds `ux0:data/mcsm` or a chapter-only copy pack from your legally owned Android files.

### What changed in this pass

- **Preference load ran before its resource could exist.** `SavePrefs` was writing correctly the whole time; the load that reads it back now retries once the resource it needs is actually registered, instead of only trying once, too early, at boot.
- **Found and fixed a real bug in the shipped engine's event log**, not a porting artifact: on a missing anchor event, `DeleteAllEventsAfterEvent` underflows to a full-log wipe instead of doing nothing. `SaveLoad_Load` calls the vulnerable path on every load; it's now guarded against exactly that case.
- **The post-save mirror was guessing which copy the engine wrote, and guessed wrong** — from the second save onward it silently overwrote every save with the first one's contents. It now checks which copy actually changed instead of assuming.
- Save writes are now staged and size-verified before being committed by rename, and a one-generation backup restores a save that's provably too small to be intact.
- **Audio mixer was writing into a buffer the hardware was still playing**, audible as tearing in busy scenes with several NPCs on screen; it now rotates through buffers that were already allocated but unused.
- **The virtual controller could be dropped by the system around common dialogs** (trophy setup, the rename keyboard) and never came back, leaving only touch controls; it's now checked and re-added automatically.
- **The 30fps cap allowed a fast frame through right after a slow one**; presents are now floored against the actual previous present so the display can't exceed the configured cap.
- **An animation-timing repair forced a quarter-second jump on every scene load**, not just on the hitches it was meant to smooth; it now treats a load as a pause (nothing to catch up to) rather than lost time.
- The save-rename on-screen keyboard could show leftover characters from a previous rename on top of the new one; its input buffer is now cleared between uses.
- New LiveArea icon and content-screen artwork.

### Data Builder v1.9

Unchanged from the 1.10 release.

name: SRB2Kart for PS Vita / PS TV — v2.1 (DualShock rumble)
body:
**Rumble.** A DualShock 3/4 plugged into a PS TV has motors — the port now uses them.

| Event | Feel |
|---|---|
| Bumping another kart | short thump |
| Spinout (banana, orbinaut…) | medium shake |
| Squish (Grow/Shrink) | heavier |
| Explosion (mine, SPB, Eggman) | full strength |
| Boost / sneaker | 2 s of high-frequency buzz |
| Offroad (grass, sand, mud) | continuous grind, scaled by how deep the offroad is and how fast you are actually ploughing through it |

Set it in **Options → Controls → Gamepad Options → Rumble** — `Off` / `Light` / `Normal` / `Strong` (default: Normal).

Splitscreen rumbles the right controller: SDL's Vita backend maps each pad to its own port. On a **handheld Vita** there are no motors, so the feature is simply inert — nothing to turn off, nothing to break. It cannot desync online play either: the rumble code only ever *reads* player state.

---

## Which VPK do I download?

| | **`srb2kart-modern-vitagl.vpk`** | **`srb2kart-2019-vitagl.vpk`** |
|---|---|---|
| **Rumble** | ✅ **new in v2.1** | ❌ (unchanged from v2.0) |
| vitaGL | latest upstream | the 2019 version (`srb2-vita`) |
| Change resolution | live, no restart | requires a restart |
| Extra file on the console | **yes** — `libshacccg.suprx` | none |
| Source branch | [`vitagl-modern`](https://github.com/Esodland/SRB2Kart-PSVita-PSTV/tree/vitagl-modern) *(default)* | [`master`](https://github.com/Esodland/SRB2Kart-PSVita-PSTV/tree/master) |

**Only the modern build changed in v2.1.** `srb2kart-2019-vitagl.vpk` is the exact same file as in v2.0 — re-attached so this release stands on its own. Rumble was not backported to it because it has not been tested on that branch.

> ⚠️ **Install only one at a time.** Both use the same title ID (`SRB2KART0`), so installing one *replaces* the other. Your data in `ux0:data/srb2kart/` is kept either way.

## Updating from v2.0

Install the VPK over the old one with VitaShell. Your game data and settings are kept, and `rumble` defaults to `Normal` on first launch.

Full install instructions, controls and build notes: [README](https://github.com/Esodland/SRB2Kart-PSVita-PSTV/blob/vitagl-modern/README.md).

## Credits

SRB2Kart by **Kart Krew**. PS Vita/PS TV port built on the work of **Rinnegatamante** (`srb2-vita`, vitaGL) with help from **Ryo**. Ported by **Esod**.

name: vitaMania! v0.1.0a
body:
# vitaMania! v0.1.0a

A PS Vita port inspired by osu!mania. This is still very much an alpha, but the core game is playable.

## Setup

1. Install the VPK with VitaShell.
2. Put beatmaps in:

`ux0:data/vitamania/`

You can drop `.osz` files directly into that folder. On launch, VitaMania will extract them into:

`ux0:data/vitamania/Songs/`

If you added new `.osz` files, the first scan may take a little while.

## What Works

vitaMania! can load and play osu! beatmaps on device. 4K mania maps work directly, and standard osu! maps or other key counts are converted to 4K automatically.

Current features include:

- Playable 4-lane mania gameplay
- `.osz` import and auto-extraction
- Beatmap/song select menu
- Multiple difficulties grouped under one song
- MP3 and OGG audio support
- Background image support
- Score saving and high scores
- Pause menu
- Custom lane binds
- Basic osu!-style UI and gameplay skinning

Alpha build, so expect bugs and rough edges.

## Still To Come

Planned improvements include:

- Video playback for maps that include videos
- Custom theme/skin support
- Optional hit sounds
- Faster loading and scanning
- Sorting/filtering in song select
- More gameplay polish
- Better results screen
- More accurate conversion behavior for non-4K maps
- General bug fixes and performance improvements

## Notes

This is an unofficial fan project. [Beatmaps can be found here.](https://osu.ppy.sh/beatmapsets?m=3)

name: GoldenIdol-Vita-v0.8.7
body:
# The Case of the Golden Idol - PS Vita Port (v0.8.7)

Originally I just wanted to get trophies working, but I ended up sneaking in a bunch of fixes and QoL updates along the way.

**What's New in v0.8.7:**

**Controls & Input:**
- **Cancel button fix:** it was mapped to both *accept* and *cancel*, so menus closed and immediately reopened. It now only cancels. (issue #4)
- **Volume sync fix:** corrected volume synchronization in the project. (issue #3)
- **Help screen:** now lists the real PS Vita controls instead of the PC ones (I'll improve it even further in a future version).

**Zoom:**
- **Progressive zoom:** holding L/R or D-Pad Up/Down now zooms smoothly (continuous) instead of fixed steps, for both the scene camera and the Thinking Panel.
- **Thinking Panel zoom (up to 3x):** zoom the deduction board to read the text on the small screen.
- **Hint zoom:** the hint illustrations can be zoomed and panned the same way.

**Visual and UI:**
- **Brightness setting:** new Settings slider that fades the screen dark or light.
- **Scene-only transitions:** the black fade between locations now only covers the scene, keeping the toolbar visible.
- **Overhauled Credits & Discord supporters screens:** rolling credits that finish and return automatically.
- **Object-description box:** fixed the text centering inside the item description box.

**Audio and Video:**
- **Intermission videos:** re-encoded to a lighter resolution for smoother playback, with the scenario selector hidden behind the video to reduce GPU load.

**Performance:**
- **DLC crash fix:** resolved the `C2-12828-1` out-of-memory crash on the *Mystery of Monkey Paw Island* DLC scene. (issue #2)
- **Project cleanup:** unused scenes and prototype images removed from the build (smaller PCK).
- **Extended memory mode:** the VPK runs in expanded RAM mode for fewer graphical glitches and smoother gameplay.
- - _I tested a low-memory version (the one used for native games). The problem is that limiting the RAM significantly increases load times between scenes and causes a bunch of graphical bugs. I ended up scrapping the idea because the trade-off just isn't worth it. The only real benefit would be the ability to use the browser or listen to music in the background while playing._

---

**Trophies (work in progress)**
- Groundwork for trophy support: `TROPHY.TRP` generated, Steam -> Vita trophy extraction and `.TRP` build tools created, and a dedicated plugin under test. Full functionality is **not guaranteed yet** in this version.

### Instructions
Please read the **[Installation section in the README](https://github.com/WolffsRoom/GoldenIdol-PSVita#installation)** to learn how to use the patcher tool and install the game on your PS Vita.

---

> **⚠️ Note:** You MUST legally own the game on Steam to generate the Vita playable files.

name: v2.4
body:
[Oh you thought there was no more updates but guess what there's an UPDATE!](https://homestarrunner.com/sbemails/51-website)

What started as a few technical fixes spiraled into a bigger update tying up a bunch of loose ends. Check it out check it out check it out:

### Changes
- **Added new "Reburninated" logo** to instructions screen and icons (it’s about time!).
- **Added custom soundtrack support**. Simply convert your music and put the WAV/OGG output in /music/custom. See the included README for more details.
- **Added volume controls** for music, sound effects, and Strong Bad’s commentary.
- **Increased volume** of most sound effects, and slightly increased volume of most voice clips. Additionally, music can now get much louder.
- **Reorganized Options menu** (again) by splitting Cosmetic Settings into separate Audio and Video sections.
- **Reworked Options menu background** to fill full (4:3) screen, and increased its resolution on most systems.
- Other assorted polish.
- [PSP] Music now fades out at the end of a level like on other systems.

### Bug Fixes
- **Fixed movement being jittery** at high framerates.
- **Fixed music not playing** on levels 47 and 48.
- Fixed Theater and sound logic misclassifying some sound effects as music and vice-versa.
- Adjusted fire breath position by one pixel to match the Flash version more closely.
- [Android] **Fixed game running too fast** at >60 Hz refresh rates.
- [PSP] **Fixed audio popping** (finally).

### Technical Improvements
- **Overhauled audio**, removing all stuttering, reducing file size for most systems, and usually reducing initial load time (depending on system). Every system now uses high-quality OGG except:
  - [Gamecube, 3DS, FunKey] Low-quality OGG (Gamecube had to be dropped to low quality to make sure all common sounds could fit in RAM... sorry)
  - [PSP] Low-quality OGG (music) and WAV (sound effects/voices, because OGG would greatly increase initial load time)
- **Reduced audio latency**.
- Optimized text rendering.
- Optimized border rendering on some systems.
- Other assorted minor optimizations.
- Updated SDL2 libraries on most systems.
- Removed OGG_SFX compiler flag since audio loading now supports OGG and WAV simultaneously.
- [Gamecube, Wii] Upgraded to libogc2, which introduces a variety of improvements including **save/load support for FlippyDrive** (thanks @Extrems!).
- [PSP] Removed OSLibAudio dependency; audio now uses SDL_mixer like every other system.
- [PSP] **Upgraded PSPDEV**, resulting in improved performance and stability.

Enjoy!

name: Wagic the Homebrew Vita v0.1.0a
body:
# Wagic the Homebrew PS Vita Port

First public build. Native PS Vita port of Wagic. Runs at 960x544 with vitaGL and SDL2.

## What works

- Gameplay, menus, deck building, settings.
- Save and load.
- Front touch screen, analog stick, all face buttons and triggers.
- Boots and runs at default Vita clocks. No overclock.

## Install

1. CFW Vita with `libshacccg.suprx` set up (see vitaGL docs if you don't have it).
2. Copy `wagic.vpk` to your Vita over FTP or USB.
3. Open VitaShell, press Cross on the VPK to install.
4. Launch from the LiveArea.

## Card art

The release VPK has no card images. Wizards of the Coast art cannot be redistributed. To play with art, build the full VPK locally. See `BUILD_VITA.md`.

## Save data

Lives at `ux0:data/Wagic/`. Delete that folder in VitaShell to wipe progress.

name: FakeName-Changer-For-PSVita v2.1
body:
### FakeName Changer Version 2.1

**Bug fixes**
Fixed restore behavior so it no longer replaces the full app.db.
Restore now only reapplies saved bubble title changes to matching title IDs.
Fixed an issue where restoring an older backup could remove newer app entries from the database.
Fixed a startup error caused by the title backup function loading too late.
Kept the full database backup as an emergency fallback only.

**Improvements**
Safer backup and restore system.
Better handling for users who install new games after making a backup.
Manual backups now save title data separately from the full database.
Restore is now better suited for normal use after database changes or new installs.
Notes

This update addresses the concern about restoring an old modified app.db. FakeName Changer now preserves the current database and only restores the renamed title fields.

Installation

Install the updated .vpk through VitaShell like normal.

**Special thanks**

Thanks to the community for pointing out the restore risk and helping improve the app.

name: wiliwili v1.6.0
body:
💡macOS 和 Windows 分别推出了适合 老系统/老设备 的版本，对于新用户，请先运行默认版，如有问题再尝试这些专门适配版。

### 相关链接 :
来 wiki 看看 wiliwili 还能玩出什么花样来： https://github.com/xfangfang/wiliwili/wiki

SteamDeck 防锁屏插件： https://github.com/xfangfang/DeckyInhibitScreenSaver

Xbox 版暂停维护：https://github.com/xfangfang/wiliwili/issues/468#issuecomment-3817713715

### v1.6.0 更新说明 :
- 【修复】非登录用户无法获取视频链接
- 【修复】搜索页偶现报错
- 【修复】无法获取直播子分区列表
- 【修复】部分情况下无法获取到用户的登录状态，感谢 @ WsureDev
- 【修复】部分情况下 DLNA 投屏崩溃，感谢@ abfactor
- 【优化】移除不支持显示的搜索结果（如：课程）
- 【优化】播放器TV模式下进度条选中拖拽更丝滑 (播放器TV模式入口：界面设置 -> 界面风格）
- 【新增】播放器TV模式下，OSD隐藏时支持左右方向键调整进度
- 【新增】进度条拖拽时显示缩略图（PSV & PS4 暂不支持）
- 【新增】支持通过修改配置文件更换应用主题色 （见 wiki -> 自定义应用主题色）
- 【新增】播放器应用内全屏时自动窗口全屏（PC Only，入口：界面设置 -> 窗口）
- 【新增】进入播放页后播放器自动全屏（入口：播放设置 -> 其他设置）
- 【其他】更新 flatpak 的 runtime，更新 fmt 依赖库，感谢 @dragonflylee 
- 【隐藏功能】进入分P视频时，在历史进度弹出时按弹幕快捷键可以跳转进度


### Change log:
- [Fixed] non-logged-in users cannot obtain video links
- [Fixed] Occasional errors on search page
- [Fixed] Failed to fetch live streaming sub-section list
- [Fixed] User login status undetectable in some cases. Thanks to @WsureDev
- [Fixed] DLNA crashes in some cases. Thanks to @abfactor
- [Improved] Remove unsupported search results (e.g., courses)
- [Improved] Smoother progress bar dragging in player's TV mode
- [New] In player's TV mode, adjust progress with arrow keys when OSD is hidden
- [New] Show thumbnails when dragging progress bar
- [New] Change app theme color via config file (see wiki)
- [New] Auto full-screen window when player is full-screen in-app (PC only, go to Interface Settings -> Window)
- [New] Player auto full-screen upon entering playback page (go to Playback Settings -> Other Settings)
- [Others] Updated the runtime of flatpak and fmt library. Thanks to @dragonflylee


Please refer to the GitHub release page for detailed information.

The project is no longer just a proof of concept and has become something more functional, although there are still several areas that need improvement. Compared to the initial prototype, the rendering system has been migrated from `debug_screen` to **vita2d**, providing a much better foundation for the interface. It may feel a bit confusing for now, but once a fully functional interactive shell is implemented, the simple command mode will likely be removed. The interactive shell currently included still has a few bugs that I hope to fix and improve in future updates. For now, it should be considered more of an experimental extra feature. Regarding the interface, there has been a big improvement compared to the first prototype. name: v1.06
body:
- Substantially improved video playback performance by passing YUV data directly to GXM, avoiding CPU color space conversion.
- Added playstation button icons and PS Vita diagram in control settings screen. Notes:
  - This works by automatically patching the original game files when the game starts. The game creates automatic backups of files before applying patches (e.g., `config.lmp.backup`). Backups are only created once and won't be overwritten. The patching code was written with the help of AI tools.
  - This was achieved in part thanks to the cool [BGDA Explorer tool for PS2 by Bryce Barbara](https://github.com/bigianb/bgda-explorer). The tool was adapted to work with the Xbox texture format and modified to support importing new textures. I will share the modified fork of BGDA Explorer in the future.
- Eliminated periodic framerate stutter every 3-4 seconds. Moved Vorbis audio decoding to a background thread on CPU core 2. Uses a [custom fork of libvorbis](https://github.com/Nevak/vorbis-vita/tree/rulas) with a lock-free ring buffer that pre-fills decoded PCM data so `ov_read()` returns instantly via memcpy. Included as a submodule at `lib/libvorbis` and built automatically by the build script. Note: The code for this custom fork was written with the help of AI tools, by creating tests to ensure the original libvorbis and the threaded version behave exactly the same for this game's use case.

body: > [!IMPORTANT] > **This is a very WIP port, expect bugs, glitches and crashes to occur.** ## Installation > [!NOTE] > The game won't run on Vita3K. > [!IMPORTANT] > You need to have bought Party Hard from **Steam** legally! > Buy the game **[here](https://store.steampowered.com/app/356570/Party_Hard/)**. > This will only work with the latest **Party Hard STEAM version** for Windows or Linux. 1. Download ``PartyHardVita.vpk``. 2. Install the ``.vpk`` on your PSVita. ### Windows 3. Locate your Party Hard installation directory on your PC (should be in ``C:/Program Files (x86)/Steam/steamapps/common/Party Hard/``) 4. Copy ``PartyHardGame.exe`` and ``steam_api.dll`` (from the installation dir.) to ``ux0:/data/PartyHard/`` (create directories on your PSVita if needed) 5. Run game. (run at 500mHz for a smoother experience) ### Linux 3. Locate your Party Hard installation directory on your PC (mine is at ``~/.var/app/com.valvesoftware.Steam/.local/share/Steam/steamapps/common/Party Hard/``) 4. Copy ``PartyHardGame.x86`` (from the installation dir.) to ``ux0:/data/PartyHard/`` (create directories on your PSVita if needed) 5. Run game. (run at 500mHz for a smoother experience) If the game crashes on startup, you either skipped step 2 and 3 or your Party Hard copy is invalid. ## Known Issues These are already known issues with the latest version of the port. If you find a new one, create an [issue](https://github.com/danssmnt/PartyHard-PSVITA-Port/issues). - Game sometimes crashes when starting / exiting a level - Loading times are long (I/O is slower on Vita) - Game has lag spikes (especially when spawning new NPCs like cops) - Cops are slower (timestep is set to 0.03, just like the official Android port) - There are fewer NPCs for almost every level - Particles are laggier - Only latest Windows (``1.4.038.r``) and Linux (``1.4.024.r``) Steam Versions are compatible to boot game. - Versions that need compatibility: - Other Steam versions - GOG versions - PS4 versions - Switch versions - Android versions - iOS versions - Xbox One versions

name: PSVita Release 2
body:
# Changelog
* the game will now buffer saves, which makes them take a lot less time;
* you can now press R in the console to bring up the on-screen keyboard (press Select in the menu to bring up the console);
* text edit boxes in the menu will automatically bring up the keyboard;
* fixed touch not working properly in the NETRICSA screen;
* fixed mod switching (**NOTE:** mods with custom DLLs such as Seriously Warped Deathmatch will not work).

# How to play
1. Obtain a copy of Serious Sam: The First Encounter or Serious Sam: The Second Encounter and install it. Steam version (Classic, not HD) will do. Apparently the GOG version of TSE might not work (#1), not sure how to fix it yet.
2. Extract `data_tfe_v2.zip` (for The First Encounter) or `data_tse_v2.zip` (for The Second Encounter) into the root of your memory card (`ux0:/`).
3. Copy everything from the game folder **except** the `Bin` folder into `ux0:/data/ssam_tfe/` (for TFE) or `ux0:/data/ssam_tse/` (for TSE). **Do not overwrite anything if it asks.**
4. Install `ssam_tfe_v2.vpk` (for TFE) or `ssam_tse_v2.vpk` (for TSE).
5. Run the game.

# Known issues
* The game takes a long time to load, both at startup and when loading into a level.
* The performance is not very good, especially in scenes with lots of dynamic lights.
* Stock demos can desync. I'm not sure if this is because this is technically version 1.10 and those are from 1.07, or because of something I did.
* Network multiplayer doesn't seem to work. Split screen kind of works, but probably runs like ass.
* TSE *might* run out of memory in levels with lots of enemies, though I haven't witnessed it happen.

# Notes
* If the game hangs after starting a level, that means it's autosaving. Should take up to 10-15 seconds.
* If controls seem to be unbound, make sure Player 0 is selected in the Options / Players and Controls menu.
* I have enabled the "Precache shadowmaps" option by default, which results in less lag in game, but significantly increases load times. If you don't want that, you can disable it in "Advanced options" -> "Rendering options".
* You can turn dynamic lights off for a performance increase by setting `shd_iAllowDynamic` in `Scripts/PersistentSymbols.ini` to 0, but beware: dynamic lights are an integral part of some levels.
* Press R to apply settings in menus where the apply button can't be selected by scrolling down. Or just tap the screen.
* If the game crashes, take a look at the log file in the game folder (`ux0:/ssam_tfe/ssam.log` or `ux0:/ssam_tse/ssam.log`).

## What's Changed

### ✨ Major Features
- **PS Button Capture**
  - Optional PS button capture implemented — double press opens the menu, single press forwarded to Sunshine as PS/Xbox button mapping.
  - To support PS button capture we disabled `-s` (safe) flag for `vita-make-fself` and added the `SceShell` permission (0x2800000000000001) to the Vita package.

- **Touch Zones While Touch Enabled**
  - Allow using front-screen touch zones independently of the selected touch input mode. When a zone is active, touch input in that area is ignored; unused touch zones behave as normal touch areas.

### 🔧 Core Improvements
- **feat:** Implement MAC address handling for devices and remove deprecated MAC retrieval functions — host MACs are saved to `device.ini` and the legacy ARP/fetch logic is removed.
- **fix:** Update subproject commits for `enet`, `inih`, and `moonlight-common-c`.

### ⚙️ Under the Hood
- Split `vitainput_process` into multiple smaller functions for readability and maintainability.
- Refactor: input and shortcut handling cleanup, improved overlay/input state handling.

name: Reaction Station
body:
* Utilises Lua Player Plus Vita (lpp-vita). [Learn more.](https://github.com/Rinnegatamante/lpp-vita)
# Create your own or remake classics
Have you ever seen or played games such as Dragons lair, Space Ace, Cobra Command?
The gameplay fully relies on quick time responses like an interactive video..

-----

![](https://github.com/AntHJ/Reaction-Station/blob/main/Reaction%20Station%201.png)

-----

With Reaction station (and a lot of time a patience) you can create or recreate your own with this tool..

- Make a folder in ux0:video/
- add a compatible mp4
- (optional) add a cover image
- launch the app and select the video with Triangle to edit

-----

![](https://github.com/AntHJ/Reaction-Station/blob/main/Reaction%20Station%202.png)

-----
# The timeline

![](https://github.com/AntHJ/Reaction-Station/blob/main/Reaction%20Station%20timeline.png)

if your familiar with video editors then this may look kind of familiar, if not then it may look confusing..
the bar represents the timeline of your video, with various markers.

- Yellow bar is the entire video
- Orange bar is the section selected for the Attract/Intro video
- White  [1 1]    [2    2]   are Stages/Levels
- Blue is end credits
- each green line is a saved quick time event
- the white circle is your current timeline position

Yes i know its confusing, Yes i know its time consuming but for your own random creations it could also be fun..
I will say that it has take me MANY.!! hours to recreate the full Cobra Command and Mad Dog 2

name: VitaDeck + Configurator + Receiver
body:
## Turn your Playstation Vita into a software simulated stream deck with 'VitaDeck'

It maybe a little confusing at first to figure out how to setup keysets and
apply them, but this app has potential to be quite handy to some people..

-----
![](https://github.com/AntHJ/VitaDeck/blob/main/imgs/bg.png)
-----

1.	Install the VPK onto your Vita
2.	Run the Config.exe app on your PC
3.	Create your own StreamDeck layout   (or use the included sample keyset)
4.	Launch SreamDeck and Send the keyset to the Vita to update its functions
5.	Use the Receiver.exe app to link your Vita and PC using the IP address
6.	Close the Vita app and the PC app will disconnect so you can close it.

-----

![](https://github.com/AntHJ/VitaDeck/blob/main/imgs/VitaDock-01.png)
-----

name: Julius 1.8.0
body:
### General improvements

- The game now enters military mode when going to a legion with hotkey
- Water range is always shown when building a reservoir, even when it cannot be placed
- Added on-screen notice when a screenshot is saved
- Editor: allowed map editors to set player rank to "Caesar"
- Campaign: Brundisium can now be played for 2 years after winning the mission
- Added option to invert direction of right-click-to-drag-map
- Added command line options:
  - `--fullscreen` starts the game fullscreen
  - `--display ID` start the game on the specified display; ID starts counting from 0
- Android: enabled setting display scale on tablets
- Windows: improved fullscreen handling: the game no longer scrolls when the mouse moves out of the window on Alt-Tab

### Language improvements

- Added support for Czech, Greek and Japanese
- Added support for Russian editor files

### Bugfixes

- Fixed clone building hotkey not honoring disallowed buildings
- Fixed crash when Caesar 3 settings contain an invalid advisor
- Fixed sounds in videos on big endian systems
- Fixed multiple horn sounds on large invasions
- Fixed water buildings sometimes getting corrupted
- Fixed trees not forming forest on elevation
- Fixed visual inconsistencies on some building animations
- Fixed Android app not honoring rotation lock

### Technical improvements

- Upgraded SDL to 2.32.8, SDL_mixer to 2.8.1
- Android: upgraded build tools and SDK version

body:
## Changes

The highlights:

- Fix text encoding detection for ZIP archives on Android and our Homebrew platforms. (#3401)
- Improve support for LZH archives (#3394)

For everything else read the release notes. Enjoy!

## Full release notes

https://blog.easyrpg.org/2025/06/easyrpg-player-0-8-1-1-stun-patch-1/

## For Developers / Maintainers / Building

This is a minor patch release. Build against liblcf 0.8.1.

Minimum supported versions were changed from _very ancient_ to _a bit less ancient_: (#3391)

- CMake 3.18 (from 3.16)
- SDL 2.0.14 (from SDL 2.0.5)

Otherwise, there are no significant changes.

As a reminder:

- Autotools (``configure``) is still deprecated and will be removed in the next major release. Please migrate to CMake
- To opt in to SDL3 (the default is SDL2) invoke CMake with ``-DPLAYER_TARGET_PLATFORM=SDL3``

name: Vita - version1
body:
## Installation vita:
- Get data.zip and openrct2.vpk from the releases tab.
- Extract data.zip into ux0:data (so that the folder structure is like this:)
```
ux0:data/
  -- OpenRCT2/
  -- -- g2.dat
  -- -- OpenRCT2/
  -- -- -- ....
  -- -- language/
  -- -- -- ....
```
- Get RollerCoaster Tycoon 2
- Extract the files to ux0:data/RCT2 (so that the folder structure is like this:)
```
ux0:data/
  -- RCT2/
  -- -- Data/
  -- -- ObjData/
  -- -- Tracks/
  ...
```
- Install the vpk
- And launch the game (first boot could take up to 5 minutes)
- Have fun!

## Control scheme vita:
- Cross: Left click
- Square: Right click
- Circle: Hold to speedup cursor
- Triangle: Close all windows

- Left stick: Move mouse cursor
- DPAD: Move viewport around
- Left shoulder button: Rotate view clockwise
- Right shoulder button: Rotate view counter-clockwise
- Start: Chat

homebrew_long_description:
mGBA is a new generation of Game Boy Advance emulator. The project started in April 2013 with the goal of being fast enough to run on lower end hardware than other emulators support, without sacrificing accuracy or portability. Even in the initial version, games generally played without problems. mGBA has only gotten better since then, and now boasts being the most accurate GBA emulator around.

Other goals include accurate enough emulation to provide a development environment for homebrew software, a good workflow for tool-assist runners, and a modern feature set for emulators that older emulators may not support.

body:
A new massive update to the relaxing match-3 game OceanPop. Enjoy!
![screenshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sharkwouter/oceanpop/2.0/screenshot.jpg)

- Challenge mode levels are now random, making each playthrough different

- Make window resizable and scale dynamically in windowed mode
- Allow opening the menu with middle click on the mouse
- Add opening animation to levels
- Improve matching animation
- Add credits screen
- Move game modes into own screen
- Fix Playstation Portable version
- Improve performance in Playstation Portable version
- Improve text positioning on all menus
- Decrease the size of binary on all platforms
- Log exceptions thanks to @mardy
